en.title: A Name for Ourselves
story: After the flood, God had told Noah’s family to ‘fill the earth’. But generations later, people decided to do the opposite. They settled together on a plain in Shinar, in what is now Iraq, and made a plan.

‘Come, let’s make bricks and bake them thoroughly,’ they said. ‘Let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the whole earth.’
Notice how often they say ‘us’ and ‘ourselves’. The tower wasn’t about honouring God. It was about their own fame and their own security. They wanted to be great without God.

Then comes a funny detail: ‘The Lord came down to see the city and the tower.’ The people thought their tower reached the heavens, but God had to ‘come down’ even to see it! However impressive human achievements seem, they are tiny compared to Him.

God saw that their pride would lead to more and more trouble. So He confused their language, so that they could not understand one another. The building stopped, and people scattered across the earth, just as God had originally told them. The place was called Babel, which sounds like the Hebrew word for ‘confused’.
Pride says, ‘Look at me! I can do it without God.’ Humility says, ‘God, you are great, and I need you.’
Just a chapter later, God would call a man named Abram and promise, ‘I will make your name great.’ The people of Babel tried to grab a great name; God gives one as a gift to those who trust Him.

verse.text: Great is the Lord and most worthy of praise; His greatness no one can fathom.

lessons: Pride tries to be great without God; humility depends on Him.
However impressive our achievements, God is far greater.
God gives a ‘great name’ as a gift to those who trust Him.
questions: What were the people of Babel really trying to do?
Why is it funny that God had to ‘come down’ to see the tower?
Where are you tempted to ‘make a name for yourself’?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there anywhere I am trying to be great without you?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you are great and worthy of all praise.
Forgive me for trying to make a name for myself in…
Help me to find who I am in you.

mission.text: This week, give someone else the credit or praise instead of drawing attention to yourself.

en.journal: Draw two towers: one called ‘My name’ and one called ‘God’s name’. Write what each one is built from.

af.title: ’n Naam vir Onsself
story: Ná die vloed het God vir Noag se familie gesê om ‘die aarde te vul’. Maar geslagte later het mense besluit om die teenoorgestelde te doen. Hulle het saam op ’n vlakte in Sinear, in wat vandag Irak is, gaan woon en ’n plan gemaak.

‘Kom, laat ons stene maak en hulle goed bak,’ het hulle gesê. ‘Laat ons vir onsself ’n stad bou, met ’n toring wat tot in die hemel reik, sodat ons vir onsself ’n naam kan maak en nie oor die hele aarde verstrooi word nie.’
Let op hoe dikwels hulle ‘ons’ en ‘onsself’ sê. Die toring het nie gegaan oor om God te eer nie. Dit het gegaan oor hulle eie roem en hulle eie veiligheid. Hulle wou groot wees sonder God.

Dan kom ’n snaakse besonderheid: ‘Die Here het afgekom om die stad en die toring te sien.’ Die mense het gedink hulle toring reik tot in die hemel, maar God moes ‘afkom’ om dit eers te sien! Hoe indrukwekkend menslike prestasies ook al lyk, hulle is klein in vergelyking met Hom.

God het gesien hulle trots sou tot al hoe meer moeilikheid lei. Toe het Hy hulle taal deurmekaar gemaak, sodat hulle mekaar nie kon verstaan nie. Die bouwerk het gestop, en mense het oor die aarde versprei, net soos God hulle oorspronklik gesê het. Die plek is Babel genoem, wat klink soos die Hebreeuse woord vir ‘deurmekaar’.
Trots sê: ‘Kyk na my! Ek kan dit sonder God doen.’ Nederigheid sê: ‘God, U is groot, en ek het U nodig.’

Net een hoofstuk later sou God ’n man met die naam Abram roep en belowe: ‘Ek sal jou naam groot maak.’ Die mense van Babel het probeer om ’n groot naam te gryp; God gee een as ’n geskenk aan die wat Hom vertrou.

verse.text: Die Here is groot en baie lof waardig; sy grootheid is onpeilbaar.

lessons: Trots probeer groot wees sonder God; nederigheid maak op Hom staat.
Hoe indrukwekkend ons prestasies ook al is, God is baie groter.
God gee ’n ‘groot naam’ as ’n geskenk aan die wat Hom vertrou.
questions: Wat het die mense van Babel eintlik probeer doen?
Hoekom is dit snaaks dat God moes ‘afkom’ om die toring te sien?
Waar kom jy in die versoeking om ‘vir jouself ’n naam te maak’?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar iewers waar ek probeer om groot te wees sonder U?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U is groot en alle lof waardig.
Vergewe my dat ek probeer om vir myself ’n naam te maak in…
Help my om te vind wie ek in U is.

mission.text: Gee hierdie week vir iemand anders die eer of lof in plaas daarvan om aandag op jouself te vestig.

af.journal: Teken twee torings: een met die naam ‘My naam’ en een met die naam ‘God se Naam’. Skryf waarvan elkeen gebou is.

en.title: Babel and the Gift of a Name
story: Genesis 1–11 tells the story of humanity before Abraham: creation, the fall, Cain and Abel, the flood. The Tower of Babel is the last story in that section, and it shows humanity at its most united, and its most proud.

The builders’ motives are clear in verse 4: ‘Let us build ourselves a city… so that we may make a name for ourselves; otherwise we will be scattered.’ They wanted fame (‘a name’) and security (not being scattered), on their own terms. In the ancient world, towers called ziggurats were built as stairways for gods to come down to humans. Babel may have been an attempt to reach heaven by human effort, to control God rather than trust Him.

The narrator uses gentle irony. The tower is supposed to reach the heavens, yet ‘the Lord came down to see’ it. From heaven’s perspective, humanity’s greatest project is so small that God has to stoop to look at it.

God’s response, confusing their language and scattering them, is both judgement and mercy. United human pride without God leads to ever greater evil, as the flood story had shown. By limiting their power, God protected humanity from itself.

Then, in Genesis 12, the story turns. God calls Abram and says, ‘I will make you into a great nation… I will make your name great… and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.’ Babel tried to grab a great name by building upwards. God gives a great name by grace, to someone who simply trusts and obeys. And His purpose isn’t one proud nation but blessing for ‘all peoples’.

Centuries later, at Pentecost, God reversed Babel. The Holy Spirit came, and people from many nations heard the disciples ‘declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues’. At Babel, languages divided people in their pride. At Pentecost, the Spirit united people from every language in worship of Jesus.
Our culture is full of tower-building: building our image, our following and our success, trying to make a name for ourselves. God invites us instead to receive our identity from Him.

verse.text: I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing… all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.

lessons: Babel shows human pride trying to reach heaven and secure itself without God.
God gives a ‘great name’ by grace to those who trust Him, for the blessing of others.
At Pentecost, the Spirit reversed Babel, uniting every language in worship.
questions: What two things did the builders want, and why were their motives wrong?
How does Genesis 12 answer Genesis 11?
What forms of ‘tower-building’ do you see in your world, including social media?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Where am I building my own tower? What name do you want to give me instead?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, your name is above every name.
I confess I try to build my own name through…
Help me receive my identity from you, and use my life to bless others.

mission.text: This week, do something good without anyone knowing, so the credit goes only to God.

en.journal: Compare Genesis 11:1–9 with Acts 2:1–11. Write down every contrast you can find between Babel and Pentecost.

af.title: Babel en die Geskenk van ’n Naam
story: Genesis 1–11 vertel die storie van die mensdom voor Abraham: skepping, die sondeval, Kain en Abel, die vloed. Die toring van Babel is die laaste storie in daardie gedeelte, en dit wys die mensdom op sy mees verenigde, en sy mees trotse.

Die bouers se motiewe is duidelik in vers 4: ‘Laat ons vir onsself ’n stad bou… sodat ons vir onsself ’n naam kan maak; anders word ons verstrooi.’ Hulle wou roem (‘’n naam’) en veiligheid (nie verstrooi word nie), op hulle eie voorwaardes. In die antieke wêreld is torings wat ziggurats genoem is, gebou as trappe waarlangs gode na mense kon afkom. Babel was dalk ’n poging om die hemel deur menslike inspanning te bereik, om God te beheer eerder as om Hom te vertrou.

Die verteller gebruik sagte ironie. Die toring is veronderstel om tot in die hemel te reik, tog ‘het die Here afgekom om dit te sien’. Uit die hemel se oogpunt is die mensdom se grootste projek so klein dat God moet buk om daarna te kyk.

God se reaksie, om hulle taal deurmekaar te maak en hulle te verstrooi, is oordeel sowel as genade. Verenigde menslike trots sonder God lei tot al hoe groter kwaad, soos die vloedstorie gewys het. Deur hulle mag te beperk, het God die mensdom teen homself beskerm.

Dan, in Genesis 12, draai die storie. God roep Abram en sê: ‘Ek sal jou ’n groot nasie maak… Ek sal jou naam groot maak… en al die volke op aarde sal deur jou geseën word.’ Babel het probeer om ’n groot naam te gryp deur opwaarts te bou. God gee ’n groot naam uit genade, aan iemand wat eenvoudig vertrou en gehoorsaam. En sy doel is nie een trotse nasie nie, maar seën vir ‘al die volke’.

Eeue later, met Pinkster, het God Babel omgekeer. Die Heilige Gees het gekom, en mense van baie nasies het die dissipels gehoor ‘wat in ons eie tale die wonderdade van God verkondig’. By Babel het tale mense in hulle trots verdeel. Met Pinkster het die Gees mense van elke taal in aanbidding van Jesus verenig.
Ons kultuur is vol toringbouery: ons bou ons beeld, ons volgelinge en ons sukses, en probeer vir onsself ’n naam maak. God nooi ons eerder om ons identiteit van Hom te ontvang.

verse.text: Ek sal jou naam groot maak, en jy sal ’n seën wees… al die volke op aarde sal deur jou geseën word.

lessons: Babel wys menslike trots wat die hemel probeer bereik en homself sonder God probeer beveilig.
God gee ’n ‘groot naam’ uit genade aan die wat Hom vertrou, tot seën vir ander.
Met Pinkster het die Gees Babel omgekeer en elke taal in aanbidding verenig.
questions: Watter twee dinge wou die bouers hê, en hoekom was hulle motiewe verkeerd?
Hoe beantwoord Genesis 12 Genesis 11?
Watter vorme van ‘toringbouery’ sien jy in jou wêreld, ook op sosiale media?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Waar bou ek my eie toring? Watter naam wil U my eerder gee?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, u Naam is bo elke naam.
Ek bely dat ek my eie naam probeer bou deur…
Help my om my identiteit van U te ontvang, en gebruik my lewe om ander te seën.

mission.text: Doen hierdie week iets goeds sonder dat iemand dit weet, sodat die eer net na God gaan.

af.journal: Vergelyk Genesis 11:1–9 met Handelinge 2:1–11. Skryf elke teenstelling neer wat jy tussen Babel en Pinkster kan kry.

en.title: The Too-Tall Tower
story: Long ago, people said, ‘Let’s build a tower up to the sky!’
Brick on brick, higher and higher!
‘Then everyone will say we are great!’ they boasted.
But God is the greatest. He mixed up their words, and they stopped building.
God is greater than everything!

verse.text: The Lord is great and most worthy of praise.

en.action: Build a tower with blocks, then say: ‘God is greater than my tower!’
lessons: God is the greatest of all.
questions: How tall can you make your tower?
prayer: Dear God,
you are the greatest! Amen.

af.title: Die Te Hoë Toring
story: Lank gelede het mense gesê: ‘Kom ons bou ’n toring tot in die lug!’
Steen op steen, hoër en hoër!
‘Dan sal almal sê ons is groot!’ het hulle gespog.
Maar God is die grootste. Hy het hulle woorde deurmekaar gemaak, en hulle het opgehou bou.
God is groter as alles!

verse.text: Die Here is groot en baie lof waardig.

af.action: Bou ’n toring met blokke, en sê dan: ‘God is groter as my toring!’
lessons: God is die grootste van almal.
questions: Hoe hoog kan jy jou toring bou?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is die grootste! Amen.

en.title: The Tower of Babel
story: A long time after the great flood, all the people in the world spoke the same language. They found a flat place called Shinar and settled there.
Someone had an idea. ‘Let’s make bricks and bake them hard,’ they said. ‘Let’s build a city with a tower that reaches up to the sky! Then we will make a great name for ourselves.’

So they built and built. Brick on brick, the tower grew taller and taller. But their hearts were growing proud. They wanted everyone to look at them and say, ‘How great you are!’ They forgot about God, who made them.

God came down to see the city and the tower. He knew that pride would lead them into trouble. So He mixed up their language! Suddenly one person said, ‘Pass me a brick,’ and the other heard something that sounded like ‘Wobble-gobble-flip!’
They couldn’t understand each other, so they couldn’t keep building. People spread out all over the earth. The city was called Babel, because there God mixed up their words.
We don’t need to make a great name for ourselves. God’s name is the greatest. When we love Him and honour Him, we find out who we really are.

verse.text: Great is the Lord and most worthy of praise.

lessons: God’s name is greater than any name we make.
Pride makes us forget God.
I can honour God instead of showing off.
questions: Why did the people want to build a tall tower?
What is the difference between doing your best and showing off?
prayer: Dear God,
your name is the greatest of all.
Help me not to show off,
but to honour you in everything I do. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, cheer for someone else instead of talking about yourself.

af.title: Die Toring van Babel
story: Lank ná die groot vloed het al die mense in die wêreld dieselfde taal gepraat. Hulle het ’n plat plek met die naam Sinear gekry en daar gaan woon.
Iemand het ’n idee gekry. ‘Kom ons maak stene en bak hulle hard,’ het hulle gesê. ‘Kom ons bou ’n stad met ’n toring wat tot in die lug reik! Dan sal ons vir onsself ’n groot naam maak.’

Toe het hulle gebou en gebou. Steen op steen het die toring al hoër en hoër geword. Maar hulle harte het trots geword. Hulle wou hê almal moet na hulle kyk en sê: ‘Hoe groot is julle!’ Hulle het van God vergeet, wat hulle gemaak het.

God het afgekom om na die stad en die toring te kyk. Hy het geweet trots sou hulle in die moeilikheid laat beland. Toe het Hy hulle taal deurmekaar gemaak! Skielik het een persoon gesê: ‘Gee vir my ’n steen,’ en die ander een het iets gehoor wat klink soos ‘Wiebel-wabbel-flip!’
Hulle kon mekaar nie verstaan nie, so hulle kon nie verder bou nie. Mense het oor die hele aarde versprei. Die stad is Babel genoem, want daar het God hulle woorde deurmekaar gemaak.
Ons hoef nie vir onsself ’n groot naam te maak nie. God se Naam is die grootste. As ons Hom liefhet en eer, vind ons uit wie ons regtig is.

verse.text: Die Here is groot en baie lof waardig.

lessons: God se Naam is groter as enige naam wat ons maak.
Trots laat ons van God vergeet.
Ek kan God eer in plaas daarvan om te spog.
questions: Hoekom wou die mense ’n hoë toring bou?
Wat is die verskil tussen jou bes doen en spog?
prayer: Liewe God,
u Naam is die grootste van almal.
Help my om nie te spog nie,
maar om U te eer in alles wat ek doen. Amen.

mission.text: Juig môre vir iemand anders in plaas daarvan om oor jouself te praat.

trait.en: God leads me step by step
trait.af: God lei my tree vir tree

en.title: Go Without a Map
story: Abram’s family came from Ur, a wealthy city in Mesopotamia with temples, schools and markets. His father Terah had moved the family north to Haran. There, when Abram was seventy-five, God spoke to him.

‘Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you.’ Three things to leave: his country, his relatives and his father’s house. In those days, your family was your security, your protection and your identity. God was asking Abram to leave everything familiar.

And where was he going? ‘To the land I will show you.’ No address. No map. Hebrews 11:8 says, ‘By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going.’

But God didn’t just give a command; He gave seven promises: ‘I will make you into a great nation; I will bless you; I will make your name great; you will be a blessing; I will bless those who bless you; whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.’

Abram went. He took Sarai, his nephew Lot, their possessions and their servants, and set off on a journey of about 650 kilometres. When they reached Canaan, God appeared to him again: ‘To your offspring I will give this land.’ Abram built an altar and worshipped. Everywhere he went, he built altars and ‘called on the name of the Lord’.

Faith doesn’t mean having all the answers. It means trusting the One who does. God often shows us the next step rather than the whole journey. Our part is to take that step, and to keep worshipping Him along the way.

verse.text: By faith Abraham… obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going.

lessons: Faith means trusting God even when we can’t see the whole way.
God’s commands come with promises.
God blesses us so that we can be a blessing to others.
questions: What three things did God ask Abram to leave? Why was that hard?
What did Abram do everywhere he went? Why?
Where do you need to trust God with the next step?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘What is the next step you want me to take?’ Write down what you sense, even if it is small.
prayer: God, thank you that you know the whole journey.
Help me to take the next step in…
Make my life a blessing to others.

mission.text: This week, take one step of obedience you have been unsure about, and trust God with the rest.

en.journal: Make a list of God’s seven promises to Abram in Genesis 12:2–3. Circle the ones that God has also given to you through Jesus.

af.title: Gaan Sonder ’n Kaart
story: Abram se familie het van Ur gekom, ’n welvarende stad in Mesopotamië met tempels, skole en markte. Sy pa Tera het die familie noord na Haran laat trek. Daar, toe Abram vyf-en-sewentig was, het God met hom gepraat.

‘Gaan weg uit jou land, van jou mense en van jou vader se huis af na die land wat Ek jou sal wys.’ Drie dinge om agter te laat: sy land, sy familie en sy vader se huis. In daardie dae was jou familie jou sekuriteit, jou beskerming en jou identiteit. God het Abram gevra om alles wat bekend was, agter te laat.

En waarheen was hy op pad? ‘Na die land wat Ek jou sal wys.’ Geen adres nie. Geen kaart nie. Hebreërs 11:8 sê: ‘Deur geloof het Abraham gehoorsaam toe hy geroep is om te gaan na ’n plek wat hy later as erfdeel sou ontvang, en hy het gegaan sonder om te weet waarheen hy gaan.’

Maar God het nie net ’n bevel gegee nie; Hy het sewe beloftes gegee: ‘Ek sal jou ’n groot nasie maak; Ek sal jou seën; Ek sal jou naam groot maak; jy sal ’n seën wees; Ek sal seën wie jou seën; wie jou vervloek, sal Ek vervloek; en al die volke op aarde sal deur jou geseën word.’

Abram het gegaan. Hy het Sarai, sy broerskind Lot, hulle besittings en hulle diensknegte saamgeneem en vertrek op ’n reis van omtrent 650 kilometer. Toe hulle in Kanaän aankom, het God weer aan hom verskyn: ‘Aan jou nageslag sal Ek hierdie land gee.’ Abram het ’n altaar gebou en aanbid. Oral waar hy gegaan het, het hy altare gebou en ‘die Naam van die Here aangeroep’.

Geloof beteken nie om al die antwoorde te hê nie. Dit beteken om die Een te vertrou wat dit het. God wys ons dikwels die volgende tree eerder as die hele reis. Ons deel is om daardie tree te neem, en om Hom langs die pad te bly aanbid.

verse.text: Deur geloof het Abraham… gehoorsaam en gegaan, al het hy nie geweet waarheen hy gaan nie.

lessons: Geloof beteken om God te vertrou selfs as ons nie die hele pad kan sien nie.
God se bevele kom met beloftes.
God seën ons sodat ons vir ander ’n seën kan wees.
questions: Watter drie dinge het God Abram gevra om agter te laat? Hoekom was dit moeilik?
Wat het Abram oral gedoen waar hy gegaan het? Hoekom?
Waar moet jy God met die volgende tree vertrou?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Wat is die volgende tree wat U wil hê ek moet neem?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel, selfs al is dit klein.
prayer: God, dankie dat U die hele reis ken.
Help my om die volgende tree te neem in…
Maak my lewe ’n seën vir ander.

mission.text: Neem hierdie week een tree van gehoorsaamheid waaroor jy onseker was, en vertrou God met die res.

af.journal: Maak ’n lys van God se sewe beloftes aan Abram in Genesis 12:2–3. Omkring die wat God ook deur Jesus aan jou gegee het.

en.title: The Call That Changed the World
story: Genesis 12 is one of the hinges of the whole Bible. After eleven chapters of human failure (the fall, violence, the flood, Babel), God starts a rescue plan, and it begins with one man and a promise.

Abram’s background makes the call even more remarkable. Joshua 24:2 tells us that his family ‘worshipped other gods’. Abram didn’t grow up knowing the Lord. God called him out of idolatry, by grace. He wasn’t chosen because he was better than others, but because God had a purpose.

The call has a cost and a promise. The cost: leave your land, your relatives and your father’s household, the three circles of identity and security in the ancient world. The promise: land, descendants, a great name, blessing, protection, and, most importantly, ‘all peoples on earth will be blessed through you’.

That last promise is the key to the rest of the Bible. God didn’t choose Abraham’s family to keep the blessing to themselves, but to be the channel through which His blessing would reach every nation. Paul explains that this promise was ‘the gospel in advance’, and that it is fulfilled in Jesus, Abraham’s descendant: ‘Those who rely on faith are blessed along with Abraham.’ If you trust in Jesus, you are part of the fulfilment of Genesis 12:3.
Abram’s response is simple: ‘So Abram went, as the Lord had told him.’ No arguing, no recorded questions. He was seventy-five, settled and wealthy, but he went.

Notice what Abram does in the land: he builds altars and ‘calls on the name of the Lord’. He is a nomad living in tents, owning none of the promised land, yet wherever he goes, he marks it as a place of worship. Hebrews says he ‘was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God’. He lived as a pilgrim, trusting God’s promises for a future he wouldn’t see fully in his lifetime.
Faith is often like that: obeying today based on promises that will be fulfilled later. Abram walked by faith, not by sight, and through him the whole world has been blessed.

verse.text: Understand, then, that those who have faith are children of Abraham… so those who rely on faith are blessed along with Abraham.

lessons: God calls people by grace, not because they deserve it.
God blessed Abraham so that all nations would be blessed through Jesus.
Faith obeys today based on promises that God will fulfil later.
questions: Why is it significant that Abram’s family worshipped other gods?
How does Galatians 3 connect Genesis 12 to you?
What does it mean to live as a ‘pilgrim’ in the world?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What are you calling me to leave behind, and what are you calling me towards?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you for calling me by grace.
Thank you that through Jesus I share in the blessing of Abraham.
Help me to obey you, even when I can’t see where it leads, especially in…

mission.text: This week, pray for one nation or people group that hasn’t yet heard of Jesus, that they would be blessed through Abraham’s Seed.

en.journal: Write about what you might need to ‘leave behind’ to follow God more fully: a habit, an attitude or a way of thinking.

af.title: Die Roeping wat die Wêreld Verander het
story: Genesis 12 is een van die skarniere van die hele Bybel. Ná elf hoofstukke van menslike mislukking (die sondeval, geweld, die vloed, Babel) begin God ’n reddingsplan, en dit begin met een man en ’n belofte.

Abram se agtergrond maak die roeping nog meer merkwaardig. Josua 24:2 vertel ons dat sy familie ‘ander gode aanbid het’. Abram het nie grootgeword en die Here geken nie. God het hom uit afgodediens geroep, uit genade. Hy is nie gekies omdat hy beter as ander was nie, maar omdat God ’n doel gehad het.

Die roeping het ’n prys en ’n belofte. Die prys: verlaat jou land, jou familie en jou vader se huis, die drie kringe van identiteit en sekuriteit in die antieke wêreld. Die belofte: land, nakomelinge, ’n groot naam, seën, beskerming, en, die belangrikste, ‘al die volke op aarde sal deur jou geseën word’.

Daardie laaste belofte is die sleutel tot die res van die Bybel. God het nie Abraham se familie gekies om die seën vir hulleself te hou nie, maar om die kanaal te wees waardeur sy seën elke nasie sou bereik. Paulus verduidelik dat hierdie belofte ‘die evangelie vooruit’ was, en dat dit vervul is in Jesus, Abraham se nakomeling: ‘Die wat op geloof staatmaak, word saam met Abraham geseën.’ As jy Jesus vertrou, is jy deel van die vervulling van Genesis 12:3.
Abram se reaksie is eenvoudig: ‘Toe het Abram gegaan, soos die Here vir hom gesê het.’ Geen stryery nie, geen opgetekende vrae nie. Hy was vyf-en-sewentig, gevestig en ryk, maar hy het gegaan.

Let op wat Abram in die land doen: hy bou altare en ‘roep die Naam van die Here aan’. Hy is ’n nomade wat in tente woon en niks van die beloofde land besit nie, tog merk hy elke plek waar hy gaan as ’n plek van aanbidding. Hebreërs sê hy ‘het uitgesien na die stad met fondamente, waarvan God die argitek en bouer is’. Hy het as ’n pelgrim gelewe, en God se beloftes vertrou vir ’n toekoms wat hy nie in sy leeftyd ten volle sou sien nie.
Geloof is dikwels so: om vandag te gehoorsaam op grond van beloftes wat later vervul sal word. Abram het deur geloof gelewe, nie deur te sien nie, en deur hom is die hele wêreld geseën.

verse.text: Besef dan dat die wat glo, kinders van Abraham is… so word die wat op geloof staatmaak, saam met Abraham geseën.

lessons: God roep mense uit genade, nie omdat hulle dit verdien nie.
God het Abraham geseën sodat al die nasies deur Jesus geseën sou word.
Geloof gehoorsaam vandag op grond van beloftes wat God later sal vervul.
questions: Hoekom is dit betekenisvol dat Abram se familie ander gode aanbid het?
Hoe verbind Galasiërs 3 Genesis 12 met jou?
Wat beteken dit om as ’n ‘pelgrim’ in die wêreld te lewe?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Wat roep U my om agter te laat, en waarheen roep U my?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie dat U my uit genade roep.
Dankie dat ek deur Jesus deel in die seën van Abraham.
Help my om U te gehoorsaam, selfs as ek nie kan sien waarheen dit lei nie, veral in…

mission.text: Bid hierdie week vir een nasie of volksgroep wat nog nie van Jesus gehoor het nie, dat hulle deur Abraham se Nakomeling geseën sal word.

af.journal: Skryf oor wat jy dalk moet ‘agterlaat’ om God voller te volg: ’n gewoonte, ’n houding of ’n manier van dink.

en.title: Abram Follows God
story: God said to Abram, ‘Pack up and go!’
‘Where to?’ Abram wondered.
‘I will show you,’ said God.
So Abram packed his tent, his sheep and his camels, and off he went!
God leads me step by step.

verse.text: Go to the land I will show you.

en.action: March on the spot, step by step, saying: ‘I follow God!’
lessons: God leads me step by step.
questions: Can you take three big steps?
prayer: Dear God,
I will follow you. Amen.

af.title: Abram Volg God
story: God het vir Abram gesê: ‘Pak op en gaan!’
‘Waarheen?’ het Abram gewonder.
‘Ek sal jou wys,’ het God gesê.
Toe pak Abram sy tent, sy skape en sy kamele, en weg is hy!
God lei my tree vir tree.

verse.text: Gaan na die land wat Ek jou sal wys.

af.action: Marsjeer op een plek, tree vir tree, en sê: ‘Ek volg God!’
lessons: God lei my tree vir tree.
questions: Kan jy drie groot treë gee?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek sal U volg. Amen.

en.title: Pack Your Tent!
story: Abram lived in a city called Haran with his wife Sarai. He had a comfortable home, lots of family around him and many animals.
One day God spoke to him: ‘Leave your country, your people and your father’s house, and go to the land I will show you.’

Go where? God didn’t give Abram a map! He just said, ‘I will show you.’ But God also made Abram a wonderful promise: ‘I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you, and all the families on earth will be blessed through you.’

Abram had to decide: stay where it was safe and familiar, or trust God and go? Abram chose to trust God. He was seventy-five years old, but he packed up his tents, his sheep, his goats and his camels, and set off with Sarai and his nephew Lot.
They walked for many days through dusty land. When they finally reached the land of Canaan, God said, ‘This is the land I will give your family.’ Abram built an altar and thanked God.
Following God is like walking with a torch at night. You can’t see the whole path, just the next step. But God knows the way, and He walks with you.

verse.text: Go to the land I will show you. I will bless you.

lessons: God leads me step by step.
I can trust God even when I can’t see the whole way.
God blesses me so that I can be a blessing.
questions: Why was it brave of Abram to leave his home?
What is something new or a bit scary you can trust God with?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you know the way.
Help me to follow you step by step,
even when I can’t see the whole path. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you try something new, say: ‘God, lead me step by step.’

af.title: Pak Jou Tent!
story: Abram het in ’n stad met die naam Haran gewoon saam met sy vrou Sarai. Hy het ’n gemaklike huis gehad, baie familie rondom hom en baie diere.
Eendag het God met hom gepraat: ‘Gaan weg uit jou land, van jou mense en jou pa se huis af, na die land wat Ek jou sal wys.’

Gaan waarheen? God het nie vir Abram ’n kaart gegee nie! Hy het net gesê: ‘Ek sal jou wys.’ Maar God het ook vir Abram ’n wonderlike belofte gemaak: ‘Ek sal jou ’n groot nasie maak. Ek sal jou seën, en al die families op aarde sal deur jou geseën word.’

Abram moes besluit: bly waar dit veilig en bekend is, of God vertrou en gaan? Abram het gekies om God te vertrou. Hy was vyf-en-sewentig jaar oud, maar hy het sy tente, sy skape, sy bokke en sy kamele gepak en saam met Sarai en sy broerskind Lot vertrek.
Hulle het baie dae deur stowwerige land geloop. Toe hulle eindelik in die land Kanaän aankom, het God gesê: ‘Dit is die land wat Ek vir jou familie sal gee.’ Abram het ’n altaar gebou en God gedank.
Om God te volg is soos om snags met ’n flitslig te loop. Jy kan nie die hele pad sien nie, net die volgende tree. Maar God ken die pad, en Hy loop saam met jou.

verse.text: Gaan na die land wat Ek jou sal wys. Ek sal jou seën.

lessons: God lei my tree vir tree.
Ek kan God vertrou selfs as ek nie die hele pad kan sien nie.
God seën my sodat ek ’n seën kan wees.
questions: Hoekom was dit dapper van Abram om sy huis te verlaat?
Wat is iets nuuts of ’n bietjie eng waarmee jy God kan vertrou?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U die pad ken.
Help my om U tree vir tree te volg,
selfs as ek nie die hele pad kan sien nie. Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre iets nuuts probeer, sê: ‘God, lei my tree vir tree.’

en.fact: Abram later got a new name from God: Abraham, which means ‘father of many’. Today, millions of people all over the world call him ‘father Abraham’.
en.deeper: God promised that all families on earth would be blessed through Abram. How did that come true through Jesus?
en.journal: Draw a road with footprints going into the distance. On each footprint, write a way God leads you.

af.fact: Abram het later ’n nuwe naam van God gekry: Abraham, wat ‘vader van baie’ beteken. Vandag noem miljoene mense regoor die wêreld hom ‘vader Abraham’.
af.deeper: God het belowe dat al die families op aarde deur Abram geseën sou word. Hoe het dit deur Jesus waar geword?
af.journal: Teken ’n pad met voetspore wat in die verte ingaan. Skryf op elke voetspoor ’n manier waarop God jou lei.

trait.en: God provides, so I can be generous
trait.af: God voorsien, so ek kan vrygewig wees

en.title: Room for Generosity
story: After a difficult time in Egypt during a famine, Abram returned to Canaan, back to the altar he had built near Bethel, and ‘there Abram called on the name of the Lord’. God had blessed him so much that he was ‘very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold’.

His nephew Lot had become rich too, with his own flocks, herds and tents. In fact, they had so many animals that ‘the land could not support them while they stayed together’. Quarrels broke out between Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders.

Abram could have pulled rank. He was the older one, the head of the family and the one God had made promises to. Instead, he said: ‘Let’s not have any quarrelling between you and me, for we are close relatives. Is not the whole land before you? Let’s part company. If you go to the left, I’ll go to the right; if you go to the right, I’ll go to the left.’

Lot looked around and saw the plain of the Jordan, ‘well watered, like the garden of the Lord’. He chose it for himself and moved his tents near Sodom, a city whose people were ‘wicked and sinning greatly against the Lord’.

After Lot left, God spoke to Abram: ‘Look around from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west. All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever… Go, walk through the length and breadth of the land.’
Abram could afford to be generous because he trusted God’s promise. He didn’t need to grab the best. People who are anxious grab; people who trust God give.
Lot chose by what looked best. Abram chose to keep peace and trust God. Lot’s choice led him towards trouble. Abram’s generosity opened the way for God’s blessing.

verse.text: Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give… for God loves a cheerful giver.

lessons: People who trust God can afford to be generous.
Keeping peace in relationships matters more than getting the best.
Choosing only by what looks good can lead us into trouble.
questions: Why could Abram afford to let Lot choose first?
What did Lot look at when he chose? What did he miss?
Where could you choose generosity instead of grabbing the best?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Where are you inviting me to be generous this week?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you that you take care of me.
Help me to stop grabbing and start giving, especially when…
Make me a peacemaker in my family.

mission.text: This week, give away something you value, or let someone else have the best, and trust God with it.

en.journal: Write about a time you grabbed the best for yourself, and a time you were generous. How did each one feel afterwards?

af.title: Plek vir Vrygewigheid
story: Ná ’n moeilike tyd in Egipte tydens ’n hongersnood het Abram na Kanaän teruggekeer, terug na die altaar wat hy naby Bet-El gebou het, en ‘daar het Abram die Naam van die Here aangeroep’. God het hom so baie geseën dat hy ‘baie ryk was aan vee en aan silwer en goud’.

Sy broerskind Lot het ook ryk geword, met sy eie troppe, kuddes en tente. Trouens, hulle het soveel diere gehad dat ‘die land hulle nie kon onderhou terwyl hulle saam gebly het nie’. Rusies het uitgebreek tussen Abram se veewagters en Lot se veewagters.

Abram kon sy posisie gebruik het. Hy was die oudste, die hoof van die familie en die een aan wie God beloftes gemaak het. In plaas daarvan het hy gesê: ‘Laat daar nie rusie wees tussen my en jou nie, want ons is naby familie. Lê die hele land nie voor jou nie? Kom ons gaan uitmekaar. As jy links gaan, gaan ek regs; as jy regs gaan, gaan ek links.’

Lot het rondgekyk en die Jordaanvlakte gesien, ‘goed natgelei, soos die tuin van die Here’. Hy het dit vir homself gekies en sy tente naby Sodom opgeslaan, ’n stad wie se mense ‘sleg was en baie teen die Here gesondig het’.

Nadat Lot weg is, het God met Abram gepraat: ‘Kyk rond van waar jy is, noord en suid, oos en wes. Al die land wat jy sien, sal Ek vir jou en jou nageslag vir altyd gee… Gaan, loop deur die lengte en die breedte van die land.’
Abram kon bekostig om vrygewig te wees omdat hy God se belofte vertrou het. Hy hoef nie die beste te gryp nie. Mense wat angstig is, gryp; mense wat God vertrou, gee.

Lot het gekies volgens wat die beste gelyk het. Abram het gekies om vrede te bewaar en God te vertrou. Lot se keuse het hom na moeilikheid gelei. Abram se vrygewigheid het die weg vir God se seën oopgemaak.

verse.text: Elkeen moet gee soos hy in sy hart besluit het… want God het iemand lief wat met blydskap gee.

lessons: Mense wat God vertrou, kan bekostig om vrygewig te wees.
Om vrede in verhoudings te bewaar, is belangriker as om die beste te kry.
Om net te kies volgens wat goed lyk, kan ons in moeilikheid laat beland.
questions: Hoekom kon Abram bekostig om Lot eerste te laat kies?
Waarna het Lot gekyk toe hy gekies het? Wat het hy gemis?
Waar kan jy vrygewigheid kies in plaas daarvan om die beste te gryp?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Waar nooi U my om hierdie week vrygewig te wees?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie dat U vir my sorg.
Help my om op te hou gryp en te begin gee, veral wanneer…
Maak my ’n vredemaker in my familie.

mission.text: Gee hierdie week iets weg wat jy waardeer, of laat iemand anders die beste kry, en vertrou God daarmee.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy die beste vir jouself gegryp het, en ’n keer toe jy vrygewig was. Hoe het elkeen daarna gevoel?

en.title: Grabbing or Trusting?
story: Genesis 13 is a quiet chapter, but it reveals the difference between two ways of living: grabbing and trusting.

The conflict was real. Abram and Lot’s combined herds were too large for the land, especially since ‘the Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land’. Their herders were quarrelling, and family conflict in front of watching neighbours is never a good witness.

Abram had every right to choose first. He was the senior family member and the recipient of God’s promise. But he gives up his rights for the sake of peace: ‘Let’s not have any quarrelling between you and me… for we are close relatives.’ Then he offers Lot first choice.
This is what freedom looks like. Abram doesn’t need to secure his future by grabbing the best land, because his future is secured by God’s promise. Generosity flows from security in God.

Lot ‘lifted up his eyes and saw’ the well-watered plain. The Hebrew phrase echoes Eve, who ‘saw that the fruit… was pleasing to the eye’. Lot chose by sight and self-interest, and he ‘pitched his tents near Sodom’. The narrator adds an ominous note about Sodom’s wickedness. Step by step, Lot moved closer to a place that would harm his family.

Immediately after Lot leaves, God tells Abram to look in every direction: all of it is his. What Abram freely let go of, God gave back abundantly. Jesus later taught the same principle: ‘Give, and it will be given to you.’ Not as a formula for getting rich, but as a description of how God’s kingdom works.

In chapter 14, after rescuing Lot from raiders, Abram refuses to keep any of the King of Sodom’s spoils, ‘so that you will never be able to say, “I made Abram rich.”’ He wanted everyone to know his blessing came from God alone.
The question for us: do we grab, fearing that if we don’t look after ourselves, no one will? Or do we trust God enough to be generous?

verse.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over.

lessons: Generosity flows from security in God’s promises.
Choosing by sight and self-interest can lead us step by step towards harm.
God’s blessing, not our grabbing, secures our future.
questions: How does Lot’s choice echo Eve’s in the Garden?
Why did Abram refuse the King of Sodom’s reward?
In what areas of life are you tempted to grab rather than trust?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What am I holding on to tightly because I don’t fully trust you?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you are my security and my provider.
I confess I am grabbing at…
Teach me to trust you enough to be generous, and to keep peace in my relationships.

mission.text: This week, resolve a disagreement by giving up your ‘rights’ for the sake of peace, as Abram did.

en.journal: Write about the difference between ambition that grabs and ambition that trusts God. How can you work hard without grabbing?

af.title: Gryp of Vertrou?
story: Genesis 13 is ’n stil hoofstuk, maar dit wys die verskil tussen twee maniere van lewe: gryp en vertrou.

Die konflik was werklik. Abram en Lot se gesamentlike kuddes was te groot vir die land, veral omdat ‘die Kanaäniete en Feresiete ook in die land gewoon het’. Hulle veewagters het gestry, en familiekonflik voor bure wat kyk, is nooit ’n goeie getuienis nie.

Abram het elke reg gehad om eerste te kies. Hy was die senior familielid en die ontvanger van God se belofte. Maar hy gee sy regte prys ter wille van vrede: ‘Laat daar nie rusie wees tussen my en jou nie… want ons is naby familie.’ Dan bied hy Lot die eerste keuse aan.
Dit is hoe vryheid lyk. Abram hoef nie sy toekoms te verseker deur die beste land te gryp nie, want sy toekoms is deur God se belofte verseker. Vrygewigheid vloei uit sekuriteit in God.

Lot ‘het sy oë opgeslaan en gesien’ die goed natgeleide vlakte. Die Hebreeuse uitdrukking eggo Eva, wat ‘gesien het dat die vrug… mooi was om na te kyk’. Lot het gekies volgens wat hy gesien het en eiebelang, en hy ‘het sy tente tot by Sodom opgeslaan’. Die verteller voeg ’n onheilspellende opmerking oor Sodom se goddeloosheid by. Tree vir tree het Lot nader beweeg aan ’n plek wat sy familie skade sou aandoen.

Onmiddellik nadat Lot weg is, sê God vir Abram om in elke rigting te kyk: alles is syne. Wat Abram vrywillig laat gaan het, het God oorvloedig teruggegee. Jesus het later dieselfde beginsel geleer: ‘Gee, en vir julle sal gegee word.’ Nie as ’n formule om ryk te word nie, maar as ’n beskrywing van hoe God se koninkryk werk.

In hoofstuk 14, nadat hy Lot van rowers gered het, weier Abram om enigiets van die koning van Sodom se buit te hou, ‘sodat jy nooit kan sê: “Ek het Abram ryk gemaak” nie’. Hy wou hê almal moet weet sy seën kom net van God.
Die vraag vir ons: gryp ons, uit vrees dat niemand anders vir ons sal sorg as ons nie self doen nie? Of vertrou ons God genoeg om vrygewig te wees?

verse.text: Gee, en vir julle sal gegee word. ’n Goeie maat, ingedruk, geskud en oorlopend.

lessons: Vrygewigheid vloei uit sekuriteit in God se beloftes.
Om volgens sig en eiebelang te kies, kan ons tree vir tree na skade lei.
God se seën, nie ons gryp nie, verseker ons toekoms.
questions: Hoe eggo Lot se keuse Eva s’n in die tuin?
Hoekom het Abram die koning van Sodom se beloning geweier?
In watter areas van die lewe kom jy in die versoeking om te gryp eerder as om te vertrou?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Waaraan hou ek styf vas omdat ek U nie ten volle vertrou nie?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U is my sekuriteit en my voorsiener.
Ek bely dat ek gryp na…
Leer my om U genoeg te vertrou om vrygewig te wees, en om vrede in my verhoudings te bewaar.

mission.text: Los hierdie week ’n meningsverskil op deur jou ‘regte’ prys te gee ter wille van vrede, soos Abram gedoen het.

af.journal: Skryf oor die verskil tussen ambisie wat gryp en ambisie wat God vertrou. Hoe kan jy hard werk sonder om te gryp?

en.title: You Choose First
story: Abram and Lot had lots and lots of sheep.
There wasn’t enough grass for everyone. Their helpers started to argue!
Abram said, ‘Let’s not fight. Lot, you choose first!’
Lot chose the green land. Abram took what was left.
God took care of Abram. I can share too!

verse.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

en.action: Share a toy or a snack with someone and say: ‘You choose first!’
lessons: I can share, because God takes care of me.
questions: What can you share tomorrow?
prayer: Dear God,
help me to share happily. Amen.

af.title: Jy Kies Eerste
story: Abram en Lot het baie, baie skape gehad.
Daar was nie genoeg gras vir almal nie. Hulle helpers het begin stry!
Abram het gesê: ‘Kom ons baklei nie. Lot, jy kies eerste!’
Lot het die groen land gekies. Abram het gevat wat oorgebly het.
God het vir Abram gesorg. Ek kan ook deel!

verse.text: God het iemand lief wat met blydskap gee.

af.action: Deel ’n speelding of ’n peuselhappie met iemand en sê: ‘Jy kies eerste!’
lessons: Ek kan deel, want God sorg vir my.
questions: Wat kan jy môre deel?
prayer: Liewe God,
help my om bly te deel. Amen.

en.title: Abram Lets Lot Choose
story: God blessed Abram and his nephew Lot. They both had so many sheep, goats and cows that the land couldn’t feed them all. Soon their herdsmen started quarrelling: ‘That’s our grass!’ ‘No, it’s ours!’

Abram didn’t want his family to fight. He took Lot up a hill where they could see the whole land. ‘Let’s not quarrel,’ Abram said. ‘We are family. Let’s split up. You choose first. If you go left, I’ll go right. If you go right, I’ll go left.’
Abram was the older one. He could have chosen first. But he was generous, because he trusted God to take care of him.
Lot looked around. Down below was the Jordan valley, green and full of water, like a garden. ‘I’ll take that!’ Lot said. So he took the best land and moved away. Abram stayed in the hills.
Then God spoke to Abram: ‘Look all around you, north, south, east and west. All the land you see, I will give to you and your children forever. Your family will be as many as the dust of the earth!’
Abram didn’t need to grab the best for himself. God had something even better for him. When we trust God, we can be generous and kind, because God takes care of us.

verse.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

lessons: God provides, so I can be generous.
Being kind is more important than winning.
God sees when I let others go first.
questions: Why was it generous of Abram to let Lot choose first?
When could you let someone else go first?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you take care of me.
Help me to be generous like Abram,
and to let others go first. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, let someone else choose first: a game, a seat or a snack.

af.title: Abram Laat Lot Kies
story: God het Abram en sy broerskind Lot geseën. Hulle het albei soveel skape, bokke en beeste gehad dat die land hulle nie almal kon kos gee nie. Gou het hulle veewagters begin stry: ‘Dis ons gras!’ ‘Nee, dis ons s’n!’

Abram wou nie hê sy familie moet baklei nie. Hy het Lot teen ’n heuwel op geneem waar hulle die hele land kon sien. ‘Kom ons stry nie,’ het Abram gesê. ‘Ons is familie. Kom ons gaan uitmekaar. Jy kies eerste. As jy links gaan, gaan ek regs. As jy regs gaan, gaan ek links.’
Abram was die oudste. Hy kon eerste gekies het. Maar hy was vrygewig, want hy het God vertrou om vir hom te sorg.
Lot het rondgekyk. Daar onder was die Jordaanvallei, groen en vol water, soos ’n tuin. ‘Ek vat daardie!’ het Lot gesê. Toe vat hy die beste land en trek weg. Abram het in die heuwels gebly.

Toe het God met Abram gepraat: ‘Kyk rondom jou, noord, suid, oos en wes. Al die land wat jy sien, sal Ek vir jou en jou kinders vir altyd gee. Jou familie sal soveel wees soos die stof van die aarde!’
Abram hoef nie die beste vir homself te gryp nie. God het iets nog beters vir hom gehad. As ons God vertrou, kan ons vrygewig en gaaf wees, want God sorg vir ons.

verse.text: God het iemand lief wat met blydskap gee.

lessons: God voorsien, so ek kan vrygewig wees.
Om gaaf te wees, is belangriker as om te wen.
God sien raak as ek ander eerste laat gaan.
questions: Hoekom was dit vrygewig van Abram om Lot eerste te laat kies?
Wanneer kan jy iemand anders eerste laat gaan?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U vir my sorg.
Help my om vrygewig te wees soos Abram,
en ander eerste te laat gaan. Amen.

mission.text: Laat môre iemand anders eerste kies: ’n speletjie, ’n sitplek of ’n peuselhappie.

trait.en: Nothing is too hard for God
trait.af: Niks is vir God te moeilik nie

en.title: Is Anything Too Hard for the Lord?
story: Twenty-four years had passed since God first promised Abram a family. God had changed his name to Abraham, ‘father of many’, and Sarai’s to Sarah, ‘princess’. But they still had no child together, and Abraham was now ninety-nine and Sarah eighty-nine.

One hot afternoon, Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent near the great trees of Mamre when he looked up and saw three men. He ran to greet them and bowed low. ‘Let a little water be brought, and then you may all wash your feet and rest under this tree. Let me get you something to eat.’

Abraham’s ‘little something’ turned into a feast. He hurried to Sarah: ‘Quick, bake some bread!’ He ran to choose a tender calf and had it prepared, then served it with curds and milk. Generous hospitality was a mark of honour, and Abraham gave his best.

As they ate, one of the visitors (the Lord Himself, as the story reveals) asked, ‘Where is your wife Sarah?’ Then He promised, ‘I will surely return about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son.’

Sarah, listening at the tent entrance, laughed to herself. ‘After I am worn out and my lord is old, will I now have this pleasure?’ The Lord asked Abraham, ‘Why did Sarah laugh?… Is anything too hard for the Lord?’ Sarah, afraid, denied it: ‘I did not laugh.’ But He said, ‘Yes, you did laugh.’ He wasn’t angry; He just wanted her to face the truth and trust Him.

A year later, Isaac was born. His name means ‘he laughs’. Sarah said, ‘God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.’ Her laugh of disbelief had become a laugh of joy.
God’s timing can feel slow, but His promises never fail. And the question He asked Sarah, He asks you too: ‘Is anything too hard for the Lord?’

verse.text: Is anything too hard for the Lord?

lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
God’s timing can feel slow, but His promises never fail.
God can turn our laughter of doubt into laughter of joy.
questions: How long did Abraham and Sarah wait for God’s promise?
Why do you think Sarah laughed the first time?
What feels ‘too hard’ in your life right now?
en.listen: Be still and bring God something that feels impossible. Ask: ‘Is this too hard for you?’ Listen, and write down what you sense.
prayer: God, nothing is too hard for you.
I confess I find it hard to believe you for…
Help me to trust your promises and your timing.

mission.text: This week, write Genesis 18:14 on a card and put it somewhere you’ll see it whenever you feel worried.

en.journal: Write about something you are waiting for. Then write a prayer that trusts God’s timing.

af.title: Is Daar Iets wat vir die Here te Moeilik Is?
story: Vier-en-twintig jaar het verbygegaan sedert God die eerste keer vir Abram ’n familie belowe het. God het sy naam verander na Abraham, ‘vader van baie’, en Sarai s’n na Sara, ‘prinses’. Maar hulle het nog steeds nie saam ’n kind gehad nie, en Abraham was nou nege-en-negentig en Sara nege-en-tagtig.

Een warm middag het Abraham by die ingang van sy tent naby die groot bome van Mamre gesit toe hy opkyk en drie mans sien. Hy het gehardloop om hulle te groet en laag gebuig. ‘Laat ’n bietjie water gebring word, dan kan julle almal julle voete was en onder hierdie boom rus. Laat ek vir julle iets kry om te eet.’

Abraham se ‘bietjie iets’ het ’n fees geword. Hy het na Sara gegaan: ‘Gou, bak brood!’ Hy het gehardloop om ’n sagte kalf uit te soek en dit laat voorberei, en dit toe met dikmelk en melk bedien. Vrygewige gasvryheid was ’n teken van eer, en Abraham het sy beste gegee.

Terwyl hulle eet, het een van die besoekers (die Here self, soos die storie wys) gevra: ‘Waar is jou vrou Sara?’ Toe het Hy belowe: ‘Ek sal beslis omtrent hierdie tyd volgende jaar terugkom, en Sara, jou vrou, sal ’n seun hê.’

Sara, wat by die tentingang geluister het, het vir haarself gelag. ‘Nadat ek uitgeput is en my man oud is, sal ek nou hierdie plesier hê?’ Die Here het vir Abraham gevra: ‘Hoekom het Sara gelag?… Is daar iets wat vir die Here te moeilik is?’ Sara, bang, het dit ontken: ‘Ek het nie gelag nie.’ Maar Hy het gesê: ‘Ja, jy het gelag.’ Hy was nie kwaad nie; Hy wou net hê sy moet die waarheid in die oë kyk en Hom vertrou.

’n Jaar later is Isak gebore. Sy naam beteken ‘hy lag’. Sara het gesê: ‘God het vir my laggery gebring, en almal wat hiervan hoor, sal saam met my lag.’ Haar lag van ongeloof het ’n lag van vreugde geword.
God se tydsberekening kan stadig voel, maar sy beloftes faal nooit. En die vraag wat Hy vir Sara gevra het, vra Hy ook vir jou: ‘Is daar iets wat vir die Here te moeilik is?’

verse.text: Is daar iets wat vir die Here te moeilik is?

lessons: Niks is vir God te moeilik nie.
God se tydsberekening kan stadig voel, maar sy beloftes faal nooit.
God kan ons lag van twyfel in ’n lag van vreugde verander.
questions: Hoe lank het Abraham en Sara vir God se belofte gewag?
Hoekom dink jy het Sara die eerste keer gelag?
Wat voel nou ‘te moeilik’ in jou lewe?
af.listen: Wees stil en bring vir God iets wat onmoontlik voel. Vra: ‘Is dit vir U te moeilik?’ Luister, en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, niks is vir U te moeilik nie.
Ek bely dat ek dit moeilik vind om U te glo vir…
Help my om u beloftes en u tydsberekening te vertrou.

mission.text: Skryf hierdie week Genesis 18:14 op ’n kaartjie en sit dit iewers waar jy dit sal sien elke keer as jy bekommerd voel.

af.journal: Skryf oor iets waarvoor jy wag. Skryf dan ’n gebed wat God se tydsberekening vertrou.

en.title: Laughter, Doubt and God’s Timing
story: By Genesis 18, Abraham and Sarah had been waiting for God’s promise for nearly twenty-five years. They had tried to ‘help’ God along: Sarah gave Abraham her servant Hagar to have a child through her, which caused years of family pain. God had confirmed again, in chapter 17, that the promised son would come through Sarah. Abraham’s reaction then? He ‘fell face down; he laughed’.

So when the Lord visits in person, shares a meal and repeats the promise with a specific timeframe, ‘about this time next year’, Sarah laughs too. Her laugh is understandable. She was well past childbearing age. Humanly speaking, it was impossible.

But listen to God’s response: ‘Is anything too hard for the Lord?’ The Hebrew word for ‘hard’ is the same word often translated ‘wonderful’ or ‘marvellous’. In effect, God asks, ‘Is anything too wonderful for me?’ The question isn’t a rebuke. It is an invitation to see God as He really is.

Notice how gently God handles Sarah. When she denies laughing out of fear, He simply says, ‘Yes, you did laugh.’ He doesn’t punish her. He lets her know He sees her heart, including her doubt, and He keeps His promise anyway. God’s faithfulness doesn’t depend on our faith being perfect.

Paul later reflects on this story: Abraham ‘faced the fact that his body was as good as dead… and that Sarah’s womb was also dead. Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith… being fully persuaded that God had power to do what He had promised.’ Faith doesn’t ignore reality. It looks reality in the face and trusts that God is bigger.
And then the promise is kept. Isaac, ‘he laughs’, is born ‘at the very time God had promised’. Sarah’s doubting laugh becomes a joyful laugh shared with everyone who hears.
Waiting is one of the hardest parts of faith. But God’s delays are not denials. He is never late, and His timing is part of His wisdom.

verse.text: He did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith… being fully persuaded that God had power to do what He had promised.

lessons: Nothing is too ‘wonderful’ for God.
God’s faithfulness doesn’t depend on our faith being perfect.
Faith faces reality honestly and trusts that God is bigger.
questions: What had Abraham and Sarah done earlier to try to ‘help’ God? What happened?
How does God respond to Sarah’s doubt?
What does Romans 4 teach about how faith deals with impossible situations?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Bring God a promise or a hope that feels delayed. Ask: ‘What do you want me to know about your timing?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, nothing is too wonderful for you.
I admit I have doubted you about…
Strengthen my faith, and help me wait for your timing without trying to force things my way.

mission.text: This week, notice when you are tempted to ‘help God along’ by forcing a situation, and instead pray and wait.

en.journal: Write about the difference between waiting passively and waiting in faith. What does active, faithful waiting look like?

af.title: Laggery, Twyfel en God se Tydsberekening
story: Teen Genesis 18 het Abraham en Sara al byna vyf-en-twintig jaar lank vir God se belofte gewag. Hulle het probeer om God te ‘help’: Sara het vir Abraham haar diensmeisie Hagar gegee om deur haar ’n kind te kry, wat jare van familiepyn veroorsaak het. God het in hoofstuk 17 weer bevestig dat die beloofde seun deur Sara sou kom. Abraham se reaksie toe? Hy ‘het op sy gesig neergeval; hy het gelag’.

So wanneer die Here persoonlik kom kuier, ’n ete deel en die belofte met ’n spesifieke tydraamwerk herhaal, ‘omtrent hierdie tyd volgende jaar’, lag Sara ook. Haar lag is verstaanbaar. Sy was ver verby die ouderdom om kinders te kry. Menslik gesproke was dit onmoontlik.

Maar luister na God se antwoord: ‘Is daar iets wat vir die Here te moeilik is?’ Die Hebreeuse woord vir ‘moeilik’ is dieselfde woord wat dikwels as ‘wonderlik’ of ‘wonderbaar’ vertaal word. Eintlik vra God: ‘Is daar iets wat vir My te wonderlik is?’ Die vraag is nie ’n teregwysing nie. Dit is ’n uitnodiging om God te sien soos Hy regtig is.

Let op hoe sag God met Sara werk. Wanneer sy uit vrees ontken dat sy gelag het, sê Hy eenvoudig: ‘Ja, jy het gelag.’ Hy straf haar nie. Hy laat haar weet dat Hy haar hart sien, ook haar twyfel, en Hy hou tog sy belofte. God se trou hang nie daarvan af dat ons geloof volmaak is nie.

Paulus dink later na oor hierdie storie: Abraham ‘het die feit in die oë gekyk dat sy liggaam so goed as dood was… en dat Sara se moederskoot ook dood was. Tog het hy nie deur ongeloof aan die belofte van God getwyfel nie, maar is hy in sy geloof versterk… ten volle oortuig dat God die mag het om te doen wat Hy belowe het.’ Geloof ignoreer nie die werklikheid nie. Dit kyk die werklikheid in die oë en vertrou dat God groter is.
En dan word die belofte gehou. Isak, ‘hy lag’, word gebore ‘presies op die tyd wat God belowe het’. Sara se twyfelende lag word ’n blye lag wat gedeel word met almal wat dit hoor.
Wag is een van die moeilikste dele van geloof. Maar God se vertragings is nie weierings nie. Hy is nooit laat nie, en sy tydsberekening is deel van sy wysheid.

verse.text: Hy het nie deur ongeloof aan die belofte van God getwyfel nie, maar is in sy geloof versterk… ten volle oortuig dat God die mag het om te doen wat Hy belowe het.

lessons: Niks is vir God te ‘wonderlik’ nie.
God se trou hang nie daarvan af dat ons geloof volmaak is nie.
Geloof kyk die werklikheid eerlik in die oë en vertrou dat God groter is.
questions: Wat het Abraham en Sara vroeër gedoen om God te probeer ‘help’? Wat het gebeur?
Hoe reageer God op Sara se twyfel?
Wat leer Romeine 4 oor hoe geloof met onmoontlike situasies omgaan?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Bring vir God ’n belofte of ’n hoop wat vertraag voel. Vra: ‘Wat wil U hê moet ek oor u tydsberekening weet?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, niks is vir U te wonderlik nie.
Ek erken ek het aan U getwyfel oor…
Versterk my geloof, en help my om vir u tydsberekening te wag sonder om dinge op my manier te probeer forseer.

mission.text: Let hierdie week op wanneer jy in die versoeking kom om ‘God te help’ deur ’n situasie te forseer, en bid en wag eerder.

af.journal: Skryf oor die verskil tussen passief wag en in geloof wag. Hoe lyk aktiewe, getroue wag?

en.title: Sarah Laughs
story: Three visitors came to Abraham’s tent.
Abraham and Sarah made them a yummy meal.
One visitor said, ‘Next year, Sarah will have a baby!’
Sarah was very old. She laughed, ‘Ha ha! Me?’
But God did it! Nothing is too hard for God!

verse.text: Is anything too hard for the Lord?

en.action: Pretend to be very old and slow, then jump up and say: ‘Nothing is too hard for God!’
lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
questions: Can you do a big happy laugh?
prayer: Dear God,
nothing is too hard for you! Amen.

af.title: Sara Lag
story: Drie besoekers het na Abraham se tent gekom.
Abraham en Sara het vir hulle ’n lekker ete gemaak.
Een besoeker het gesê: ‘Volgende jaar sal Sara ’n baba kry!’
Sara was baie oud. Sy het gelag: ‘Ha ha! Ek?’
Maar God het dit gedoen! Niks is vir God te moeilik nie!

verse.text: Is daar iets wat vir die Here te moeilik is?

af.action: Maak of jy baie oud en stadig is, spring dan op en sê: ‘Niks is vir God te moeilik nie!’
lessons: Niks is vir God te moeilik nie.
questions: Kan jy ’n groot blye lag lag?
prayer: Liewe God,
niks is vir U te moeilik nie! Amen.

en.title: Visitors at the Tent
story: God had changed Abram’s name to Abraham, and Sarai’s to Sarah. God had promised them a son. But they were very, very old now. Abraham was ninety-nine! And still no baby.

One hot afternoon, Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent when he saw three men standing nearby. He jumped up and ran to meet them. ‘Please stay and rest,’ he said. ‘Let me bring you water to wash your feet, and something to eat!’
Abraham hurried. Sarah baked fresh bread. A servant cooked a tender calf. Abraham served them under a big tree. This was the Lord Himself visiting with two angels!
‘Where is your wife Sarah?’ the visitor asked. ‘In the tent,’ said Abraham. Then the Lord said, ‘About this time next year, Sarah will have a son.’
Sarah was listening behind the tent door. She laughed to herself. ‘Me? Have a baby? I’m far too old!’ But the Lord heard. ‘Why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too hard for the Lord?’

A year later, just as God promised, Sarah had a baby boy! They named him Isaac, which means ‘he laughs’. Sarah said, ‘God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears will laugh with me!’ This time it was a happy laugh.
God always keeps His promises. Nothing is too hard for Him.

verse.text: Is anything too hard for the Lord?

lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
God always keeps His promises.
God loves it when we are kind to visitors.
questions: Why did Sarah laugh the first time? Why did she laugh the second time?
What seems too hard to you that you can trust God with?
prayer: Dear God,
nothing is too hard for you.
Thank you that you always keep your promises.

af.title: Besoekers by die Tent

God hou altyd sy beloftes. Niks is vir Hom te moeilik nie.

en.title: Visitors at the Tent
story: God had changed Abram’s name to Abraham, and Sarai’s to Sarah. God had promised them a son. But they were very, very old now. Abraham was ninety-nine! And still no baby.

One hot afternoon, Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent when he saw three men standing nearby. He jumped up and ran to meet them. ‘Please stay and rest,’ he said. ‘Let me bring you water to wash your feet, and something to eat!’
Abraham hurried. Sarah baked fresh bread. A servant cooked a tender calf. Abraham served them under a big tree. This was the Lord Himself visiting with two angels!
‘Where is your wife Sarah?’ the visitor asked. ‘In the tent,’ said Abraham. Then the Lord said, ‘About this time next year, Sarah will have a son.’
Sarah was listening behind the tent door. She laughed to herself. ‘Me? Have a baby? I’m far too old!’ But the Lord heard. ‘Why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too hard for the Lord?’

A year later, just as God promised, Sarah had a baby boy! They named him Isaac, which means ‘he laughs’. Sarah said, ‘God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears will laugh with me!’ This time it was a happy laugh.
God always keeps His promises. Nothing is too hard for Him.

verse.text: Is anything too hard for the Lord?

lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
God always keeps His promises.
God loves it when we are kind to visitors.
questions: Why did Sarah laugh the first time? Why did she laugh the second time?
What seems too hard to you that you can trust God with?
prayer: Dear God,
nothing is too hard for you.
Thank you that you always keep your promises.
I trust you with… Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when something feels too hard, remember: ‘Nothing is too hard for God!’

en.fact: Abraham was 100 years old and Sarah was 90 when Isaac was born. Imagine having a baby when you are as old as a great-great-grandparent!
en.deeper: Abraham welcomed strangers kindly, not knowing who they were. Why is it good to be kind to visitors?
en.journal: Draw Abraham’s tent under a big tree with three visitors. Write: ‘Is anything too hard for the Lord?’

en.title: The Friend Who Prayed
story: After the meal, the three visitors set out towards Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to see them on their way. Then the Lord said something remarkable: ‘Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?’ God chose to share His plans with Abraham, as a friend does.

‘The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is so great and their sin so grievous that I will go down and see.’ The people of those cities were known for cruelty, violence and refusing to care for the poor and needy.

The two angels went on towards Sodom, ‘but Abraham remained standing before the Lord’. Then Abraham ‘approached’ God, and began one of the boldest prayers in the Bible. ‘Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked? What if there are fifty righteous people in the city?… Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?’
The Lord answered, ‘If I find fifty righteous people in the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.’

Abraham kept going, humbly but persistently: ‘Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, though I am nothing but dust and ashes… what if there are forty-five?’ Then forty, thirty, twenty, ten. Each time God agreed. God wasn’t annoyed. He welcomed Abraham’s prayer for mercy.

Sadly, not even ten righteous people were found. But Genesis 19:29 says, ‘God remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe.’ Abraham’s prayer made a difference for his nephew’s family.
This is called intercession: standing before God on behalf of others. God invites His friends to pray boldly for people, cities and nations. Your prayers for others matter to Him.

verse.text: The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

lessons: God shares His heart with His friends.
God invites us to pray boldly for mercy for others.
Our prayers for others make a real difference.
questions: Why do you think God chose to tell Abraham His plans?
How did Abraham balance boldness and humility in his prayer?
Who could you ‘stand before God’ for this week?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Who do you want me to pray for?’ Write down the names that come, and pray for each one.
prayer: God, thank you that you call me your friend.
I stand before you for…
Please show them your mercy and your love.

mission.text: This week, choose a person, a school or a town to pray for every day, like Abraham prayed for Sodom.

en.journal: Start a prayer journal page called ‘Standing before God for others’. Write names and requests, and leave space to record answers.

af.title: Die Vriend wat Gebid het
story: Ná die ete het die drie besoekers na Sodom vertrek, en Abraham het saam met hulle geloop om hulle weg te sien. Toe het die Here iets merkwaardigs gesê: ‘Moet Ek vir Abraham wegsteek wat Ek gaan doen?’ God het gekies om sy planne met Abraham te deel, soos ’n vriend doen.

‘Die geroep teen Sodom en Gomorra is so groot en hulle sonde so ernstig dat Ek sal afgaan en kyk.’ Die mense van daardie stede was bekend vir wreedheid, geweld en dat hulle geweier het om vir die armes en behoeftiges te sorg.

Die twee engele het verder na Sodom gegaan, ‘maar Abraham het nog voor die Here bly staan’. Toe het Abraham nader aan God gekom en een van die dapperste gebede in die Bybel begin. ‘Sal U die regverdiges saam met die goddeloses wegvee? Wat as daar vyftig regverdiges in die stad is?… Sal die Regter van die hele aarde nie reg doen nie?’
Die Here het geantwoord: ‘As Ek vyftig regverdiges in die stad kry, sal Ek die hele plek ter wille van hulle spaar.’

Abraham het aangehou, nederig maar volhardend: ‘Noudat ek so vrypostig was om met die Here te praat, al is ek net stof en as… wat as daar vyf-en-veertig is?’ Toe veertig, dertig, twintig, tien. Elke keer het God ingestem. God was nie geïrriteerd nie. Hy het Abraham se gebed om genade verwelkom.

Ongelukkig is nie eers tien regverdiges gekry nie. Maar Genesis 19:29 sê: ‘God het aan Abraham gedink, en Hy het Lot uit die ramp gered.’ Abraham se gebed het ’n verskil gemaak vir sy broerskind se familie.
Dit word voorbidding genoem: om namens ander voor God te staan. God nooi sy vriende om vrymoedig vir mense, stede en nasies te bid. Jou gebede vir ander maak vir Hom saak.

verse.text: Die gebed van ’n regverdige het groot krag.

lessons: God deel sy hart met sy vriende.
God nooi ons om vrymoedig vir genade vir ander te bid.
Ons gebede vir ander maak ’n werklike verskil.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het God gekies om Abraham sy planne te vertel?
Hoe het Abraham vrymoedigheid en nederigheid in sy gebed gebalanseer?
Vir wie kan jy hierdie week ‘voor God staan’?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Vir wie wil U hê moet ek bid?’ Skryf die name neer wat kom, en bid vir elkeen.
prayer: God, dankie dat U my u vriend noem.
Ek staan voor U vir…
Bewys asseblief aan hulle u genade en u liefde.

mission.text: Kies hierdie week ’n persoon, ’n skool of ’n dorp om elke dag voor te bid, soos Abraham vir Sodom gebid het.

af.journal: Begin ’n gebedsjoernaalbladsy met die naam ‘Om vir ander voor God te staan’. Skryf name en versoeke neer, en laat plek om antwoorde op te teken.

en.title: Will Not the Judge of All the Earth Do Right?
story: Genesis 18 gives us an extraordinary window into how God relates to His friends. The Lord deliberately chooses to reveal His plans to Abraham: ‘For I have chosen him, so that he will direct his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing what is right and just.’ God shares His heart with Abraham partly so that Abraham will learn justice and mercy, and pass them on.

What was Sodom’s sin? Genesis 19 describes violent, abusive behaviour. Ezekiel 16:49 adds another dimension: ‘She and her daughters were arrogant, overfed and unconcerned; they did not help the poor and needy.’ Sodom was a city of pride, cruelty and indifference to suffering. The ‘outcry’ God heard was the cry of its victims.

Abraham’s prayer is a model of intercession. He appeals to God’s character: ‘Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?’ He doesn’t argue that God is wrong to judge; he appeals to God’s own justice and mercy. He is bold, coming back again and again. Yet he is humble: ‘I am nothing but dust and ashes.’ Boldness and humility aren’t opposites in prayer; they belong together.

Notice that God never says no. Each time Abraham asks, God agrees. Abraham stops at ten, not God. This reveals something about God’s heart. He is ‘slow to anger and abounding in love’, and He is looking for reasons to show mercy. Later, God says through Ezekiel, ‘I looked for someone… who would stand before me in the gap on behalf of the land.’ God is looking for intercessors.
Even though Sodom was destroyed, God ‘remembered Abraham’ and rescued Lot. Abraham’s prayer was not wasted.
The Bible calls Abraham ‘God’s friend’ three times. Friendship with God isn’t only about receiving blessing; it involves sharing God’s concerns for the world and praying for others.

Jesus is the ultimate intercessor. He stood in the gap not just with words but with His life, and He ‘always lives to intercede’ for us. As His friends, we are invited to join Him in praying for a broken world.

verse.text: Abraham believed God… and he was called God’s friend.

lessons: God shares His heart with His friends and invites them into His concerns.
Effective intercession appeals to God’s character with both boldness and humility.
God is looking for people who will stand in the gap for others.
questions: What does Ezekiel 16:49 add to our understanding of Sodom’s sin?
Why did Abraham appeal to God’s character, and not just ask for what he wanted?
What situation in your community or the world could you ‘stand in the gap’ for?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What situation in the world is on your heart that you want me to pray about?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you are the Judge of all the earth, and you always do right.
I stand in the gap for…
Have mercy, and let your love and justice be seen there.

mission.text: This week, pray every day for one injustice in the world: poverty, violence or the persecution of Christians.

en.journal: Write a prayer of intercession modelled on Genesis 18: appeal to God’s character, be bold, be humble and be specific.

af.title: Sal die Regter van die Hele Aarde nie Reg Doen nie?
story: Genesis 18 gee ons ’n buitengewone blik op hoe God met sy vriende omgaan. Die Here kies doelbewus om sy planne aan Abraham te openbaar: ‘Want Ek het hom gekies, sodat hy sy kinders en sy huis ná hom kan beveel om die weg van die Here te hou deur te doen wat reg en regverdig is.’ God deel sy hart met Abraham deels sodat Abraham geregtigheid en genade kan leer en dit kan oordra.

Wat was Sodom se sonde? Genesis 19 beskryf gewelddadige, mishandelende gedrag. Esegiël 16:49 voeg ’n ander dimensie by: ‘Sy en haar dogters was hoogmoedig, oorvoed en onverskillig; hulle het die armes en behoeftiges nie gehelp nie.’ Sodom was ’n stad van trots, wreedheid en onverskilligheid teenoor lyding. Die ‘geroep’ wat God gehoor het, was die geroep van sy slagoffers.

Abraham se gebed is ’n voorbeeld van voorbidding. Hy beroep hom op God se karakter: ‘Sal die Regter van die hele aarde nie reg doen nie?’ Hy argumenteer nie dat God verkeerd is om te oordeel nie; hy beroep hom op God se eie geregtigheid en genade. Hy is vrymoedig, en kom weer en weer terug. Tog is hy nederig: ‘Ek is net stof en as.’ Vrymoedigheid en nederigheid is nie teenoorgesteldes in gebed nie; hulle hoort saam.

Let op dat God nooit nee sê nie. Elke keer as Abraham vra, stem God in. Abraham stop by tien, nie God nie. Dit wys iets van God se hart. Hy is ‘lankmoedig en oorvloedig in liefde’, en Hy soek redes om genade te bewys. Later sê God deur Esegiël: ‘Ek het gesoek na iemand… wat voor My in die bres sou staan ter wille van die land.’ God soek voorbidders.
Al is Sodom vernietig, het God ‘aan Abraham gedink’ en Lot gered. Abraham se gebed was nie verniet nie.
Die Bybel noem Abraham drie keer ‘God se vriend’. Vriendskap met God gaan nie net daaroor om seën te ontvang nie; dit sluit in om God se besorgdheid oor die wêreld te deel en vir ander te bid.

Jesus is die grootste voorbidder. Hy het in die bres gestaan, nie net met woorde nie, maar met sy lewe, en Hy ‘lewe altyd om vir ons in te tree’. As sy vriende word ons genooi om saam met Hom vir ’n gebroke wêreld te bid.

verse.text: Abraham het God geglo… en hy is God se vriend genoem.

lessons: God deel sy hart met sy vriende en nooi hulle in sy besorgdheid in.
Doeltreffende voorbidding beroep hom op God se karakter met vrymoedigheid sowel as nederigheid.
God soek mense wat vir ander in die bres sal staan.
questions: Wat voeg Esegiël 16:49 by tot ons begrip van Sodom se sonde?
Hoekom het Abraham hom op God se karakter beroep, en nie net gevra vir wat hy wou hê nie?
Vir watter situasie in jou gemeenskap of die wêreld kan jy ‘in die bres staan’?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Watter situasie in die wêreld lê op u hart waaroor U wil hê ek moet bid?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U is die Regter van die hele aarde, en U doen altyd reg.
Ek staan in die bres vir…
Wees genadig, en laat u liefde en geregtigheid daar gesien word.

mission.text: Bid hierdie week elke dag vir een onreg in die wêreld: armoede, geweld of die vervolging van Christene.

af.journal: Skryf ’n voorbiddingsgebed op die patroon van Genesis 18: beroep jou op God se karakter, wees vrymoedig, wees nederig en wees spesifiek.

en.title: Abraham Prays for Others
story: Abraham’s nephew Lot lived in a city where people did bad things.
Abraham talked to God about it.
‘Please, God, be kind to the people there!’ Abraham prayed.
God listened to Abraham, and He rescued Lot.
