verse.text: Bid vir mekaar. Die gebed van ’n goeie mens het groot krag.

lessons: God luister as ek vir ander bid.
God is lief daarvoor om genade te bewys.
Ek kan met God praat soos met ’n vriend.
questions: Wat het Abraham aangehou om vir God te vra?
Vir wie wil jy graag bid?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat ek met U kan praat soos met ’n vriend.
Vanaand bid ek vir…
Wys hulle asseblief u liefde en goedheid. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre op die naam vir drie mense: iemand in jou familie, ’n maat en iemand wat siek of hartseer is.

af.fact: Die Bybel noem Abraham drie keer ‘God se vriend’. Dis ’n spesiale naam! Jesus het ook vir sy dissipels gesê: ‘Ek noem julle vriende.’
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het God Abraham laat aanhou vra, heeltemal tot by tien?
af.journal: Skryf die name van mense vir wie jy wil bid op ’n lys, en merk elkeen af nadat jy gebid het.

trait.en: The Lord will provide
trait.af: Die Here sal voorsien

en.title: The Lord Will Provide
story: Isaac was the miracle son, the one God had promised for twenty-five years. Through Isaac, God had said, His promises would come true. Then came the hardest moment of Abraham’s life.

‘Some time later God tested Abraham.’ He told him to take Isaac, ‘your only son, whom you love’, to the region of Moriah and offer him there as a burnt offering. This command is shocking. Later in the Bible, God strictly forbids child sacrifice, calling it detestable. So why this test?

The story makes clear from the first verse that it was a test, and that God never intended Isaac to die. The question was whether Abraham trusted God more than he loved God’s gift. Would he hold on to the promise, or to the Promiser?

Abraham obeyed. Early the next morning, he set off. On the third day, he saw the place in the distance and told his servants, ‘We will worship and then we will come back to you.’ We, not I. Hebrews 11 says Abraham reasoned that ‘God could even raise the dead’. He was sure God would keep His promise about Isaac somehow.
As they climbed, Isaac carried the wood. ‘Father, the fire and wood are here, but where is the lamb?’ Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb, my son.’

At the top, at the decisive moment, the angel of the Lord called out, ‘Abraham! Abraham!… Do not lay a hand on the boy… Now I know that you fear God.’ Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He offered it instead of his son. He called the place ‘The Lord Will Provide’, Jehovah Jireh.

About two thousand years later, on the same range of hills, God did what He didn’t require of Abraham. He gave His only Son, whom He loved. Jesus carried the wood of His cross up the hill. John the Baptist had called Him ‘the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world’. God Himself provided the Lamb.

verse.text: God Himself will provide the lamb.

lessons: God provides, even in the hardest situations.
Faith trusts the Promiser more than the gift.
God provided the true Lamb, Jesus, for us.
questions: What did Abraham mean when he told his servants, ‘We will come back’?
How does this story point to Jesus?
Is there a gift from God you are holding more tightly than God Himself?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘How have you provided for me? How do you want me to trust you now?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jehovah Jireh, you are the God who provides.
Thank you for providing Jesus, the Lamb of God, for me.
I trust you with…

mission.text: This week, keep a ‘Jehovah Jireh’ list: write down every way you notice God providing for you.

en.journal: Make two columns: ‘Abraham and Isaac’ and ‘God and Jesus’. Write down all the connections you can find.

af.title: Die Here Sal Voorsien
story: Isak was die wonderwerk-seun, die een wat God vyf-en-twintig jaar lank belowe het. Deur Isak, het God gesê, sou sy beloftes waar word. Toe kom die moeilikste oomblik van Abraham se lewe.

‘’n Ruk later het God Abraham getoets.’ Hy het hom gesê om Isak, ‘jou enigste seun vir wie jy lief is’, na die streek Moria te neem en hom daar as brandoffer te offer. Hierdie bevel is skokkend. Later in die Bybel verbied God streng kinderoffers, en noem dit ’n gruwel. Hoekom dan hierdie toets?

Die storie maak van die eerste vers af duidelik dat dit ’n toets was, en dat God nooit bedoel het dat Isak moet sterf nie. Die vraag was of Abraham God meer vertrou as wat hy God se geskenk liefgehad het. Sou hy aan die belofte vashou, of aan die Een wat belowe het?

Abraham het gehoorsaam. Vroeg die volgende oggend het hy vertrek. Op die derde dag het hy die plek in die verte gesien en vir sy diensknegte gesê: ‘Ons sal aanbid en dan na julle terugkom.’ Ons, nie ek nie. Hebreërs 11 sê Abraham het geredeneer dat ‘God selfs dooies kan opwek’. Hy was seker God sou sy belofte oor Isak op een of ander manier hou.
Terwyl hulle uitklim, het Isak die hout gedra. ‘Pa, die vuur en die hout is hier, maar waar is die lam?’ Abraham het geantwoord: ‘God self sal die lam voorsien, my seun.’

Bo-op, op die beslissende oomblik, het die engel van die Here geroep: ‘Abraham! Abraham!… Moenie aan die seun raak nie… Nou weet Ek dat jy God vrees.’ Abraham het opgekyk en ’n ram gesien wat met sy horings in ’n struik vasgehaak het. Hy het dit in die plek van sy seun geoffer. Hy het die plek ‘Die Here Sal Voorsien’ genoem, Jahwe Jireh.

Omtrent tweeduisend jaar later, op dieselfde heuwelreeks, het God gedoen wat Hy nie van Abraham vereis het nie. Hy het sy enigste Seun gegee, vir wie Hy lief was. Jesus het die hout van sy kruis teen die heuwel uitgedra. Johannes die Doper het Hom ‘die Lam van God wat die sonde van die wêreld wegneem’ genoem. God self het die Lam voorsien.

verse.text: God self sal die lam voorsien.

lessons: God voorsien, selfs in die moeilikste situasies.
Geloof vertrou die Een wat belowe meer as die geskenk.
God het die ware Lam, Jesus, vir ons voorsien.
questions: Wat het Abraham bedoel toe hy vir sy diensknegte gesê het: ‘Ons sal terugkom’?
Hoe wys hierdie storie na Jesus?
Is daar ’n geskenk van God waaraan jy stywer vashou as aan God self?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Hoe het U vir my voorsien? Hoe wil U hê moet ek U nou vertrou?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jahwe Jireh, U is die God wat voorsien.
Dankie dat U Jesus, die Lam van God, vir my voorsien het.
Ek vertrou U met…

mission.text: Hou hierdie week ’n ‘Jahwe Jireh’-lys: skryf elke manier neer waarop jy agterkom God voorsien vir jou.

af.journal: Maak twee kolomme: ‘Abraham en Isak’ en ‘God en Jesus’. Skryf al die verbande neer wat jy kan kry.

en.title: On the Mountain of the Lord
story: Genesis 22 is one of the most difficult and profound chapters in the Bible. It needs to be read carefully, in its full context.

First, the narrator tells us at the start: ‘God tested Abraham.’ The reader knows from the first line what Abraham didn’t: this is a test, not God’s real intention. And elsewhere the Bible is absolutely clear that God abhors child sacrifice (Leviticus 18:21; Jeremiah 7:31). Genesis 22 isn’t teaching that God wants such things; it is showing that God is utterly unlike the gods of the surrounding nations, who did demand them.

Second, what was being tested? Abraham had waited twenty-five years for Isaac. Isaac was the fulfilment of every promise. The test asked, in effect: do you love the gift more than the Giver? Do you trust Me even when you can’t see how My promise will be kept? Hebrews tells us Abraham’s reasoning: ‘He considered that God was able even to raise him from the dead.’ His confident words to the servants, ‘We will come back to you’, show that he expected God to keep the promise somehow.

Third, the details point forward. The phrase ‘your son, your only son, whom you love’ is echoed at Jesus’ baptism: ‘This is my Son, whom I love.’ Isaac carries the wood up the mountain; Jesus carries His cross. Moriah is the region where Solomon’s temple was later built, close to where Jesus was crucified. And Abraham’s prophetic words, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb’, find their fulfilment when John points to Jesus: ‘Look, the Lamb of God!’

Fourth, the substitute. A ram dies in Isaac’s place. This is the first clear picture of substitution in Scripture: one life given in place of another. God stopped Abraham’s hand, but God did not spare His own Son. Paul writes: ‘He who did not spare His own Son, but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, graciously give us all things?’

Abraham named the place ‘The Lord Will Provide’, and the saying remained: ‘On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.’ On that mountain, centuries later, God provided everything we need: forgiveness, life and a relationship with Him.

verse.text: He who did not spare His own Son, but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, graciously give us all things?

lessons: Genesis 22 shows that God, unlike the false gods, provides the sacrifice Himself.
Faith trusts the Giver more than the gift, believing God will keep His promises.
The ram in Isaac’s place points to Jesus, the Lamb who died in our place.
questions: Why is it important that the reader knows from verse 1 that this is a test?
List the parallels between Isaac and Jesus. Which one strikes you most?
What does Romans 8:32 mean for your daily life and needs?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there a gift from you that I am holding more tightly than you?’ Write down what you sense, and offer it back to Him in prayer.
prayer: Jehovah Jireh, you provided the Lamb for me.
Thank you that you did not spare your own Son.
I offer back to you… and trust you to provide all I need.

mission.text: This week, read Hebrews 11 and choose one person from that chapter whose faith you want to learn from.

en.journal: Write about the difference between loving God’s gifts and loving God. How can you enjoy His gifts without letting them replace Him?

af.title: Op die Berg van die Here
story: Genesis 22 is een van die moeilikste en diepste hoofstukke in die Bybel. Dit moet versigtig gelees word, in sy volle konteks.

Eerstens vertel die verteller ons aan die begin: ‘God het Abraham getoets.’ Die leser weet van die eerste reël af wat Abraham nie geweet het nie: dit is ’n toets, nie God se werklike bedoeling nie. En elders is die Bybel absoluut duidelik dat God kinderoffers verafsku (Levitikus 18:21; Jeremia 7:31). Genesis 22 leer nie dat God sulke dinge wil hê nie; dit wys dat God heeltemal anders is as die gode van die nasies rondom, wat dit wel geëis het.

Tweedens, wat is getoets? Abraham het vyf-en-twintig jaar vir Isak gewag. Isak was die vervulling van elke belofte. Die toets het eintlik gevra: het jy die geskenk meer lief as die Gewer? Vertrou jy My selfs as jy nie kan sien hoe my belofte gehou sal word nie? Hebreërs vertel ons Abraham se redenasie: ‘Hy het daarmee rekening gehou dat God hom selfs uit die dood kon opwek.’ Sy vol vertroue woorde aan die diensknegte, ‘Ons sal na julle terugkom’, wys dat hy verwag het God sou die belofte op een of ander manier hou.

Derdens wys die besonderhede vorentoe. Die uitdrukking ‘jou seun, jou enigste seun, vir wie jy lief is’ eggo by Jesus se doop: ‘Dit is my Seun, vir wie Ek lief is.’ Isak dra die hout teen die berg op; Jesus dra sy kruis. Moria is die streek waar Salomo se tempel later gebou is, naby waar Jesus gekruisig is. En Abraham se profetiese woorde, ‘God self sal die lam voorsien’, word vervul wanneer Johannes na Jesus wys: ‘Kyk, die Lam van God!’

Vierdens, die plaasvervanger. ’n Ram sterf in Isak se plek. Dit is die eerste duidelike prentjie van plaasvervanging in die Skrif: een lewe wat in die plek van ’n ander gegee word. God het Abraham se hand gekeer, maar God het sy eie Seun nie gespaar nie. Paulus skryf: ‘Hy wat sy eie Seun nie gespaar het nie, maar Hom vir ons almal oorgegee het, sal Hy ons nie ook saam met Hom alles genadiglik gee nie?’

Abraham het die plek ‘Die Here Sal Voorsien’ genoem, en die gesegde het gebly: ‘Op die berg van die Here sal voorsien word.’ Op daardie berg het God eeue later alles voorsien wat ons nodig het: vergifnis, lewe en ’n verhouding met Hom.

verse.text: Hy wat sy eie Seun nie gespaar het nie, maar Hom vir ons almal oorgegee het, sal Hy ons nie ook saam met Hom alles genadiglik gee nie?

lessons: Genesis 22 wys dat God, anders as die vals gode, self die offer voorsien.
Geloof vertrou die Gewer meer as die geskenk, en glo dat God sy beloftes sal hou.
Die ram in Isak se plek wys na Jesus, die Lam wat in ons plek gesterf het.
questions: Hoekom is dit belangrik dat die leser van vers 1 af weet dat dit ’n toets is?
Lys die ooreenkomste tussen Isak en Jesus. Watter een tref jou die meeste?
Wat beteken Romeine 8:32 vir jou daaglikse lewe en behoeftes?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is daar ’n geskenk van U waaraan ek stywer vashou as aan U?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel, en bied dit in gebed aan Hom terug.
prayer: Jahwe Jireh, U het die Lam vir my voorsien.
Dankie dat U u eie Seun nie gespaar het nie.
Ek bied… aan U terug en vertrou U om alles te voorsien wat ek nodig het.

mission.text: Lees hierdie week Hebreërs 11 en kies een persoon uit daardie hoofstuk van wie se geloof jy wil leer.

af.journal: Skryf oor die verskil tussen om God se gawes lief te hê en om God lief te hê. Hoe kan jy sy gawes geniet sonder om hulle Hom te laat vervang?

en.title: God Provides
story: Abraham and his son Isaac climbed a big mountain to worship God.
Isaac asked, ‘Where is the lamb for the offering?’
Abraham said, ‘God will provide.’
And God did! There was a ram stuck in a bush.
God gives us what we need!

verse.text: The Lord will provide.

en.action: Climb up a pretend mountain, then point and say: ‘Look! God provides!’
lessons: God gives me what I need.
questions: What has God given you today?
prayer: Thank you, God,
you give me everything I need. Amen.

af.title: God Voorsien
story: Abraham en sy seun Isak het teen ’n groot berg uitgeklim om God te aanbid.
Isak het gevra: ‘Waar is die lam vir die offer?’
Abraham het gesê: ‘God sal voorsien.’
En God het! Daar was ’n ram wat in ’n bos vasgehaak het.
God gee vir ons wat ons nodig het!

verse.text: Die Here sal voorsien.

af.action: Klim teen ’n speel-berg uit, wys dan en sê: ‘Kyk! God voorsien!’
lessons: God gee my wat ek nodig het.
questions: Wat het God vandag vir jou gegee?
prayer: Dankie, God,
U gee my alles wat ek nodig het. Amen.

I can trust God even with the hardest things.
God gave His own Son, Jesus, because He loves me.

How does this story remind you of Jesus?
prayer: Dear God,
you are the God who provides.
Thank you for giving Jesus for me.
Help me to trust you with everything. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, thank God for three things He has provided for you.

Hoe herinner hierdie storie jou aan Jesus?

en.title: Campfire Night: The Tent of Promises
story: Welcome to the first campfire of the Trail of the Promise Keeper! This week you camped with Abraham, the man the Bible calls ‘God’s friend’. You saw people at Babel trying to make a name for themselves, and Abram receiving a great name by trusting God. You watched him leave everything to follow God without a map, let Lot choose first, welcome visitors who brought an impossible promise, pray boldly for a wicked city and climb a mountain where God provided a ram. Through it all, God kept every promise, and Abraham learned that nothing is too hard for the Lord.
en.game: Promise chain: write as many of God’s promises to Abraham as you can remember on strips of paper. Loop them together into a paper chain. How long can you make it?
questions: Which moment in Abraham’s life would you have found hardest? Why?
What have you learned about God from Abraham’s story?
What have you sensed God saying in your Listening times?
prayer: God, you are the Promise Keeper.
Thank you that nothing is too hard for you and that you always provide.
Make me your friend, like Abraham.

mission.text: Learn Genesis 18:14 by heart this week, and say it whenever you face something hard.

en.journal: Draw a tent under the stars. Around it, write six things you learned about God from Abraham this week.

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Die Tent van Beloftes
story: Welkom by die eerste kampvuur van Die Pad van die Beloftehouer! Hierdie week het jy saam met Abraham kamp gemaak, die man wat die Bybel ‘God se vriend’ noem. Jy het mense by Babel gesien wat vir hulleself ’n naam wou maak, en Abram wat ’n groot naam ontvang het deur God te vertrou. Jy het gesien hoe hy alles agterlaat om God sonder ’n kaart te volg, Lot eerste laat kies, besoekers verwelkom wat ’n onmoontlike belofte gebring het, vrymoedig vir ’n goddelose stad bid en teen ’n berg uitklim waar God ’n ram voorsien het. Deur dit alles het God elke belofte gehou, en Abraham het geleer dat niks vir die Here te moeilik is nie.
af.game: Beloftekettinkie: skryf soveel van God se beloftes aan Abraham as wat jy kan onthou op stroke papier. Haak hulle aan mekaar tot ’n papierketting. Hoe lank kan jy dit maak?
questions: Watter oomblik in Abraham se lewe sou jy die moeilikste gevind het? Hoekom?
Wat het jy oor God geleer uit Abraham se storie?
Wat het jy aangevoel God sê in jou Luistertye?
prayer: God, U is die Beloftehouer.
Dankie dat niks vir U te moeilik is nie en dat U altyd voorsien.
Maak my u vriend, soos Abraham.

mission.text: Leer hierdie week Genesis 18:14 uit jou kop, en sê dit elke keer as jy voor iets moeiliks staan.

af.journal: Teken ’n tent onder die sterre. Skryf rondom dit ses dinge wat jy hierdie week by Abraham oor God geleer het.

en.title: Campfire Night: The Tent of Promises
story: This week you followed the man through whom God began His rescue plan for the whole world. At Babel, humanity tried to grab a great name; with Abram, God gave one by grace. You saw faith that went without a map, generosity that flowed from security in God, doubtful laughter turned to joy, bold intercession for a wicked city and a mountain where God provided a substitute, pointing to Jesus, the Lamb of God. Abraham wasn’t perfect. He doubted, he lied in Egypt, and he tried to force God’s promise through Hagar. But God was faithful, and Abraham grew into a friend of God whose faith Hebrews holds up for all of us.

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Die Tent van Beloftes

Jy het geloof gesien wat sonder ’n kaart gegaan het, vrygewigheid wat uit sekuriteit in God gevloei het, twyfelende gelag wat in vreugde verander het, vrymoedige voorbidding vir ’n goddelose stad en ’n berg waar God ’n plaasvervanger voorsien het, wat na Jesus, die Lam van God, wys. Abraham was nie volmaak nie. Hy het getwyfel, hy het in Egipte gelieg, en hy het probeer om God se belofte deur Hagar te forseer. Maar God was getrou, en Abraham het gegroei tot ’n vriend van God wie se geloof Hebreërs vir ons almal as voorbeeld stel.
af.game: Lees saam Hebreërs 11:8–19. Maak dan ’n tydlyn van Abraham se lewe, en merk elke belofte wat God gemaak het en elke oomblik wat Abraham Hom vertrou het (of gesukkel het om Hom te vertrou).
questions: Watter deel van Abraham se storie het jou geloof hierdie week die meeste uitgedaag?
Hoe is Abraham se storie verbind met Jesus en met jou?
Wat het jy in jou Luisterjoernaal aangevoel?
prayer: God, dankie dat U getrou is selfs as ek nie is nie.
Hierdie week het ek geleer dat U…

story: Well done, little explorer! Let’s sit by the campfire and remember: God is the greatest. God leads me. I can share. Nothing is too hard for God. God listens when I pray. The Lord will provide.

you always keep your promises. Amen.

prayer: Dankie, God,

en.title: Is the Lord Among Us?
story: Only weeks earlier, God had split the Red Sea, turned bitter water sweet and begun sending manna from heaven every morning. You would think God’s people would trust Him completely. But when they camped at Rephidim and found no water, they quarrelled with Moses: ‘Give us water to drink!’

Moses answered, ‘Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the Lord to the test?’ But they were thirsty, and they kept grumbling: ‘Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?’ It got so bad that Moses cried out to the Lord, ‘What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.’
Notice what Moses did with his frustration. He didn’t shout back. He took it to God.

God’s answer was full of patience. ‘Walk on ahead of the people. Take with you some of the elders and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go. I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it.’ Moses did, and water flowed for everyone.
Moses named the place Massah, meaning ‘testing’, and Meribah, meaning ‘quarrelling’, ‘because the Israelites quarrelled and because they tested the Lord saying, “Is the Lord among us or not?”’
That was the real problem. Their question wasn’t only about water. It was about whether God was really with them. After everything God had done, they still doubted His presence and His goodness.

Paul later wrote that the rock that gave water was a picture of Christ: ‘They drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.’ Jesus is the one who satisfies our deepest thirst. When we face hard times, the answer to ‘Is the Lord among us?’ is always yes.

verse.text: The Lord is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love.

lessons: God is patient with us, even when we grumble.
Bringing our frustrations to God is better than complaining.
God is always with us, even when we doubt it.
questions: What was the people’s real question, underneath the request for water?
How did Moses deal with his frustration?
When are you most tempted to grumble? What could you do instead?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Where have I been grumbling instead of trusting you?’ Write down what you sense, and turn it into a prayer.
prayer: God, thank you for being patient with me.
Forgive me for grumbling about…
I trust that you are with me, even when life is hard.

mission.text: This week, try a ‘no grumbling’ challenge: every time you want to complain, thank God for something instead.

en.journal: Make a list of five things you have grumbled about recently. Next to each one, write something you could thank God for in that situation.

af.title: Is die Here by Ons?
story: Net weke tevore het God die Rietsee oopgemaak, bitter water soet gemaak en begin om elke oggend manna uit die hemel te stuur. Jy sou dink God se volk sou Hom heeltemal vertrou. Maar toe hulle by Refidim kamp opslaan en geen water kry nie, het hulle met Moses gestry: ‘Gee vir ons water om te drink!’

Moses het geantwoord: ‘Hoekom stry julle met my? Hoekom stel julle die Here op die proef?’ Maar hulle was dors, en hulle het aangehou kla: ‘Hoekom het jy ons uit Egipte gebring om ons en ons kinders en ons vee van dors te laat sterf?’ Dit het so erg geword dat Moses tot die Here geroep het: ‘Wat moet ek met hierdie mense doen? Hulle is amper gereed om my met klippe te gooi.’
Let op wat Moses met sy frustrasie gedoen het. Hy het nie teruggeskree nie. Hy het dit na God geneem.

God se antwoord was vol geduld. ‘Loop voor die mense uit. Neem van die oudstes saam en neem in jou hand die staf waarmee jy die Nyl geslaan het, en gaan. Ek sal daar voor jou by die rots by Horeb staan. Slaan die rots, en water sal daaruit kom.’ Moses het dit gedoen, en water het vir almal gevloei.

Moses het die plek Massa genoem, wat ‘toets’ beteken, en Meriba, wat ‘rusie’ beteken, ‘omdat die Israeliete gestry het en omdat hulle die Here op die proef gestel het deur te sê: “Is die Here by ons of nie?”’

Dit was die werklike probleem. Hulle vraag het nie net oor water gegaan nie. Dit het gegaan oor of God regtig by hulle was. Ná alles wat God gedoen het, het hulle steeds aan sy teenwoordigheid en sy goedheid getwyfel.

Paulus het later geskryf dat die rots wat water gegee het, ’n prentjie van Christus was: ‘Hulle het gedrink uit die geestelike rots wat met hulle saamgegaan het, en daardie rots was Christus.’ Jesus is die een wat ons diepste dors les. As ons moeilike tye beleef, is die antwoord op ‘Is die Here by ons?’ altyd ja.

verse.text: Die Here is barmhartig en genadig, lankmoedig en oorvloedig in liefde.

lessons: God is geduldig met ons, selfs as ons kla.
Om ons frustrasies na God te bring, is beter as om te kla.
God is altyd by ons, selfs as ons daaraan twyfel.
questions: Wat was die mense se werklike vraag, onder die versoek om water?
Hoe het Moses sy frustrasie hanteer?
Wanneer kom jy die meeste in die versoeking om te kla? Wat kan jy eerder doen?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Waar het ek gekla in plaas daarvan om U te vertrou?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel, en maak dit ’n gebed.
prayer: God, dankie dat U geduldig is met my.
Vergewe my dat ek kla oor…
Ek vertrou dat U by my is, selfs as die lewe moeilik is.

mission.text: Probeer hierdie week ’n ‘geen-klaery’-uitdaging: elke keer as jy wil kla, dank God eerder vir iets.

af.journal: Maak ’n lys van vyf dinge waaroor jy onlangs gekla het. Skryf langs elkeen iets waarvoor jy God in daardie situasie kan dank.

en.title: Testing God or Trusting God?
story: Exodus 15–17 is a series of tests in the wilderness: bitter water at Marah, hunger in the Desert of Sin, and now no water at Rephidim. Each one reveals what is in the people’s hearts. God had said at Marah, ‘I am the Lord, who heals you.’ He had provided manna and quail. The pattern should have built trust. Instead, each crisis brought fresh complaining.

At Rephidim, the people ‘quarrelled’ with Moses. The Hebrew word suggests a legal dispute, like bringing a lawsuit. They put God on trial. And Moses names what they were really doing: ‘Why do you put the Lord to the test?’ Their underlying question comes at the end: ‘Is the Lord among us or not?’

There is a difference between bringing honest questions to God and putting God on trial. The Psalms are full of honest laments: ‘How long, Lord?’ That is faith wrestling. But testing God demands that He prove Himself on our terms, as if His past faithfulness counted for nothing. It is unbelief dressed up as a question.

God’s response is remarkable. He doesn’t destroy them. He tells Moses to take the elders as witnesses, and He says, ‘I will stand there before you by the rock.’ God Himself stands on the rock that Moses strikes. Some see here a picture of the cross: God receiving the blow, so that life-giving water can flow to a rebellious people.

Paul makes the connection explicit: ‘that rock was Christ.’ Jesus later stood up at a festival and shouted, ‘Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.’ The water from the rock points to the living water of the Spirit, given through Christ.

Centuries later, Psalm 95 used this story as a warning: ‘Today, if only you would hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah.’ Hebrews quotes it again for Christians: ‘See to it… that none of you has a sinful, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.’
The lesson isn’t that we must never struggle. It is that we should bring our struggles to God with trust in His character, remembering everything He has already done.

verse.text: Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.

lessons: Honest questions to God are faith; putting God on trial is unbelief.
God graciously provides even for grumbling people.
The rock points to Christ, the source of living water.
questions: What is the difference between lament and testing God?
Why do you think the Israelites kept forgetting God’s past faithfulness?
How can remembering what God has done help you trust Him now?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Remember three times God has been faithful to you. Then ask Him: ‘Where is my heart hardening?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you have been faithful to me so many times, including…
Forgive me when I put you on trial instead of trusting you.
Keep my heart soft to your voice.

mission.text: Start a ‘Faithfulness Journal’ this week: each day, write one way God has been faithful to you or your family.

en.journal: Write a psalm of honest lament about something hard, but end it, as the Psalms often do, with trust in God’s character.

af.title: God Toets of God Vertrou?
story: Eksodus 15–17 is ’n reeks toetse in die woestyn: bitter water by Mara, honger in die Sinwoestyn, en nou geen water by Refidim nie. Elkeen wys wat in die mense se harte is. God het by Mara gesê: ‘Ek is die Here wat jou gesond maak.’ Hy het manna en kwartels voorsien. Die patroon moes vertroue gebou het. In plaas daarvan het elke krisis nuwe geklaag gebring.

By Refidim het die mense met Moses ‘gestry’. Die Hebreeuse woord dui op ’n regsgeding, soos om ’n hofsaak aanhangig te maak. Hulle het God verhoor. En Moses noem wat hulle eintlik gedoen het: ‘Hoekom stel julle die Here op die proef?’ Hulle onderliggende vraag kom aan die einde: ‘Is die Here by ons of nie?’

Daar is ’n verskil tussen om eerlike vrae na God te bring en om God te verhoor. Die Psalms is vol eerlike klaagliedere: ‘Hoe lank nog, Here?’ Dit is geloof wat worstel. Maar om God op die proef te stel, eis dat Hy Homself op ons voorwaardes bewys, asof sy vorige trou niks tel nie. Dit is ongeloof wat soos ’n vraag aangetrek is.

God se reaksie is merkwaardig. Hy vernietig hulle nie. Hy sê vir Moses om die oudstes as getuies saam te neem, en Hy sê: ‘Ek sal daar voor jou by die rots staan.’ God self staan op die rots wat Moses slaan. Party sien hier ’n prentjie van die kruis: God wat die slag ontvang, sodat lewegewende water na ’n opstandige volk kan vloei.

Paulus maak die verband duidelik: ‘daardie rots was Christus.’ Jesus het later by ’n fees opgestaan en geroep: ‘As iemand dors het, laat hy na My toe kom en drink.’ Die water uit die rots wys na die lewende water van die Gees, wat deur Christus gegee word.

Eeue later het Psalm 95 hierdie storie as ’n waarskuwing gebruik: ‘Vandag, as julle maar net na sy stem wil luister, moenie julle harte verhard soos by Meriba nie.’ Hebreërs haal dit weer aan vir Christene: ‘Pas op… dat niemand van julle ’n sondige, ongelowige hart het wat van die lewende God afvallig word nie.’
Die les is nie dat ons nooit mag sukkel nie. Dit is dat ons ons stryd na God moet bring met vertroue in sy karakter, en alles onthou wat Hy reeds gedoen het.

verse.text: Vandag, as julle sy stem hoor, moenie julle harte verhard nie.

lessons: Eerlike vrae aan God is geloof; om God te verhoor, is ongeloof.
God voorsien genadig selfs vir mense wat kla.
Die rots wys na Christus, die bron van lewende water.
questions: Wat is die verskil tussen klaag en God op die proef stel?
Hoekom dink jy het die Israeliete aanhou vergeet van God se vorige trou?
Hoe kan dit om te onthou wat God gedoen het, jou help om Hom nou te vertrou?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Onthou drie keer wat God aan jou getrou was. Vra Hom dan: ‘Waar raak my hart verhard?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U was al soveel keer aan my getrou, ook…
Vergewe my as ek U verhoor in plaas daarvan om U te vertrou.
Hou my hart sag vir u stem.

mission.text: Begin hierdie week ’n ‘Troujoernaal’: skryf elke dag een manier neer waarop God aan jou of jou familie getrou was.

af.journal: Skryf ’n psalm van eerlike klag oor iets moeiliks, maar eindig dit, soos die Psalms dikwels doen, met vertroue in God se karakter.

en.title: Water from a Rock
story: God’s people were in the hot desert. They were so thirsty!
They grumbled, ‘We want water!’
Moses prayed to God.
God said, ‘Hit the rock with your stick.’ Whack! Out came water! Splash!
God is patient, and He takes care of us.

verse.text: God is patient and full of love.

en.action: Tap the floor like Moses hitting the rock, then pretend to drink: ‘Thank you, God!’
lessons: God is patient and takes care of me.
questions: What do you say when you’re thirsty?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for being patient with me. Amen.

af.title: Water uit ’n Rots
story: God se mense was in die warm woestyn. Hulle was so dors!
Hulle het gekla: ‘Ons wil water hê!’
Moses het tot God gebid.
God het gesê: ‘Slaan die rots met jou stok.’ Kaboem! Daar kom water uit! Spat!
God is geduldig, en Hy sorg vir ons.

verse.text: God is geduldig en vol liefde.

af.action: Tik op die vloer soos Moses wat die rots slaan, en maak dan of jy drink: ‘Dankie, God!’
lessons: God is geduldig en sorg vir my.
questions: Wat sê jy as jy dors is?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U geduldig is met my. Amen.

en.title: Grumbling in the Desert
story: After God rescued His people from Egypt, they travelled through the desert with Moses. God had already done so many miracles for them. He had parted the sea and sent bread from heaven every morning!
One day they camped at a place called Rephidim, and there was no water at all. The sun was hot, the children were thirsty and the animals were thirsty.

But instead of asking God for help, the people grumbled and complained. ‘Give us water!’ they shouted at Moses. ‘Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die of thirst?’ They were so cross that Moses was afraid they might throw stones at him.
Moses did the right thing. He cried out to God. ‘What shall I do with these people?’

God was patient with them. He said, ‘Take your staff and go ahead of the people. I will stand before you by the rock. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it.’ Moses did it, and water gushed out of the rock, enough for everyone!

God took care of them, even when they were grumbling. But He wanted them to learn to trust Him and ask Him nicely, instead of complaining. When we need something, we can tell God about it. He loves to help.

verse.text: The Lord is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, full of love.

lessons: God is patient even when we grumble.
I can ask God for help instead of complaining.
God takes care of His children.
questions: What did the people do when they were thirsty? What did Moses do?
What do you sometimes grumble about? How could you pray instead?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for being so patient with me.
Help me to ask you for help
instead of grumbling. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, every time you feel like grumbling, say a little prayer instead.

af.title: Kla in die Woestyn
story: Nadat God sy volk uit Egipte gered het, het hulle saam met Moses deur die woestyn gereis. God het al soveel wonderwerke vir hulle gedoen. Hy het die see oopgemaak en elke oggend brood uit die hemel gestuur!
Eendag het hulle by ’n plek met die naam Refidim kamp opgeslaan, en daar was glad nie water nie. Die son was warm, die kinders was dors en die diere was dors.

Maar in plaas daarvan om God vir hulp te vra, het die mense gekla en gebrom. ‘Gee vir ons water!’ het hulle vir Moses geskree. ‘Hoekom het jy ons uit Egipte gebring om van dors dood te gaan?’ Hulle was so kwaad dat Moses bang was hulle sou klippe na hom gooi.
Moses het die regte ding gedoen. Hy het tot God geroep. ‘Wat moet ek met hierdie mense doen?’

God was geduldig met hulle. Hy het gesê: ‘Vat jou staf en gaan voor die mense uit. Ek sal voor jou by die rots staan. Slaan die rots, en water sal daaruit kom.’ Moses het dit gedoen, en water het uit die rots gestroom, genoeg vir almal!

God het vir hulle gesorg, selfs terwyl hulle gekla het. Maar Hy wou hê hulle moet leer om Hom te vertrou en mooi te vra, in plaas daarvan om te kla. As ons iets nodig het, kan ons God daarvan vertel. Hy help graag.

verse.text: Die Here is barmhartig en genadig, lankmoedig, vol liefde.

lessons: God is geduldig selfs as ons kla.
Ek kan God vir hulp vra in plaas daarvan om te kla.
God sorg vir sy kinders.
questions: Wat het die mense gedoen toe hulle dors was? Wat het Moses gedoen?
Waaroor kla jy soms? Hoe kan jy eerder bid?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U so geduldig is met my.
Help my om U vir hulp te vra
in plaas daarvan om te kla. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre elke keer as jy lus voel om te kla, eerder ’n klein gebedjie.

prayer: Dear God,
thank you for being so patient with me.
Help me to ask you for help
instead of grumbling. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, every time you feel like grumbling, say a little prayer instead.

en.fact: The New Testament says that the rock that gave water in the desert was a picture of Jesus. Jesus gives us living water that never runs out!
en.deeper: Why do you think the people forgot so quickly all the good things God had done?
en.journal: Draw a rock with water gushing out. Write: ‘God is patient with me.’

af.title: Kla in die Woestyn
story: Nadat God sy volk uit Egipte gered het, het hulle saam met Moses deur die woestyn gereis. God het al soveel wonderwerke vir hulle gedoen. Hy het die see oopgemaak en elke oggend brood uit die hemel gestuur!
Eendag het hulle by ’n plek met die naam Refidim kamp opgeslaan, en daar was glad nie water nie. Die son was warm, die kinders was dors en die diere was dors.

Maar in plaas daarvan om God vir hulp te vra, het die mense gekla en gebrom. ‘Gee vir ons water!’ het hulle vir Moses geskree. ‘Hoekom het jy ons uit Egipte gebring om van dors dood te gaan?’ Hulle was so kwaad dat Moses bang was hulle sou klippe na hom gooi.
Moses het die regte ding gedoen. Hy het tot God geroep. ‘Wat moet ek met hierdie mense doen?’

God was geduldig met hulle. Hy het gesê: ‘Vat jou staf en gaan voor die mense uit. Ek sal voor jou by die rots staan. Slaan die rots, en water sal daaruit kom.’ Moses het dit gedoen, en water het uit die rots gestroom, genoeg vir almal!

God het vir hulle gesorg, selfs terwyl hulle gekla het. Maar Hy wou hê hulle moet leer om Hom te vertrou en mooi te vra, in plaas daarvan om te kla. As ons iets nodig het, kan ons God daarvan vertel. Hy help graag.

verse.text: Die Here is barmhartig en genadig, lankmoedig, vol liefde.

lessons: God is geduldig selfs as ons kla.
Ek kan God vir hulp vra in plaas daarvan om te kla.
God sorg vir sy kinders.
questions: Wat het die mense gedoen toe hulle dors was? Wat het Moses gedoen?
Waaroor kla jy soms? Hoe kan jy eerder bid?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U so geduldig is met my.
Help my om U vir hulp te vra
in plaas daarvan om te kla. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre elke keer as jy lus voel om te kla, eerder ’n klein gebedjie.

af.fact: Die Nuwe Testament sê dat die rots wat in die woestyn water gegee het, ’n prentjie van Jesus was. Jesus gee vir ons lewende water wat nooit opraak nie!
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het die mense so gou al die goeie dinge vergeet wat God gedoen het?
af.journal: Teken ’n rots met water wat uitstroom. Skryf: ‘God is geduldig met my.’

trait.en: God gives friends to hold me up
trait.af: God gee vriende om my op te hou

en.title: The Lord Is My Banner
story: Soon after God provided water from the rock, the Amalekites attacked Israel at Rephidim. Deuteronomy tells us they targeted the weak and weary stragglers at the back of the line. It was a cruel attack on a tired people.

Moses said to Joshua, ‘Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hands.’ This is the first time Joshua appears in the Bible: a young military leader who would one day lead Israel into the promised land.

Joshua fought in the valley while Moses, Aaron and Hur went to the top of the hill. ‘As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning, but whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.’ Moses’ raised hands, holding God’s staff, showed that Israel’s strength depended on God, not on their own swords.

But Moses was a human being, and ‘his hands grew tired’. So Aaron and Hur took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. ‘Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on one side, one on the other, so that his hands remained steady till sunset.’ Joshua and his army won.

Then Moses built an altar and called it ‘The Lord is my Banner’ (Jehovah Nissi). A banner was a flag raised high in battle so soldiers knew where to rally. God Himself was their flag, their rallying point and the source of their victory.

This story shows us three things. God gives the victory. Even the greatest leaders get tired. And God provides friends to hold us up. Moses didn’t need to be strong enough on his own, and neither do you. Be the kind of friend who holds others up, and be humble enough to let others hold you up too.

verse.text: Two are better than one… If either of them falls down, one can help the other up.

lessons: Victory comes from God, not from our own strength.
Even strong leaders get tired and need help.
God gives us friends to hold us up, and calls us to hold others up.
questions: Why do you think Moses’ raised hands affected the battle?
Who are the ‘Aaron and Hur’ people in your life?
Who might need you to hold up their arms this week?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Who do you want me to hold up this week? And who can I ask to hold me up?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, you are my Banner and my victory.
Thank you for the friends who hold me up, like…
Help me to hold up… this week.

mission.text: This week, encourage someone who seems tired or discouraged with a note, a prayer or practical help.

en.journal: Draw a banner with ‘Jehovah Nissi: The Lord is my Banner’ on it. Around it, write the names of friends who hold you up.

af.title: Die Here Is My Banier
story: Kort nadat God water uit die rots voorsien het, het die Amalekiete Israel by Refidim aangeval. Deuteronomium vertel ons hulle het die swakkes en moeëes wat agter in die ry gesukkel het, geteiken. Dit was ’n wrede aanval op ’n moeë volk.

Moses het vir Josua gesê: ‘Kies van ons mans en gaan veg teen die Amalekiete. Môre sal ek bo-op die heuwel staan met die staf van God in my hande.’ Dit is die eerste keer dat Josua in die Bybel verskyn: ’n jong militêre leier wat eendag Israel na die beloofde land sou lei.

Josua het in die vallei geveg terwyl Moses, Aäron en Hur tot bo-op die heuwel gegaan het. ‘Solank Moses sy hande ophou, het die Israeliete gewen, maar elke keer as hy sy hande laat sak, het die Amalekiete gewen.’ Moses se opgehefte hande, met God se staf daarin, het gewys dat Israel se krag van God afhang, nie van hulle eie swaarde nie.

Maar Moses was ’n mens, en ‘sy hande het moeg geword’. Toe het Aäron en Hur ’n klip gevat en dit onder hom gesit, en hy het daarop gesit. ‘Aäron en Hur het sy hande opgehou, een aan die een kant, een aan die ander kant, sodat sy hande stil gebly het tot sononder.’ Josua en sy leër het gewen.

Toe het Moses ’n altaar gebou en dit ‘Die Here is my Banier’ genoem (Jahwe Nissi). ’n Banier was ’n vlag wat hoog in die geveg opgehou is sodat soldate geweet het waar om bymekaar te kom. God self was hulle vlag, hulle versamelpunt en die bron van hulle oorwinning.

Hierdie storie wys ons drie dinge. God gee die oorwinning. Selfs die grootste leiers word moeg. En God voorsien vriende om ons op te hou. Moses hoef nie op sy eie sterk genoeg te wees nie, en jy ook nie. Wees die soort vriend wat ander ophou, en wees nederig genoeg om ander jou ook te laat ophou.

verse.text: Twee is beter as een… As een van hulle val, kan die ander een hom ophelp.

lessons: Oorwinning kom van God, nie van ons eie krag nie.
Selfs sterk leiers word moeg en het hulp nodig.
God gee ons vriende om ons op te hou, en roep ons om ander op te hou.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Moses se opgehefte hande die geveg beïnvloed?
Wie is die ‘Aäron en Hur’-mense in jou lewe?
Wie het jou dalk hierdie week nodig om hulle arms op te hou?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Wie wil U hê moet ek hierdie week ophou? En wie kan ek vra om my op te hou?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, U is my Banier en my oorwinning.
Dankie vir die vriende wat my ophou, soos…
Help my om… hierdie week op te hou.

mission.text: Bemoedig hierdie week iemand wat moeg of moedeloos lyk met ’n briefie, ’n gebed of praktiese hulp.

af.journal: Teken ’n banier met ‘Jahwe Nissi: Die Here is my Banier’ daarop. Skryf rondom dit die name van vriende wat jou ophou.

en.title: Raised Hands and Faithful Friends
story: Exodus 17 places two stories side by side: water from the rock and victory over Amalek. In the first, the people test God. In the second, God shows how He fights for them. Both happen at Rephidim, and both reveal that Israel’s survival depends entirely on God.

The attack was cowardly. Deuteronomy says Amalek ‘met you on your journey and attacked all who were lagging behind; when you were weary and worn out, they had no fear of God.’ They preyed on the vulnerable.

God’s strategy combined human action and divine power. Joshua and the soldiers had to fight; they didn’t just sit and watch. But the outcome depended on what happened on the hilltop. Moses’ raised hands with God’s staff were a visible prayer, a public declaration of dependence on God. When his hands dropped, Israel faltered. The lesson is clear: effort matters, but prayer and dependence on God matter more.

Then the human element: Moses’ hands grew heavy. The great prophet who had confronted Pharaoh and parted the sea couldn’t hold his arms up for a whole day. Leadership in God’s kingdom is never a solo act. Aaron, the priest, and Hur, a respected elder, supported him. Their role seems small, standing beside someone and holding his arms, but the battle was won because of their faithfulness.

Paul writes, ‘Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ.’ The Christian life is designed to be lived in community. We need people who will pray for us when we can’t pray, encourage us when we are discouraged and stand with us in our battles. And we are called to be those people for others.

The altar’s name, ‘The Lord is my Banner’, gathers it all up. Israel didn’t win under Moses’ banner or Joshua’s banner, but under God’s. Isaiah later prophesied that the Messiah would be ‘a banner for the peoples’, and Jesus said, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself.’ The cross is our banner: the place where we rally, and the source of our victory.

verse.text: Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ.

lessons: God’s victories combine our faithful effort with dependence on Him.
No one is meant to carry the battle alone; even great leaders need support.
Jesus, lifted up on the cross, is our banner and our victory.
questions: Why did the battle depend on what happened on the hilltop, not just in the valley?
Why do you think God designed us to need each other?
Are you better at holding others up or at letting others hold you up? Why?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What battle am I trying to fight alone? Who could stand with me?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, you are my Banner. My victory comes from you.
I confess I try to fight… on my own.
Give me faithful friends, and make me a faithful friend to others.

mission.text: This week, commit to praying daily for a friend who is going through a hard time, and tell them you are praying.

en.journal: Write about the ‘Aaron and Hur’ role. Why is it so important, even though it rarely gets noticed? How could you live that way?

af.title: Opgehefte Hande en Getroue Vriende
story: Eksodus 17 plaas twee stories langs mekaar: water uit die rots en oorwinning oor Amalek. In die eerste stel die mense God op die proef. In die tweede wys God hoe Hy vir hulle veg. Albei gebeur by Refidim, en albei wys dat Israel se oorlewing heeltemal van God afhang.

Die aanval was lafhartig. Deuteronomium sê Amalek ‘het jou op jou reis teëgekom en almal aangeval wat agtergebly het; toe jy moeg en uitgeput was, het hulle God nie gevrees nie.’ Hulle het die kwesbares aangeval.

God se strategie het menslike optrede en goddelike krag gekombineer. Josua en die soldate moes veg; hulle het nie net gesit en kyk nie. Maar die uitslag het afgehang van wat op die heuweltop gebeur het. Moses se opgehefte hande met God se staf was ’n sigbare gebed, ’n openbare verklaring van afhanklikheid van God. As sy hande sak, het Israel gewankel. Die les is duidelik: inspanning maak saak, maar gebed en afhanklikheid van God maak meer saak.

Dan die menslike element: Moses se hande het swaar geword. Die groot profeet wat Farao gekonfronteer en die see oopgemaak het, kon nie sy arms ’n hele dag lank ophou nie. Leierskap in God se koninkryk is nooit ’n alleenoptrede nie. Aäron, die priester, en Hur, ’n gerespekteerde oudste, het hom ondersteun. Hulle rol lyk klein, om langs iemand te staan en sy arms op te hou, maar die geveg is gewen weens hulle getrouheid.

Paulus skryf: ‘Dra mekaar se laste, en so sal julle die wet van Christus nakom.’ Die Christelike lewe is ontwerp om in gemeenskap geleef te word. Ons het mense nodig wat vir ons sal bid as ons nie kan bid nie, ons sal bemoedig as ons moedeloos is en saam met ons in ons gevegte sal staan. En ons word geroep om sulke mense vir ander te wees.

Die altaar se naam, ‘Die Here is my Banier’, som alles op. Israel het nie onder Moses se banier of Josua se banier gewen nie, maar onder God s’n. Jesaja het later geprofeteer dat die Messias ‘’n banier vir die volke’ sou wees, en Jesus het gesê: ‘Wanneer Ek van die aarde af verhoog word, sal Ek almal na My toe trek.’ Die kruis is ons banier: die plek waar ons bymekaarkom, en die bron van ons oorwinning.

verse.text: Dra mekaar se laste, en so sal julle die wet van Christus nakom.

lessons: God se oorwinnings kombineer ons getroue inspanning met afhanklikheid van Hom.
Niemand is bedoel om die stryd alleen te voer nie; selfs groot leiers het ondersteuning nodig.
Jesus, aan die kruis verhoog, is ons banier en ons oorwinning.
questions: Hoekom het die geveg afgehang van wat op die heuweltop gebeur het, nie net in die vallei nie?
Hoekom dink jy het God ons so ontwerp dat ons mekaar nodig het?
Is jy beter daarmee om ander op te hou of om ander jou te laat ophou? Hoekom?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Watter stryd probeer ek alleen voer? Wie kan saam met my staan?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, U is my Banier. My oorwinning kom van U.
Ek bely dat ek probeer om… op my eie te veg.
Gee my getroue vriende, en maak my ’n getroue vriend vir ander.

mission.text: Verbind jou hierdie week om daagliks te bid vir ’n vriend wat deur ’n moeilike tyd gaan, en sê vir hulle jy bid.

af.journal: Skryf oor die ‘Aäron-en-Hur’-rol. Hoekom is dit so belangrik, al word dit selde raakgesien? Hoe kan jy so lewe?

en.title: Hold Up My Arms
story: Moses held up his arms high on a hill.
When his arms were up, God’s people were winning!
But Moses got tired. His arms came down.
His friends Aaron and Hur held his arms up high!
God gives me friends to help me.

verse.text: Two are better than one.

en.action: Hold your arms up high, and ask someone to help hold them up!
lessons: God gives me friends to help me.
questions: How long can you hold your arms up?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for my friends who help me. Amen.

af.title: Hou My Arms Op
story: Moses het sy arms hoog op ’n heuwel opgehou.
As sy arms op was, het God se mense gewen!
Maar Moses het moeg geword. Sy arms het afgesak.
Sy vriende Aäron en Hur het sy arms hoog opgehou!
God gee my vriende om my te help.

verse.text: Twee is beter as een.

af.action: Hou jou arms hoog op, en vra iemand om te help om hulle op te hou!
lessons: God gee my vriende om my te help.
questions: Hoe lank kan jy jou arms ophou?
prayer: Dankie, God,
vir my vriende wat my help. Amen.

en.title: Tired Arms, Good Friends
story: While God’s people were travelling through the desert, an enemy army called the Amalekites attacked them.
Moses said to a young man called Joshua, ‘Choose some men and go out to fight. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with God’s staff in my hands.’

So Joshua led the soldiers in the valley, and Moses, Aaron and Hur climbed to the top of the hill. Moses lifted his hands high, holding the staff up to God. Whenever Moses held his hands up, Israel was winning! But whenever he lowered them, the enemy started winning.
Moses’ arms got tired, then heavy, then very, very heavy. Have you ever tried to hold your arms up for a long time? It’s hard!

So Aaron and Hur had an idea. They found a big stone for Moses to sit on. Then Aaron stood on one side and Hur on the other, and they held his arms up, all day long, until the sun went down. And Joshua and the soldiers won the battle!

Moses built an altar and called it ‘The Lord is my Banner’. God had given the victory. But God had also given Moses good friends who helped him when he was tired. We all need friends like that, and we can be that kind of friend too.

verse.text: Two are better than one… If either of them falls down, one can help the other up.

lessons: God gives me friends to hold me up.
I can help my friends when they are tired or sad.
The victory comes from God.
questions: How did Aaron and Hur help Moses?
Who is a friend who helps you? Who could you help?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for friends who help me.
Help me to be a good friend too,
and to help others when they are tired. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, be an ‘Aaron and Hur’ friend: help someone who is tired, sad or struggling.

af.title: Moeë Arms, Goeie Vriende
story: Terwyl God se mense deur die woestyn gereis het, het ’n vyandige leër, die Amalekiete, hulle aangeval.
Moses het vir ’n jong man met die naam Josua gesê: ‘Kies ’n paar mans en gaan veg. Môre sal ek bo-op die heuwel staan met God se staf in my hande.’

Toe het Josua die soldate in die vallei gelei, en Moses, Aäron en Hur het tot bo-op die heuwel geklim. Moses het sy hande hoog opgelig, en die staf na God toe opgehou. Elke keer as Moses sy hande ophou, het Israel gewen! Maar elke keer as hy hulle laat sak, het die vyand begin wen.
Moses se arms het moeg geword, toe swaar, toe baie, baie swaar. Het jy al probeer om jou arms vir ’n lang tyd op te hou? Dis moeilik!

Toe het Aäron en Hur ’n plan gemaak. Hulle het ’n groot klip gekry waarop Moses kon sit. Toe het Aäron aan die een kant gestaan en Hur aan die ander kant, en hulle het sy arms die hele dag lank opgehou, totdat die son ondergaan. En Josua en die soldate het die geveg gewen!

Moses het ’n altaar gebou en dit ‘Die Here is my Banier’ genoem. God het die oorwinning gegee. Maar God het Moses ook goeie vriende gegee wat hom gehelp het toe hy moeg was. Ons het almal sulke vriende nodig, en ons kan ook so ’n vriend wees.

verse.text: Twee is beter as een… As een van hulle val, kan die ander een hom ophelp.

lessons: God gee my vriende om my op te hou.
Ek kan my vriende help as hulle moeg of hartseer is.
Die oorwinning kom van God.
questions: Hoe het Aäron en Hur vir Moses gehelp?
Wie is ’n vriend wat jou help? Wie kan jy help?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir vriende wat my help.
Help my om ook ’n goeie vriend te wees,
en ander te help as hulle moeg is. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre ’n ‘Aäron-en-Hur’-vriend: help iemand wat moeg, hartseer of sukkel.

trait.en: God wants to live among His people
trait.af: God wil tussen sy mense woon

en.title: God Moves In
story: At Mount Sinai, God gave His people the Ten Commandments. Then He gave them something else: detailed plans for a portable sanctuary called the tabernacle. Why? God explained: ‘Have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.’
Think about that. The God who created the universe wanted to live in the middle of His people’s campsite. He wasn’t a distant God on a mountain; He wanted to be close.

The tabernacle was a large tent inside a courtyard. It had two rooms. The first, the Holy Place, held a golden lampstand, a table with bread and an altar of incense. The second, the Most Holy Place, held the ark of the covenant, a gold-covered chest containing the stone tablets of the law. A thick curtain separated the two rooms.

Building it required everyone’s gifts. Moses invited ‘everyone who is willing’ to bring offerings, and God filled skilled workers like Bezalel ‘with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of skills’. This is the first time the Bible says someone was filled with the Spirit, and it was for craftsmanship! The people were so generous that Moses had to tell them to stop giving.

When it was finished, ‘the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.’ The glory was so strong that even Moses couldn’t go in. From then on, the cloud by day and fire by night led them through the wilderness.

The tabernacle was a preview of something greater. John writes that Jesus ‘became flesh and made His dwelling among us’. The word literally means ‘pitched His tent among us’. And now Paul says, ‘Your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit.’ God has moved in!

verse.text: Have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.

lessons: God wants to live close to His people.
God gives gifts and skills, and we can use them for Him.
Jesus ‘pitched His tent’ among us, and the Spirit now lives in us.
questions: Why did God want a tabernacle in the middle of the camp?
What was surprising about the first person ‘filled with the Spirit’?
How does John 1:14 connect Jesus to the tabernacle?
en.listen: Be still and remember that God lives in you by His Spirit. Ask Him: ‘How do you want to use my gifts?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you that you want to live close to me.
Thank you that your Spirit lives in me.
I offer you my gifts, like…

mission.text: This week, use one of your skills or talents to serve at church, at home or at school, as a gift to God.

en.journal: Draw the tabernacle, with its courtyard, two rooms and the cloud above. Label each part, and write how each one points to Jesus.

af.title: God Kom Woon by Ons
story: By die berg Sinai het God sy volk die Tien Gebooie gegee. Toe het Hy hulle iets anders gegee: gedetailleerde planne vir ’n draagbare heiligdom wat die tabernakel genoem word. Hoekom? God het verduidelik: ‘Laat hulle vir My ’n heiligdom maak, en Ek sal tussen hulle woon.’
Dink daaraan. Die God wat die heelal geskep het, wou in die middel van sy volk se kampterrein woon. Hy was nie ’n verre God op ’n berg nie; Hy wou naby wees.

Die tabernakel was ’n groot tent binne ’n voorhof. Dit het twee kamers gehad. Die eerste, die Heilige Plek, het ’n goue lampstaander, ’n tafel met brood en ’n reukofferaltaar gehad. Die tweede, die Allerheiligste, het die verbondsark gehad, ’n kis met goud oorgetrek wat die klipplate van die wet bevat het. ’n Dik gordyn het die twee kamers geskei.

Om dit te bou, het almal se gawes gevra. Moses het ‘almal wat gewillig is’ genooi om offergawes te bring, en God het bekwame werkers soos Besaleël ‘met die Gees van God gevul, met wysheid, met insig, met kennis en met allerhande vaardighede’. Dit is die eerste keer dat die Bybel sê iemand is met die Gees gevul, en dit was vir vakmanskap! Die mense was so vrygewig dat Moses vir hulle moes sê om op te hou gee.

Toe dit klaar was, ‘het die wolk die tent van ontmoeting bedek, en die heerlikheid van die Here het die tabernakel gevul.’ Die heerlikheid was so sterk dat selfs Moses nie kon ingaan nie. Van toe af het die wolk bedags en vuur snags hulle deur die woestyn gelei.

Die tabernakel was ’n voorsmaak van iets groters. Johannes skryf dat Jesus ‘mens geword het en onder ons kom woon het’. Die woord beteken letterlik ‘sy tent onder ons opgeslaan het’. En nou sê Paulus: ‘Julle liggame is tempels van die Heilige Gees.’ God het by ons kom woon!

verse.text: Laat hulle vir My ’n heiligdom maak, en Ek sal tussen hulle woon.

lessons: God wil naby sy mense woon.
God gee gawes en vaardighede, en ons kan hulle vir Hom gebruik.
Jesus het ‘sy tent onder ons opgeslaan’, en die Gees woon nou in ons.
questions: Hoekom wou God ’n tabernakel in die middel van die kamp hê?
Wat was verrassend aan die eerste persoon wat ‘met die Gees gevul’ is?
Hoe verbind Johannes 1:14 Jesus met die tabernakel?
af.listen: Wees stil en onthou dat God deur sy Gees in jou woon. Vra Hom: ‘Hoe wil U my gawes gebruik?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie dat U naby my wil woon.
Dankie dat u Gees in my woon.
Ek bied U my gawes aan, soos…

mission.text: Gebruik hierdie week een van jou vaardighede of talente om by die kerk, by die huis of by die skool te dien, as ’n geskenk aan God.

af.journal: Teken die tabernakel, met sy voorhof, twee kamers en die wolk bo-oor. Benoem elke deel, en skryf hoe elkeen na Jesus wys.

en.title: The God Who Pitches His Tent
story: Readers are sometimes surprised that Exodus spends about thirteen chapters on the tabernacle, with measurements, materials and furniture described in detail, often twice. Why so much attention to a tent? Because it answers the central question of the whole Bible: how can a holy God live with sinful people?

The structure taught Israel about God. The tabernacle sat at the centre of the camp, showing that God belonged at the centre of their life. Its layout moved from the outer courtyard (where anyone in Israel could come) to the Holy Place (where only priests went) to the Most Holy Place (where only the high priest could enter, once a year, with sacrificial blood). God was near, but His holiness meant access was limited and costly.

The materials told a story too. Gold, blue, purple and scarlet were royal colours. Cherubim were woven into the curtains, echoing the cherubim that guarded Eden after the fall. The tabernacle was like a miniature Eden: a place where God and humans could meet again.

Notice how it was built. The people gave freely; nothing was taxed or forced. And God filled Bezalel with His Spirit for artistic skill, the first person in Scripture described as Spirit-filled. Creativity and craftsmanship are gifts of the Spirit, offered back to God in worship.

When it was complete, ‘the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.’ The book of Exodus begins with Israel enslaved, building cities for Pharaoh. It ends with Israel free, building a dwelling for God, and God filling it with His glory. That is the shape of redemption: from slavery to worship.

Then the New Testament takes the story further. ‘The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory.’ John uses the Greek word for ‘tabernacled’. Jesus is the true meeting place of God and humanity. At His death, the curtain tore, opening the Most Holy Place. And now believers are ‘a temple of the Holy Spirit’. The God who once lived in a tent now lives in His people.
That changes how we see our bodies, our community and our worship. You are where God dwells.

verse.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory.

lessons: The tabernacle shows how a holy God can live among sinful people.
Exodus moves from slavery to worship, and so does redemption.
Jesus is the true tabernacle, and the Spirit now makes believers God’s temple.
questions: What did the layout of the tabernacle teach about God’s nearness and holiness?
Why is it significant that the first Spirit-filled person was a craftsman?
How should knowing you are a ‘temple of the Holy Spirit’ affect your daily life?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Sit quietly and remind yourself: ‘God dwells in me.’ Ask Him: ‘How do you want to fill this temple with your glory?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you that you came to dwell with us in Jesus.
Thank you that your Spirit lives in me.
Fill me with your glory, and help me honour you with my body and my gifts.

mission.text: This week, use a creative gift (art, music, building, writing or cooking) as an act of worship to God.

en.journal: Trace God’s dwelling through the Bible: Eden, tabernacle, temple, Jesus, believers, new creation. Write one sentence about each.

af.title: Die God wat sy Tent Opslaan
story: Lesers is soms verbaas dat Eksodus omtrent dertien hoofstukke aan die tabernakel bestee, met afmetings, materiale en meubels in besonderhede beskryf, dikwels twee keer. Hoekom soveel aandag aan ’n tent? Omdat dit die sentrale vraag van die hele Bybel beantwoord: hoe kan ’n heilige God by sondige mense woon?

Die struktuur het Israel oor God geleer. Die tabernakel was in die middel van die kamp, wat gewys het dat God in die middel van hulle lewe hoort. Die uitleg het beweeg van die buitenste voorhof (waar enigiemand in Israel kon kom) na die Heilige Plek (waar net priesters gegaan het) na die Allerheiligste (waar net die hoëpriester kon ingaan, een keer per jaar, met offerbloed). God was naby, maar sy heiligheid het beteken toegang was beperk en duur.

Die materiale het ook ’n storie vertel. Goud, blou, pers en skarlaken was koninklike kleure. Gérubs is in die gordyne ingeweef, wat die gérubs eggo wat Eden ná die sondeval bewaak het. Die tabernakel was soos ’n klein Eden: ’n plek waar God en mense mekaar weer kon ontmoet.

Let op hoe dit gebou is. Die mense het vrywillig gegee; niks is belas of afgedwing nie. En God het Besaleël met sy Gees gevul vir kunsvaardigheid, die eerste persoon in die Skrif wat as met die Gees gevul beskryf word. Kreatiwiteit en vakmanskap is gawes van die Gees, wat in aanbidding aan God teruggegee word.

Toe dit voltooi was, ‘het die heerlikheid van die Here die tabernakel gevul.’ Die boek Eksodus begin met Israel in slawerny, besig om stede vir Farao te bou. Dit eindig met Israel vry, besig om ’n woonplek vir God te bou, en God wat dit met sy heerlikheid vul. Dit is die vorm van verlossing: van slawerny na aanbidding.

Dan neem die Nuwe Testament die storie verder. ‘Die Woord het mens geword en onder ons kom woon. Ons het sy heerlikheid gesien.’ Johannes gebruik die Griekse woord vir ‘getabernakel’. Jesus is die ware ontmoetingsplek van God en die mensdom. By sy dood het die gordyn geskeur, en die Allerheiligste oopgemaak. En nou is gelowiges ‘’n tempel van die Heilige Gees’. Die God wat eens in ’n tent gewoon het, woon nou in sy mense.
Dit verander hoe ons na ons liggame, ons gemeenskap en ons aanbidding kyk. Jy is waar God woon.

verse.text: Die Woord het mens geword en onder ons kom woon. Ons het sy heerlikheid gesien.

lessons: Die tabernakel wys hoe ’n heilige God tussen sondige mense kan woon.
Eksodus beweeg van slawerny na aanbidding, en verlossing ook.
Jesus is die ware tabernakel, en die Gees maak gelowiges nou God se tempel.
questions: Wat het die uitleg van die tabernakel oor God se nabyheid en heiligheid geleer?
Hoekom is dit betekenisvol dat die eerste persoon wat met die Gees gevul is, ’n vakman was?
Hoe behoort die wete dat jy ’n ‘tempel van die Heilige Gees’ is, jou daaglikse lewe te beïnvloed?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Sit stil en herinner jouself: ‘God woon in my.’ Vra Hom: ‘Hoe wil U hierdie tempel met u heerlikheid vul?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie dat U in Jesus by ons kom woon het.
Dankie dat u Gees in my woon.
Vul my met u heerlikheid, en help my om U met my liggaam en my gawes te eer.

mission.text: Gebruik hierdie week ’n kreatiewe gawe (kuns, musiek, bou, skryf of kook) as ’n daad van aanbidding aan God.

af.journal: Volg God se woonplek deur die Bybel: Eden, tabernakel, tempel, Jesus, gelowiges, nuwe skepping. Skryf een sin oor elkeen.

en.title: God’s Special Tent
story: God said, ‘Make me a special tent.’
Everyone helped! They brought gold, cloth and wood.
When the tent was finished, God’s cloud filled it!
God wanted to live close to His people.

af.title: God se Spesiale Tent
story: God het gesê: ‘Maak vir My ’n spesiale tent.’
Almal het gehelp! Hulle het goud, materiaal en hout gebring.
Toe die tent klaar was, het God se wolk dit gevul!
God wou naby sy mense woon.
God wil ook naby my wees!

verse.text: Ek sal tussen hulle woon.

af.action: Maak ’n tent met ’n kombers, sit binne-in en fluister: ‘God is naby my.’
lessons: God wil naby my wees.
questions: Kan jy ’n tentjie bou?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U naby my is. Amen.

en.title: A Tent Where God Lived
story: At Mount Sinai, God gave Moses wonderful instructions. ‘Have the people make a sanctuary for me,’ God said, ‘and I will live among them.’
A sanctuary is a holy place. Because God’s people were travelling, it would be a special tent called the tabernacle, which they could take down and carry with them.

Moses told the people, and they were so excited that everyone wanted to help! They brought gold and silver, blue and purple cloth, soft goat hair, wood and sweet-smelling oil. Some were good at sewing, some at carving and some at making things from gold. They brought so much that Moses had to say, ‘Stop! We have more than enough!’
When the tabernacle was finished, something amazing happened. A cloud covered the tent, and the glory of the Lord filled it! God’s presence was right there, in the middle of His people’s camp.

From then on, whenever the cloud lifted from the tabernacle, the people packed up and followed it. When the cloud stayed, they stayed. At night the cloud glowed like fire. God was leading them and living with them!
God wanted to be close to His people. Later, God came even closer: Jesus came to live among us. And now, the Holy Spirit lives in everyone who loves Jesus. God is never far away.

verse.text: Have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will live among them.

lessons: God wants to live among His people.
I can give my gifts and talents to God with joy.
God leads me and stays close to me.
questions: How did the people help to build the tabernacle?
How is God close to you today?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you want to be close to me.
Thank you that your Holy Spirit lives in me.
I give you my gifts with joy. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, use one of your talents (drawing, singing, helping) as a gift to God.

af.title: ’n Tent waar God Gewoon het
story: By die berg Sinai het God vir Moses wonderlike opdragte gegee. ‘Laat die mense vir My ’n heiligdom maak,’ het God gesê, ‘en Ek sal tussen hulle woon.’
’n Heiligdom is ’n heilige plek. Omdat God se mense op reis was, sou dit ’n spesiale tent wees wat die tabernakel genoem word, wat hulle kon afbreek en saamdra.

Moses het die mense vertel, en hulle was so opgewonde dat almal wou help! Hulle het goud en silwer gebring, blou en pers materiaal, sagte bokhaar, hout en olie wat lekker ruik. Party was goed met naaldwerk, party met houtsneewerk en party met dinge van goud maak. Hulle het so baie gebring dat Moses moes sê: ‘Stop! Ons het meer as genoeg!’

Toe die tabernakel klaar was, het iets wonderliks gebeur. ’n Wolk het die tent bedek, en die heerlikheid van die Here het dit gevul! God se teenwoordigheid was net daar, in die middel van sy mense se kamp.

Van toe af, elke keer as die wolk van die tabernakel af opgelig het, het die mense opgepak en dit gevolg. As die wolk bly, het hulle gebly. Snags het die wolk soos vuur gegloei. God het hulle gelei en by hulle gewoon!
God wou naby sy mense wees. Later het God nog nader gekom: Jesus het gekom om onder ons te woon. En nou woon die Heilige Gees in almal wat Jesus liefhet. God is nooit ver weg nie.

verse.text: Laat hulle vir My ’n heiligdom maak, en Ek sal tussen hulle woon.

lessons: God wil tussen sy mense woon.
Ek kan my gawes en talente met vreugde aan God gee.
God lei my en bly naby my.
questions: Hoe het die mense gehelp om die tabernakel te bou?
Hoe is God vandag naby jou?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U naby my wil wees.
Dankie dat u Heilige Gees in my woon.
Ek gee U my gawes met vreugde. Amen.

mission.text: Gebruik môre een van jou talente (teken, sing, help) as ’n geskenk aan God.

en.title: Face to Face, as a Friend
story: Something terrible had happened. While Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving God’s law, the people had made a golden calf and worshipped it. God was so grieved that He said He would send an angel to lead them, but He Himself would not go with them.

Moses had a tent of meeting outside the camp. When he went in, the pillar of cloud came down to the entrance, and ‘the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.’ Young Joshua ‘did not leave the tent’. He wanted to stay in God’s presence.

There Moses pleaded with God: ‘If your Presence does not go with us, do not send us up from here. How will anyone know that you are pleased with me and with your people unless you go with us?’ Moses knew that the promised land without God would be worthless. God’s presence was what made them different.
God answered: ‘My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest… I will do the very thing you have asked, because I am pleased with you and I know you by name.’

Then Moses made the boldest request of all: ‘Now show me your glory.’ God replied that no one could see His face and live, but He would hide Moses in a cleft of the rock, cover him with His hand and let him see His back as He passed by.

As God passed, He proclaimed His name: ‘The Lord, the Lord, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness, maintaining love to thousands, and forgiving wickedness.’ That’s who God is! Moses bowed to the ground and worshipped.

When Moses came down the mountain, his face was radiant because he had spoken with the Lord. Time with God changes us. Paul says that as we look to the Lord, we ‘are being transformed into His image with ever-increasing glory’.

verse.text: My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.

lessons: God’s presence is what makes His people different.
God is compassionate, gracious, slow to anger and full of love.
Time in God’s presence changes us.
questions: Why did Moses refuse to go on without God’s presence?
What did God say about Himself when He passed by Moses?
What can you learn from Joshua, who stayed in the tent?
en.listen: Be still, like Joshua in the tent of meeting. Ask God: ‘What do you want me to know about who you are?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, I don’t want to go anywhere without your presence.
Thank you that you are compassionate, gracious and full of love.
Change me as I spend time with you.
