af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy was die rooi tou ’n goeie teken vir redding? Waaraan herinner rooi jou in die Paasstorie?
af.journal: Teken Ragab se huis in die stadsmuur met ’n rooi tou in die venster. Skryf: ‘God red die wat Hom vertrou.’

trait.en: I remember what God has done
trait.af: Ek onthou wat God gedoen het

en.title: What Do These Stones Mean?
story: Forty years earlier, God had parted the Red Sea for their parents. Now a new generation stood at the Jordan River, which was in flood because it was harvest season. Between them and the promised land lay a deep, fast-flowing barrier.

God told Joshua, ‘Today I will begin to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.’ The priests carrying the ark of the covenant were to go first and step into the river.

Imagine being one of those priests. You can see the rushing water. God has promised it will stop, but nothing happens until your feet actually touch the edge. Faith sometimes means stepping into the water before you see the miracle.

‘As soon as the priests who carried the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water’s edge, the water from upstream stopped flowing.’ It piled up in a heap far away at a town called Adam. The priests stood on dry ground in the middle of the riverbed while the whole nation crossed over.

Then God gave an instruction: choose twelve men, one from each tribe, to take twelve stones from the middle of the river where the priests stood. They set them up at Gilgal, their first camp in the promised land.

Joshua explained why: ‘In the future, when your descendants ask their parents, “What do these stones mean?” tell them, “Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.”’ And the stones had a purpose for the whole world: ‘so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the Lord is powerful and so that you might always fear the Lord your God.’
We forget easily. That’s why God gives us ways to remember: stories, celebrations, Communion and journals. What are your ‘remembering stones’?

verse.text: He did this so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the Lord is powerful.

lessons: Sometimes faith steps into the water before seeing the miracle.
God wants us to remember what He has done.
Our stories of God’s faithfulness can help others know Him.
questions: When did the water stop? What does that teach about faith?
Why did God want the people to set up stones?
What are some of your family’s ‘remembering stones’?
en.listen: Be still and remember a time God helped you. Ask Him: ‘What do you want me to remember about you?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you for all the wonderful things you have done for me, like…
Help me to remember your faithfulness when I face new rivers.
Help me tell others what you have done.

mission.text: This week, tell someone (a friend or family member) a story of something God has done in your life.

en.journal: Draw twelve stones. On each one, write something God has done for you or your family that you never want to forget.

af.title: Wat Beteken Hierdie Klippe?
story: Veertig jaar tevore het God die Rietsee vir hulle ouers oopgemaak. Nou het ’n nuwe geslag by die Jordaanrivier gestaan, wat in vloed was omdat dit oestyd was. Tussen hulle en die beloofde land was ’n diep, vinnigvloeiende versperring.

God het vir Josua gesê: ‘Vandag sal Ek begin om jou in die oë van die hele Israel groot te maak, sodat hulle kan weet dat Ek by jou is soos Ek by Moses was.’ Die priesters wat die verbondsark dra, moes eerste gaan en in die rivier instap.

Stel jou voor jy is een van daardie priesters. Jy kan die bruisende water sien. God het belowe dit sal stop, maar niks gebeur totdat jou voete werklik aan die rand raak nie. Geloof beteken soms om in die water in te stap voordat jy die wonderwerk sien.

‘Sodra die priesters wat die ark dra, by die Jordaan aankom en hulle voete aan die rand van die water raak, het die water van bo af opgehou vloei.’ Dit het ver weg by ’n dorp met die naam Adam in ’n hoop opgedam. Die priesters het op droë grond in die middel van die rivierbedding gestaan terwyl die hele volk oorgegaan het.

Toe het God ’n opdrag gegee: kies twaalf mans, een uit elke stam, om twaalf klippe uit die middel van die rivier te vat waar die priesters gestaan het. Hulle het dit by Gilgal opgerig, hulle eerste kamp in die beloofde land.

Josua het verduidelik hoekom: ‘As julle nakomelinge in die toekoms vir hulle ouers vra: “Wat beteken hierdie klippe?” vertel hulle: “Israel het die Jordaan op droë grond oorgesteek.”’ En die klippe het ’n doel vir die hele wêreld gehad: ‘sodat al die volke van die aarde kan weet dat die hand van die Here kragtig is en sodat julle altyd die Here julle God kan vrees.’
Ons vergeet maklik. Dit is hoekom God ons maniere gee om te onthou: stories, feeste, Nagmaal en joernale. Wat is jou ‘onthou-klippe’?

verse.text: Hy het dit gedoen sodat al die volke van die aarde kan weet dat die hand van die Here kragtig is.

lessons: Soms stap geloof in die water in voordat dit die wonderwerk sien.
God wil hê ons moet onthou wat Hy gedoen het.
Ons stories van God se trou kan ander help om Hom te ken.
questions: Wanneer het die water gestop? Wat leer dit oor geloof?
Hoekom wou God hê die mense moet klippe oprig?
Wat is van jou familie se ‘onthou-klippe’?
af.listen: Wees stil en onthou ’n keer toe God jou gehelp het. Vra Hom: ‘Wat wil U hê moet ek van U onthou?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie vir al die wonderlike dinge wat U vir my gedoen het, soos…
Help my om u trou te onthou as ek voor nuwe riviere staan.
Help my om ander te vertel wat U gedoen het.

mission.text: Vertel hierdie week vir iemand (’n vriend of familielid) ’n storie van iets wat God in jou lewe gedoen het.

af.journal: Teken twaalf klippe. Skryf op elkeen iets wat God vir jou of jou familie gedoen het wat jy nooit wil vergeet nie.

en.title: Stepping In and Looking Back
story: The crossing of the Jordan deliberately echoes the crossing of the Red Sea. A new generation, under a new leader, needed to experience for themselves that the God of their parents was their God too. Faith can be passed on, but each generation must encounter God personally.

The order of events matters. The people were told to ‘consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do amazing things among you.’ Preparation of the heart came before the miracle. Then the ark, the symbol of God’s presence, went first, about a kilometre ahead of the people. God led the way into the unknown.

Notice the timing of the miracle: the water stopped only when the priests’ feet touched it. Earlier, at the Red Sea, God parted the waters before anyone stepped in. Here, the priests had to step into a flooded river trusting that God would act. As we mature in faith, God often asks us to take steps of obedience before we see the outcome.
The priests then stood in the middle of the riverbed, holding the ark, until everyone had crossed. Leaders who are faithful stand in the place of risk so that others can pass through.

The memorial stones serve two audiences. Inwardly, they were for Israel’s children: a prompt for parents to tell the story. Outwardly, they were for the nations: ‘so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the Lord is powerful.’ Memory isn’t only private; it is a form of testimony.

Scripture is full of remembering. The psalmist, in a dark season, wrote, ‘I will remember the deeds of the Lord; yes, I will remember your miracles of long ago.’ Jesus said at the Last Supper, ‘Do this in remembrance of me.’ When present circumstances look overwhelming, looking back at God’s faithfulness gives courage to step forward.
A wise habit is to build your own ‘stones’: keep a record of answered prayers and God’s faithfulness. One day someone will ask, ‘What do these stones mean?’ and you will have a story to tell.

verse.text: I will remember the deeds of the Lord; yes, I will remember your miracles of long ago.

lessons: Each generation needs to encounter God personally.
Mature faith often steps forward before seeing the outcome.
Remembering God’s faithfulness strengthens us and becomes testimony to others.
questions: Why might God have stopped the water only when the priests stepped in, unlike at the Red Sea?
What two audiences were the memorial stones for?
What practices could help you remember God’s faithfulness?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What step of faith are you asking me to take before I see the outcome?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you have been faithful through every generation, and you are my God too.
Help me step into… trusting you to act.
I will remember your deeds, especially…

mission.text: Start a ‘stones journal’ this week: record answered prayers and moments of God’s faithfulness.

en.journal: Interview a parent or grandparent about a time God was faithful in their life. Write their story down as a ‘remembering stone’ for your family.

af.title: Instap en Terugkyk
story: Die oorsteek van die Jordaan eggo doelbewus die oorsteek van die Rietsee. ’n Nuwe geslag, onder ’n nuwe leier, moes self ervaar dat die God van hulle ouers ook hulle God was. Geloof kan oorgedra word, maar elke geslag moet God persoonlik ontmoet.

Die volgorde van gebeure is belangrik. Die mense is gesê om ‘julle te heilig, want môre sal die Here wonderlike dinge onder julle doen.’ Voorbereiding van die hart het voor die wonderwerk gekom. Toe het die ark, die simbool van God se teenwoordigheid, eerste gegaan, omtrent ’n kilometer voor die mense. God het die pad die onbekende in gelei.

Let op die tydsberekening van die wonderwerk: die water het eers gestop toe die priesters se voete daaraan raak. Vroeër, by die Rietsee, het God die water oopgemaak voordat iemand ingestap het. Hier moes die priesters in ’n rivier in vloed instap en vertrou dat God sou optree. Soos ons in geloof groei, vra God ons dikwels om treë van gehoorsaamheid te neem voordat ons die uitkoms sien.
Die priesters het toe in die middel van die rivierbedding gestaan, met die ark, totdat almal oorgegaan het. Leiers wat getrou is, staan op die plek van gevaar sodat ander kan deurgaan.

Die gedenkklippe dien twee gehore. Na binne was hulle vir Israel se kinders: ’n aansporing vir ouers om die storie te vertel. Na buite was hulle vir die nasies: ‘sodat al die volke van die aarde kan weet dat die hand van die Here kragtig is.’ Herinnering is nie net privaat nie; dit is ’n vorm van getuienis.

Die Skrif is vol herinnering. Die psalmdigter het in ’n donker seisoen geskryf: ‘Ek sal die dade van die Here onthou; ja, ek sal u wonders van lank gelede onthou.’ Jesus het by die Laaste Avondmaal gesê: ‘Doen dit tot my gedagtenis.’ Wanneer huidige omstandighede oorweldigend lyk, gee dit moed om terug te kyk na God se trou om vorentoe te tree.
’n Wyse gewoonte is om jou eie ‘klippe’ te bou: hou rekord van beantwoorde gebede en God se trou. Eendag sal iemand vra: ‘Wat beteken hierdie klippe?’ en jy sal ’n storie hê om te vertel.

verse.text: Ek sal die dade van die Here onthou; ja, ek sal u wonders van lank gelede onthou.

lessons: Elke geslag moet God persoonlik ontmoet.
Volwasse geloof tree dikwels vorentoe voordat dit die uitkoms sien.
Om God se trou te onthou, versterk ons en word getuienis vir ander.
questions: Hoekom het God dalk die water eers gestop toe die priesters instap, anders as by die Rietsee?
Vir watter twee gehore was die gedenkklippe?
Watter gewoontes kan jou help om God se trou te onthou?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Watter tree van geloof vra U my om te neem voordat ek die uitkoms sien?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U was getrou deur elke geslag, en U is ook my God.
Help my om in… in te stap en U te vertrou om op te tree.
Ek sal u dade onthou, veral…

mission.text: Begin hierdie week ’n ‘klippejoernaal’: teken beantwoorde gebede en oomblikke van God se trou aan.

af.journal: Voer ’n onderhoud met ’n ouer of grootouer oor ’n keer toe God in hulle lewe getrou was. Skryf hulle storie neer as ’n ‘onthou-klip’ vir jou familie.

en.title: Remember Stones
story: God’s people came to a big, wide river.
When the priests stepped in, the water stopped! Whoa!
Everyone walked across on dry ground.
They picked up twelve stones to remember.
I remember what God has done for me!

verse.text: Remember the wonderful things God has done.

en.action: Collect a few small stones or toys in a pile and say: ‘I remember what God did!’
lessons: I remember what God has done.
questions: Can you count twelve stones?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for all the good things you do. Amen.

af.title: Onthou-Klippe
story: God se volk het by ’n groot, breë rivier gekom.
Toe die priesters instap, het die water gestop! Sjoe!
Almal het op droë grond oorgeloop.
Hulle het twaalf klippe opgetel om te onthou.
Ek onthou wat God vir my gedoen het!

verse.text: Onthou die wonderlike dinge wat God gedoen het.

af.action: Maak ’n paar klein klippies of speelgoed op ’n hopie bymekaar en sê: ‘Ek onthou wat God gedoen het!’
lessons: Ek onthou wat God gedoen het.
questions: Kan jy twaalf klippe tel?
prayer: Dankie, God,
vir al die goeie dinge wat U doen. Amen.

en.title: Twelve Stones from the River
story: God’s people stood at the edge of the Jordan River. On the other side was the promised land! But it was harvest time, and the river was flooding. The water was wide and deep and fast. How could thousands of people, with babies and grandparents and animals, get across?
God told Joshua, ‘Tell the priests carrying the ark of the covenant to step into the river.’ The ark was the special golden box that showed God was with His people.

So the priests lifted the ark onto their shoulders and walked towards the rushing water. As soon as their feet touched the edge of the river, the water stopped flowing! It piled up in a heap far upstream, and the riverbed became dry ground.
The priests stood in the middle of the river, and everyone walked across on dry ground: mums and dads, children, grandparents and all the animals.
Then God told Joshua, ‘Choose twelve men, one from each tribe. Each one must take a big stone from the middle of the river.’ They carried the stones to their camp and piled them up.
Joshua said, ‘In the future, when your children ask, “What do these stones mean?”, tell them how God stopped the river so we could cross.’
God wants us to remember the wonderful things He has done, and to tell our children and friends about them.

verse.text: Remember the wonderful things He has done.

lessons: I remember what God has done.
God makes a way where there seems to be no way.
I can tell others about the good things God has done.
questions: What happened when the priests’ feet touched the water?
What is something good God has done for your family that you want to remember?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for all the wonderful things you have done.
Help me always to remember,
and to tell others about you. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, ask a grown-up in your family to tell you about a time God helped them.

af.title: Twaalf Klippe uit die Rivier
story: God se volk het op die oewer van die Jordaanrivier gestaan. Aan die ander kant was die beloofde land! Maar dit was oestyd, en die rivier was in vloed. Die water was breed en diep en vinnig. Hoe kon duisende mense, met babas en oupas en oumas en diere, oorkom?
God het vir Josua gesê: ‘Sê vir die priesters wat die verbondsark dra om in die rivier in te stap.’ Die ark was die spesiale goue kis wat gewys het dat God by sy volk is.

Toe het die priesters die ark op hulle skouers gelig en na die bruisende water geloop. Sodra hulle voete aan die rand van die rivier raak, het die water opgehou vloei! Dit het ver bo in ’n hoop opgedam, en die rivierbedding het droë grond geword.
Die priesters het in die middel van die rivier gestaan, en almal het op droë grond oorgeloop: mammas en pappas, kinders, oupas en oumas en al die diere.
Toe het God vir Josua gesê: ‘Kies twaalf mans, een uit elke stam. Elkeen moet ’n groot klip uit die middel van die rivier vat.’ Hulle het die klippe na hulle kamp gedra en dit opgestapel.
Josua het gesê: ‘As julle kinders in die toekoms vra: “Wat beteken hierdie klippe?”, vertel hulle hoe God die rivier gestop het sodat ons kon oorgaan.’
God wil hê ons moet die wonderlike dinge onthou wat Hy gedoen het, en ons kinders en vriende daarvan vertel.

verse.text: Onthou die wonderlike dinge wat Hy gedoen het.

lessons: Ek onthou wat God gedoen het.
God maak ’n pad waar daar geen pad lyk nie.
Ek kan ander vertel van die goeie dinge wat God gedoen het.
questions: Wat het gebeur toe die priesters se voete aan die water raak?
Wat is iets goeds wat God vir jou familie gedoen het wat jy wil onthou?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir al die wonderlike dinge wat U gedoen het.
Help my om altyd te onthou,
en ander van U te vertel. Amen.

mission.text: Vra môre ’n grootmens in jou familie om jou te vertel van ’n keer toe God hulle gehelp het.

af.fact: Josua het ook twaalf klippe in die middel van die rivier opgerig, waar die priesters gestaan het. Die Bybel sê hulle was nog daar ‘tot vandag toe’, toe die boek Josua geskryf is!
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy wou God hê die mense moet iets maak wat hulle kon sien om hulle te help onthou?
af.journal: Maak jou eie ‘onthou-klippe’: skryf op klein klippies of papiersirkels op elkeen een ding wat God vir jou gedoen het.

trait.en: I choose to serve the Lord
trait.af: Ek kies om die Here te dien

en.title: Choose for Yourselves
story: Joshua was about 110 years old, and he knew his life was nearly over. He gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem, where Abraham had first built an altar in the land centuries before.

First, Joshua retold the story, but he told it as God speaking: ‘I took your father Abraham… I gave him Isaac… I sent Moses and Aaron… I brought you out of Egypt… I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities you did not build.’ Over and over: ‘I… I… I.’ Everything they had was God’s gift.

Then came the challenge: ‘Now fear the Lord and serve Him with all faithfulness. Throw away the gods your ancestors worshipped… and serve the Lord.’ Some families were still secretly keeping little idols. Joshua knew that a half-hearted faith wouldn’t survive.
Then he spoke the famous words: ‘But if serving the Lord seems undesirable to you, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve… But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.’

The people answered enthusiastically: ‘Far be it from us to forsake the Lord!’ But Joshua pushed them to think seriously: ‘You are not able to serve the Lord. He is a holy God.’ He wanted them to understand this was a serious commitment, not just an emotional moment. They insisted, ‘No! We will serve the Lord.’
Joshua wrote their promise in the Book of the Law and set up a large stone under an oak tree as a witness.
Nobody can make this choice for you. Your parents can show you the way, but you must choose for yourself. And it isn’t a one-time decision; it is a choice we make again ‘this day’, every day.

verse.text: Choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve… But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.

lessons: Everything we have is a gift from God.
Following God is a personal choice that no one can make for us.
Serving God is a daily, wholehearted commitment.
questions: Why did Joshua retell everything God had done before asking the people to choose?
What ‘idols’ might people hold on to today?
What does choosing God ‘this day’ look like for you?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there anything in my life competing with you for first place?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, everything I have is a gift from you.
Today I choose to serve you with all my heart.
Help me to let go of anything that competes with you, like…

mission.text: This week, talk with your family about what it means for your household to serve the Lord, and choose one way to do it together.

en.journal: Write your own ‘Joshua 24:15’ commitment in your own words, and sign it.

af.title: Kies vir Julleself
story: Josua was omtrent 110 jaar oud, en hy het geweet sy lewe was amper verby. Hy het al die stamme van Israel by Sigem bymekaargemaak, waar Abraham eeue tevore die eerste altaar in die land gebou het.

Eers het Josua die storie oorvertel, maar hy het dit vertel asof God praat: ‘Ek het julle vader Abraham geneem… Ek het hom Isak gegee… Ek het Moses en Aäron gestuur… Ek het julle uit Egipte gebring… Ek het julle ’n land gegee waarvoor julle nie gewerk het nie, en stede wat julle nie gebou het nie.’ Oor en oor: ‘Ek… Ek… Ek.’ Alles wat hulle gehad het, was God se geskenk.

Toe kom die uitdaging: ‘Vrees nou die Here en dien Hom met volle trou. Gooi die gode weg wat julle voorvaders aanbid het… en dien die Here.’ Party families het nog in die geheim klein afgode gehou. Josua het geweet dat ’n halfhartige geloof nie sou oorleef nie.
Toe het hy die bekende woorde gespreek: ‘Maar as dit vir julle onaanvaarbaar is om die Here te dien, kies dan vandag vir julleself wie julle wil dien… Maar ek en my huis, ons sal die Here dien.’

Die mense het geesdriftig geantwoord: ‘Ver sy dit van ons om die Here te verlaat!’ Maar Josua het hulle gedwing om ernstig te dink: ‘Julle kan nie die Here dien nie. Hy is ’n heilige God.’ Hy wou hê hulle moet verstaan dit is ’n ernstige verbintenis, nie net ’n emosionele oomblik nie. Hulle het volgehou: ‘Nee! Ons sal die Here dien.’
Josua het hulle belofte in die Boek van die Wet geskryf en ’n groot klip onder ’n eikeboom as getuie opgerig.
Niemand kan hierdie keuse vir jou maak nie. Jou ouers kan jou die pad wys, maar jy moet self kies. En dit is nie ’n eenmalige besluit nie; dit is ’n keuse wat ons ‘vandag’ weer maak, elke dag.

verse.text: Kies vandag vir julleself wie julle wil dien… Maar ek en my huis, ons sal die Here dien.

lessons: Alles wat ons het, is ’n geskenk van God.
Om God te volg, is ’n persoonlike keuse wat niemand vir ons kan maak nie.
Om God te dien, is ’n daaglikse, volhartige verbintenis.
questions: Hoekom het Josua alles oorvertel wat God gedoen het voordat hy die mense gevra het om te kies?
Aan watter ‘afgode’ hou mense vandag dalk vas?
Hoe lyk dit vir jou om God ‘vandag’ te kies?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar iets in my lewe wat met U meeding vir die eerste plek?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, alles wat ek het, is ’n geskenk van U.
Vandag kies ek om U met my hele hart te dien.
Help my om enigiets te los wat met U meeding, soos…

mission.text: Gesels hierdie week met jou familie oor wat dit beteken dat julle huis die Here dien, en kies een manier om dit saam te doen.

af.journal: Skryf jou eie ‘Josua 24:15’-verbintenis in jou eie woorde, en teken dit.

en.title: A Faith of Your Own
story: Joshua 24 is a covenant renewal ceremony, and it follows the pattern of ancient treaties between kings and their people: an introduction of the king, a history of what the king has done, the obligations of the people, a written record and witnesses. Joshua presents God as the great King who has acted graciously, and calls Israel to respond with loyalty.

Notice the history section. In verses 2–13, God speaks in the first person seventeen times: ‘I took… I gave… I sent… I brought… I handed… I gave you a land.’ The emphasis is entirely on grace. Israel’s obedience is meant to be a response to what God has already done, not a way of earning His favour. This is the pattern throughout Scripture: grace first, then obedience flowing from gratitude and love.

Joshua’s call is uncompromising: ‘Throw away the gods your ancestors worshipped beyond the Euphrates River and in Egypt.’ Even after all God had done, some Israelites still kept household idols, a kind of spiritual insurance policy. Joshua demands exclusive loyalty. You can’t serve the Lord and keep a backup god.

Then the famous choice: ‘Choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve.’ Joshua even offers them the options: the gods of their ancestors or the gods of the Amorites. And he declares his own decision publicly: ‘As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.’ Leadership begins with personal example.

Joshua’s strange response to their eager commitment, ‘You are not able to serve the Lord’, is a warning against shallow enthusiasm. He wants them to count the cost. The New Testament gives the answer to Joshua’s concern: we aren’t able, in our own strength, but the Holy Spirit makes us able.

The sad footnote comes in Judges 2: ‘After that whole generation had been gathered to their ancestors, another generation grew up who knew neither the Lord nor what He had done for Israel.’ Within a generation, the faith had faded. Inherited faith that is never made personal doesn’t last.
This is your generation’s question. Will your faith be just your parents’ faith, or will you choose for yourself this day?

verse.text: Another generation grew up who knew neither the Lord nor what He had done for Israel.

lessons: Obedience is a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn it.
God calls for exclusive loyalty; there is no room for ‘backup gods’.
Faith must become personal in each generation, or it fades.
questions: Why does God speak in the first person so many times in Joshua 24:2–13?
What are some ‘backup gods’ people trust in today?
What would it look like for your faith to become truly your own?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is my faith my own, or am I just borrowing someone else’s?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you for your grace that came first.
I choose for myself this day to serve you, and I let go of my ‘backup gods’, like…
Make my faith my own, so that it lasts.

mission.text: This week, write down three reasons you personally believe in Jesus, not just because others do.

en.journal: Write about Judges 2:10. What could your generation do so that this doesn’t happen again?

af.title: ’n Geloof van Jou Eie
story: Josua 24 is ’n seremonie van verbondsvernuwing, en dit volg die patroon van antieke verdrae tussen konings en hulle volk: ’n voorstelling van die koning, ’n geskiedenis van wat die koning gedoen het, die verpligtinge van die volk, ’n geskrewe rekord en getuies. Josua stel God voor as die groot Koning wat genadig opgetree het, en roep Israel op om met lojaliteit te reageer.

Let op die geskiedenisgedeelte. In verse 2–13 praat God sewentien keer in die eerste persoon: ‘Ek het geneem… Ek het gegee… Ek het gestuur… Ek het uitgebring… Ek het oorgegee… Ek het julle ’n land gegee.’ Die klem is heeltemal op genade. Israel se gehoorsaamheid is bedoel as ’n reaksie op wat God reeds gedoen het, nie as ’n manier om sy guns te verdien nie. Dit is die patroon deur die hele Skrif: eers genade, dan gehoorsaamheid wat uit dankbaarheid en liefde vloei.

Josua se oproep is kompromisloos: ‘Gooi die gode weg wat julle voorvaders oorkant die Eufraatrivier en in Egipte aanbid het.’ Selfs ná alles wat God gedoen het, het party Israeliete nog huisgode gehou, ’n soort geestelike versekeringspolis. Josua eis volkome lojaliteit. Jy kan nie die Here dien en ’n rugsteun-god hou nie.

Dan die bekende keuse: ‘Kies vandag vir julleself wie julle wil dien.’ Josua bied hulle selfs die opsies: die gode van hulle voorvaders of die gode van die Amoriete. En hy verklaar sy eie besluit in die openbaar: ‘Ek en my huis, ons sal die Here dien.’ Leierskap begin met persoonlike voorbeeld.

Josua se vreemde reaksie op hulle geesdriftige verbintenis, ‘Julle kan nie die Here dien nie’, is ’n waarskuwing teen oppervlakkige geesdrif. Hy wil hê hulle moet die koste bereken. Die Nuwe Testament gee die antwoord op Josua se kommer: ons kan nie, in ons eie krag nie, maar die Heilige Gees maak ons in staat.

Die hartseer voetnoot kom in Rigters 2: ‘Nadat daardie hele geslag by hulle voorvaders versamel is, het ’n ander geslag grootgeword wat die Here nie geken het nie en ook nie wat Hy vir Israel gedoen het nie.’ Binne een geslag het die geloof vervaag. Geërfde geloof wat nooit persoonlik gemaak word nie, hou nie.
Dit is jou geslag se vraag. Sal jou geloof net jou ouers se geloof wees, of sal jy vandag self kies?

verse.text: ’n Ander geslag het grootgeword wat die Here nie geken het nie en ook nie wat Hy vir Israel gedoen het nie.

lessons: Gehoorsaamheid is ’n reaksie op God se genade, nie ’n manier om dit te verdien nie.
God vra volkome lojaliteit; daar is geen plek vir ‘rugsteun-gode’ nie.
Geloof moet in elke geslag persoonlik word, of dit vervaag.
questions: Hoekom praat God so baie keer in die eerste persoon in Josua 24:2–13?
Wat is party ‘rugsteun-gode’ wat mense vandag vertrou?
Hoe sou dit lyk as jou geloof regtig jou eie word?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is my geloof my eie, of leen ek net iemand anders s’n?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie vir u genade wat eerste gekom het.
Vandag kies ek self om U te dien, en ek los my ‘rugsteun-gode’, soos…
Maak my geloof my eie, sodat dit hou.

mission.text: Skryf hierdie week drie redes neer hoekom jy persoonlik in Jesus glo, nie net omdat ander dit doen nie.

af.journal: Skryf oor Rigters 2:10. Wat kan jou geslag doen sodat dit nie weer gebeur nie?

en.title: We Choose God!
story: Joshua was very old now.
He called all God’s people together.
He said, ‘Choose today whom you will follow.’
Then he said, ‘Me and my family, we will follow the Lord!’
I choose God too!

verse.text: As for me and my family, we will serve the Lord.

en.action: Put your hand up high and say: ‘I choose God!’
lessons: I choose to follow God.
questions: Who is in your family?
prayer: Dear God,
I choose to follow you. Amen.

af.title: Ons Kies God!
story: Josua was nou baie oud.
Hy het al God se mense bymekaargeroep.
Hy het gesê: ‘Kies vandag wie julle gaan volg.’
Toe het hy gesê: ‘Ek en my familie, ons sal die Here volg!’
Ek kies ook God!

verse.text: Ek en my familie, ons sal die Here dien.

af.action: Steek jou hand hoog op en sê: ‘Ek kies God!’
lessons: Ek kies om God te volg.
questions: Wie is in jou familie?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek kies om U te volg. Amen.

en.title: Choose This Day
story: Many years had passed. God’s people were living in the promised land, in houses and towns, with fields and vineyards. Joshua had led them faithfully, but now he was very old.

Joshua called all the people together at a place called Shechem. He reminded them of everything God had done: how God called Abraham, rescued them from Egypt, led them through the desert, stopped the Jordan River and gave them the land.
Then Joshua said something very important. ‘Now love the Lord and serve Him with all your heart. Some of you still keep little idols, pretend gods that can’t see or hear or help. Throw them away!’
‘If you don’t want to serve the Lord, then choose today whom you will serve,’ Joshua said. ‘But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord!’
The people answered, ‘We will serve the Lord too! He is our God!’ Joshua wrote down their promise and set up a big stone under a tree to remind them.

Following God is a choice. Nobody can make it for you. Your mum and dad can’t choose for you. But you can choose today to love God and follow Him. And families can choose together: ‘We will serve the Lord!’

verse.text: As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.

lessons: Following God is my choice.
I can choose to love God with all my heart.
Families can choose to follow God together.
questions: What did Joshua remind the people about before he asked them to choose?
What does it mean for your family to ‘serve the Lord’?
prayer: Dear God,
I choose to love you and follow you.
Please help our whole family
to serve you together. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, think of one way your family can serve God together, and do it.

af.title: Kies Vandag
story: Baie jare het verbygegaan. God se volk het in die beloofde land gewoon, in huise en dorpe, met lande en wingerde. Josua het hulle getrou gelei, maar nou was hy baie oud.

Josua het al die mense by ’n plek met die naam Sigem bymekaargeroep. Hy het hulle herinner aan alles wat God gedoen het: hoe God Abraham geroep het, hulle uit Egipte gered het, hulle deur die woestyn gelei het, die Jordaanrivier gestop het en vir hulle die land gegee het.

Toe het Josua iets baie belangriks gesê. ‘Het nou die Here lief en dien Hom met julle hele hart. Party van julle hou nog klein afgode, speel-gode wat nie kan sien of hoor of help nie. Gooi hulle weg!’
‘As julle nie die Here wil dien nie, kies dan vandag wie julle wil dien,’ het Josua gesê. ‘Maar ek en my huis, ons sal die Here dien!’
Die mense het geantwoord: ‘Ons sal ook die Here dien! Hy is ons God!’ Josua het hulle belofte neergeskryf en ’n groot klip onder ’n boom opgerig om hulle te herinner.

Om God te volg, is ’n keuse. Niemand kan dit vir jou maak nie. Jou ma en pa kan nie vir jou kies nie. Maar jy kan vandag kies om God lief te hê en Hom te volg. En families kan saam kies: ‘Ons sal die Here dien!’

verse.text: Ek en my huis, ons sal die Here dien.

lessons: Om God te volg, is my keuse.
Ek kan kies om God met my hele hart lief te hê.
Families kan kies om God saam te volg.
questions: Waaraan het Josua die mense herinner voordat hy hulle gevra het om te kies?
Wat beteken dit vir jou familie om ‘die Here te dien’?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek kies om U lief te hê en U te volg.
Help asseblief ons hele familie
om U saam te dien. Amen.

mission.text: Dink môre aan een manier waarop jou familie God saam kan dien, en doen dit.

en.title: Choose This Day
story: Many years had passed. God’s people were living in the promised land, in houses and towns, with fields and vineyards. Joshua had led them faithfully, but now he was very old.

Joshua called all the people together at a place called Shechem. He reminded them of everything God had done: how God called Abraham, rescued them from Egypt, led them through the desert, stopped the Jordan River and gave them the land.
Then Joshua said something very important. ‘Now love the Lord and serve Him with all your heart. Some of you still keep little idols, pretend gods that can’t see or hear or help. Throw them away!’
‘If you don’t want to serve the Lord, then choose today whom you will serve,’ Joshua said. ‘But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord!’
The people answered, ‘We will serve the Lord too! He is our God!’ Joshua wrote down their promise and set up a big stone under a tree to remind them.

Following God is a choice. Nobody can make it for you. Your mum and dad can’t choose for you. But you can choose today to love God and follow Him. And families can choose together: ‘We will serve the Lord!’

verse.text: As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.

lessons: Following God is my choice.
I can choose to love God with all my heart.
Families can choose to follow God together.
questions: What did Joshua remind the people about before he asked them to choose?
What does it mean for your family to ‘serve the Lord’?
prayer: Dear God,
I choose to love you and follow you.
Please help our whole family
to serve you together. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, think of one way your family can serve God together, and do it.

en.fact: Shechem was the same place where God first appeared to Abraham when he arrived in the land, hundreds of years earlier. God’s story had come full circle!
en.deeper: Why do you think Joshua reminded the people of God’s goodness before asking them to choose?
en.journal: Make a sign for your home: ‘As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.’ Decorate it and hang it up.

trait.en: God gives true friends
trait.af: God gee ware vriende

en.title: A Friendship Sealed by God
story: After David defeated Goliath, he was brought to King Saul. Standing nearby was Saul’s son, Prince Jonathan, a brave warrior himself. ‘Jonathan became one in spirit with David, and he loved him as himself.’

Jonathan made a covenant with David, a binding promise of friendship before God. To seal it, he took off his royal robe and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow and his belt. In that culture, this was enormous. Jonathan was the heir to the throne. By giving David his royal robe and weapons, he was saying, ‘I recognise that God has chosen you. I will not fight you for the throne.’
Most people would have been jealous. Jonathan was happy to step aside, because he loved God and he loved his friend.

But King Saul grew bitterly jealous of David’s success and tried to kill him. David fled and asked Jonathan, ‘What have I done? Why is your father trying to take my life?’ Jonathan couldn’t believe it at first, but he promised to find out.

They arranged a secret signal. At the new moon feast, Jonathan would test his father. Then he would go to a field and shoot arrows. If he told his servant the arrows were near, David was safe. If he said, ‘The arrows are beyond you,’ David must flee.

At the feast, Saul exploded in anger, and even threw a spear at Jonathan for defending David. The next morning Jonathan went to the field and called out, ‘Isn’t the arrow beyond you? Hurry! Go quickly!’ When the boy had gone, David came out. They wept together. Jonathan said, ‘Go in peace, for we have sworn friendship with each other in the name of the Lord.’
True friendship is loyal, unselfish and rooted in God. It is happy for the other person’s success, and it stands by them in danger.

verse.text: A friend loves at all times.

lessons: True friends are happy for each other’s success, not jealous.
Loyal friendship stands by people in danger, even at a cost.
The best friendships are rooted in God.
questions: What did it mean when Jonathan gave David his royal robe and weapons?
Why do you think Jonathan wasn’t jealous of David?
How can you be a ‘Jonathan’ to someone?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘How can I be a better friend this week?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you for the gift of friends.
Help me not to be jealous, but to be happy when my friends do well.
Make me a loyal friend to…

mission.text: This week, celebrate a friend’s success genuinely, especially one you might be tempted to be jealous of.

en.journal: Make a list of qualities of a true friend from this story. Circle the ones you want to grow in.

af.title: ’n Vriendskap deur God Beseël
story: Nadat Dawid vir Goliat verslaan het, is hy na koning Saul gebring. Naby het Saul se seun gestaan, prins Jonatan, self ’n dapper krygsman. ‘Jonatan het een van gees met Dawid geword, en hy het hom liefgehad soos homself.’

Jonatan het ’n verbond met Dawid gesluit, ’n bindende belofte van vriendskap voor God. Om dit te beseël, het hy sy koninklike mantel uitgetrek en dit vir Dawid gegee, saam met sy tuniek, sy swaard, sy boog en sy belt. In daardie kultuur was dit enorm. Jonatan was die troonopvolger. Deur vir Dawid sy koninklike mantel en wapens te gee, het hy gesê: ‘Ek erken dat God jou gekies het. Ek sal nie met jou om die troon veg nie.’
Die meeste mense sou jaloers gewees het. Jonatan was bly om eenkant toe te staan, omdat hy God liefgehad het en sy vriend liefgehad het.

Maar koning Saul het bitter jaloers geword op Dawid se sukses en probeer om hom dood te maak. Dawid het gevlug en vir Jonatan gevra: ‘Wat het ek gedoen? Hoekom probeer jou pa my lewe neem?’ Jonatan kon dit eers nie glo nie, maar hy het belowe om uit te vind.

Hulle het ’n geheime teken gereël. By die nuwemaanfees sou Jonatan sy pa toets. Dan sou hy na ’n veld gaan en pyle skiet. As hy vir sy dienskneg sê die pyle is naby, was Dawid veilig. As hy sê: ‘Die pyle is verder as jy,’ moes Dawid vlug.

By die fees het Saul van woede ontplof, en selfs ’n spies na Jonatan gegooi omdat hy Dawid verdedig het. Die volgende oggend het Jonatan na die veld gegaan en geroep: ‘Is die pyl nie verder as jy nie? Maak gou! Gaan vinnig!’ Toe die seun weg is, het Dawid uitgekom. Hulle het saam gehuil. Jonatan het gesê: ‘Gaan in vrede, want ons het mekaar in die Naam van die Here vriendskap gesweer.’
Ware vriendskap is lojaal, onselfsugtig en in God gewortel. Dit is bly oor die ander persoon se sukses, en dit staan by hulle in gevaar.

verse.text: ’n Vriend het altyd lief.

lessons: Ware vriende is bly oor mekaar se sukses, nie jaloers nie.
Lojale vriendskap staan by mense in gevaar, selfs as dit iets kos.
Die beste vriendskappe is in God gewortel.
questions: Wat het dit beteken toe Jonatan vir Dawid sy koninklike mantel en wapens gegee het?
Hoekom dink jy was Jonatan nie jaloers op Dawid nie?
Hoe kan jy ’n ‘Jonatan’ vir iemand wees?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Hoe kan ek hierdie week ’n beter vriend wees?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie vir die geskenk van vriende.
Help my om nie jaloers te wees nie, maar bly te wees as my vriende goed doen.
Maak my ’n lojale vriend vir…

mission.text: Vier hierdie week opreg ’n vriend se sukses, veral een op wie jy dalk in die versoeking kom om jaloers te wees.

af.journal: Maak ’n lys van eienskappe van ’n ware vriend uit hierdie storie. Omkring die waarin jy wil groei.

en.title: The Friend Who Gave Up a Crown
story: Jonathan is one of the most admirable people in the Old Testament, yet he is often overlooked. He was a courageous warrior: in 1 Samuel 14 he and his armour-bearer climbed a cliff to attack a Philistine outpost, saying, ‘Nothing can hinder the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few.’ He was also Saul’s eldest son, the natural heir to the throne.

When David appeared, Jonathan faced a choice. David was clearly anointed by God, gifted, popular and destined to rule. Jonathan could have seen him as a rival. Instead, ‘Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.’ He gave David his robe, armour, sword, bow and belt, the symbols of his identity as crown prince. It was a deliberate act of surrender to God’s plan.
This reveals the secret of Jonathan’s character: his security was in God, not in his position. He didn’t need the crown to know who he was. That freedom allowed him to love David without envy.

His loyalty was costly. When Saul raged against David, Jonathan defended him, and Saul screamed insults at his own son and hurled a spear at him. Jonathan chose friendship and truth over his father’s approval and his own future.

In 1 Samuel 23, when David was hunted and discouraged in the wilderness, Jonathan found him ‘and helped him to find strength in God’. That is the highest form of friendship: not just making someone feel better, but pointing them to God. He told David, ‘Don’t be afraid… You will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you.’
Jonathan didn’t live to see that day. He died in battle beside his father. David’s lament for him is one of the most moving poems in the Bible: ‘I grieve for you, Jonathan my brother.’

Jonathan foreshadows Jesus, who ‘made Himself nothing’, laid aside His glory, and said, ‘Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.’ Jesus is the friend who gave up a crown for us.

verse.text: Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.

lessons: Security in God frees us to love without envy.
The highest friendship helps others ‘find strength in God’.
Jesus is the ultimate friend, who laid aside His glory for us.
questions: What made Jonathan able to give up the throne without bitterness?
What does it mean to help someone ‘find strength in God’?
How does Jonathan point forward to Jesus?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Who in my life needs me to help them find strength in you?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for being the friend who laid down your life for me.
Free me from envy by making me secure in you, especially about…
Help me to strengthen my friends in God.

mission.text: This week, encourage a discouraged friend by pointing them to a promise of God, not just with general encouragement.

en.journal: Write about envy and comparison. Where do you feel them most (school, sport, social media)? How could security in God change that?

af.title: Die Vriend wat ’n Kroon Prysgegee het
story: Jonatan is een van die mees bewonderenswaardige mense in die Ou Testament, tog word hy dikwels oor die hoof gesien. Hy was ’n dapper krygsman: in 1 Samuel 14 het hy en sy wapendraer teen ’n krans uitgeklim om ’n Filistynse buitepos aan te val, en gesê: ‘Niks kan die Here keer om te red nie, deur baie of deur min.’ Hy was ook Saul se oudste seun, die natuurlike troonopvolger.

Toe Dawid verskyn, het Jonatan voor ’n keuse gestaan. Dawid was duidelik deur God gesalf, begaafd, gewild en bestem om te regeer. Jonatan kon hom as ’n mededinger gesien het. In plaas daarvan ‘het Jonatan ’n verbond met Dawid gesluit omdat hy hom liefgehad het soos homself.’ Hy het vir Dawid sy mantel, wapenrusting, swaard, boog en belt gegee, die simbole van sy identiteit as kroonprins. Dit was ’n doelbewuste daad van oorgawe aan God se plan.

Dit wys die geheim van Jonatan se karakter: sy sekuriteit was in God, nie in sy posisie nie. Hy het nie die kroon nodig gehad om te weet wie hy is nie. Daardie vryheid het hom in staat gestel om Dawid sonder afguns lief te hê.

Sy lojaliteit het iets gekos. Toe Saul teen Dawid te kere gegaan het, het Jonatan hom verdedig, en Saul het beledigings na sy eie seun geskree en ’n spies na hom gegooi. Jonatan het vriendskap en waarheid gekies bo sy pa se goedkeuring en sy eie toekoms.

In 1 Samuel 23, toe Dawid gejag en moedeloos in die woestyn was, het Jonatan hom gaan soek ‘en hom gehelp om krag in God te vind’. Dit is die hoogste vorm van vriendskap: nie net om iemand beter te laat voel nie, maar om hulle na God te wys. Hy het vir Dawid gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie… Jy sal koning oor Israel wees, en ek sal tweede na jou wees.’

Jonatan het nie geleef om daardie dag te sien nie. Hy het langs sy pa in die geveg gesterf. Dawid se klaaglied oor hom is een van die mees roerende gedigte in die Bybel: ‘Ek treur oor jou, Jonatan my broer.’

Jonatan wys vooruit na Jesus, wat ‘Homself niks gemaak het nie’, sy heerlikheid eenkant gesit het, en gesê het: ‘Niemand het groter liefde as dit nie: dat iemand sy lewe vir sy vriende gee.’ Jesus is die vriend wat ’n kroon vir ons prysgegee het.

verse.text: Niemand het groter liefde as dit nie: dat iemand sy lewe vir sy vriende gee.

lessons: Sekuriteit in God maak ons vry om sonder afguns lief te hê.
Die hoogste vriendskap help ander om ‘krag in God te vind’.
Jesus is die grootste vriend, wat sy heerlikheid vir ons eenkant gesit het.
questions: Wat het Jonatan in staat gestel om die troon sonder bitterheid prys te gee?
Wat beteken dit om iemand te help om ‘krag in God te vind’?
Hoe wys Jonatan vooruit na Jesus?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Wie in my lewe het my nodig om hulle te help om krag in U te vind?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U die vriend is wat u lewe vir my gegee het.
Maak my vry van afguns deur my veilig in U te maak, veral oor…
Help my om my vriende in God te versterk.

mission.text: Bemoedig hierdie week ’n moedelose vriend deur hulle na ’n belofte van God te wys, nie net met algemene bemoediging nie.

af.journal: Skryf oor afguns en vergelyking. Waar voel jy dit die meeste (skool, sport, sosiale media)? Hoe kan sekuriteit in God dit verander?

en.title: Best Friends
story: David and Jonathan were best friends.
Jonathan gave David his coat, his sword and his bow.
When David was in danger, Jonathan helped him.
They promised to always be kind to each other.
God gives me friends!

verse.text: A friend loves at all times.

en.action: Give someone a big friendship hug!
lessons: God gives me friends.
questions: Who is your friend?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for my friends. Amen.

af.title: Beste Vriende
story: Dawid en Jonatan was beste vriende.
Jonatan het vir Dawid sy jas, sy swaard en sy boog gegee.
Toe Dawid in gevaar was, het Jonatan hom gehelp.
Hulle het belowe om altyd goed vir mekaar te wees.
God gee my vriende!

verse.text: ’n Vriend het altyd lief.

lessons: God gee my vriende.
questions: Wie is jou vriend?
prayer: Dankie, God,
vir my vriende. Amen.

en.title: Jonathan’s Arrows
story: After David beat the giant Goliath, King Saul’s son Jonathan became his best friend. Jonathan loved David like his own brother. To show it, he gave David his royal robe, his sword, his bow and his belt.
Jonathan was a prince. One day he might have been king. But God had chosen David to be the next king. Instead of being jealous, Jonathan was happy for his friend!
King Saul was not happy. He became jealous of David and wanted to hurt him. David was scared. ‘Jonathan, why does your father want to hurt me?’

Jonathan made a plan. ‘Hide in the field. I will find out what my father is planning. Then I will come and shoot three arrows. If I tell my servant boy, “The arrows are on this side,” you are safe. But if I say, “The arrows are beyond you,” you must run away.’
Jonathan found out that his father really did want to hurt David. So he went to the field and shot an arrow far beyond the boy. ‘Isn’t the arrow beyond you?’ he called. David knew he had to go.

When the boy had gone, David and Jonathan hugged and cried. ‘Go in peace,’ said Jonathan. ‘We have promised each other, in the name of the Lord, to be friends forever.’ A true friend is kind, loyal and happy for you, even when it costs them something.

verse.text: A friend loves at all times.

lessons: God gives true friends.
A true friend is happy for others, not jealous.
I can be a loyal friend, even when it’s hard.
questions: Why was it special that Jonathan wasn’t jealous of David?
How can you be a good friend like Jonathan?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for my friends.
Help me to be a true friend:
kind, loyal and never jealous. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, be happy for a friend when something good happens to them, and tell them.

lessons: God gee ware vriende.
’n Ware vriend is bly vir ander, nie jaloers nie.
Ek kan ’n lojale vriend wees, selfs as dit moeilik is.
questions: Hoekom was dit spesiaal dat Jonatan nie jaloers op Dawid was nie?
Hoe kan jy ’n goeie vriend wees soos Jonatan?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir my vriende.
Help my om ’n ware vriend te wees:
gaaf, lojaal en nooit jaloers nie. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre bly vir ’n vriend as iets goeds met hulle gebeur, en sê vir hulle.

en.journal: Draw a bow and three arrows. Write: ‘A friend loves at all times.’

prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir my vriende.
Help my om ’n ware vriend te wees:
gaaf, lojaal en nooit jaloers nie. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre bly vir ’n vriend as iets goeds met hulle gebeur, en sê vir hulle.

af.fact: Jonatan was ook ’n dapper soldaat. Eendag het hy en sy wapendraer teen ’n krans uitgeklim en ’n hele groep vyandige soldate verslaan, terwyl hulle God vertrou het om hulle te help!
af.deeper: Jonatan het vir Dawid sy koninklike goed gegee. Wat dink jy het dit beteken?
af.journal: Teken ’n boog en drie pyle. Skryf: ‘’n Vriend het altyd lief.’

trait.en: God helps me choose mercy, not revenge
trait.af: God help my om genade te kies, nie wraak nie

en.title: Mercy in the Cave
story: King Saul had become consumed with jealousy and was hunting David like a wild animal. He took three thousand of his best soldiers to search for David in the rocky desert near En Gedi.
Along the road were sheep pens and a large cave. Saul went into the cave alone to relieve himself. He had no idea that David and his men were hiding deep inside that very cave, in the darkness.

David’s men were excited. ‘This is the day the Lord spoke of when He said to you, “I will give your enemy into your hands for you to deal with as you wish.”’ It seemed like the perfect opportunity. After all, Saul was trying to kill David!

David crept up silently and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe. But then his conscience troubled him, even for that. He said to his men, ‘The Lord forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the Lord’s anointed.’ He refused to let them attack Saul.

When Saul had left the cave, David came out and called after him, ‘My lord the king!’ He bowed low and held up the corner of the robe. ‘See, my father, look at this piece of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe but did not kill you. Now understand that I am not guilty of wrongdoing… May the Lord judge between you and me… but my hand will not touch you.’
Saul wept aloud. ‘You are more righteous than I. You have treated me well, but I have treated you badly.’

David had every reason for revenge. But he trusted God to bring justice in His time. Paul later wrote, ‘Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath… Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.’

verse.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

lessons: God helps me choose mercy instead of revenge.
I can trust God to bring justice in His time.
Overcoming evil with good can soften hard hearts.
questions: Why did David’s men think this was God’s opportunity for him?
Why did David refuse to harm Saul?
Who do you find it hardest to show mercy to?
en.listen: Be still and bring God someone who has hurt you. Ask: ‘How do you want me to treat them?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you are the just Judge.
I give you my hurt about…, and I choose not to take revenge.
Help me to overcome evil with good.

mission.text: This week, do something kind for someone who has been unkind to you.

en.journal: Write about the difference between justice and revenge. Why is it better to leave justice to God?

af.title: Genade in die Grot
story: Koning Saul is deur jaloesie verteer en het Dawid soos ’n wilde dier gejag. Hy het drieduisend van sy beste soldate geneem om na Dawid te soek in die rotsagtige woestyn naby En-Gedi.

Langs die pad was skaapkrale en ’n groot grot. Saul het alleen in die grot ingegaan om hom te ontlas. Hy het geen idee gehad dat Dawid en sy manne diep binne-in daardie einste grot, in die donker, wegkruip nie.

Dawid se manne was opgewonde. ‘Dit is die dag waarvan die Here gepraat het toe Hy vir jou gesê het: “Ek sal jou vyand in jou hande gee sodat jy met hom kan doen wat jy wil.”’ Dit het na die perfekte geleentheid gelyk. Saul het tog probeer om Dawid dood te maak!

Dawid het geruisloos nader gekruip en ’n hoek van Saul se mantel afgesny. Maar toe het sy gewete hom gepla, selfs daaroor. Hy het vir sy manne gesê: ‘Die Here verhoed dat ek so iets aan my heer, die gesalfde van die Here, doen.’ Hy het geweier om hulle toe te laat om Saul aan te val.

Toe Saul die grot verlaat het, het Dawid uitgekom en agter hom aan geroep: ‘My heer die koning!’ Hy het laag gebuig en die hoek van die mantel opgehou. ‘Kyk, my vader, kyk na hierdie stuk van u mantel in my hand! Ek het die hoek van u mantel afgesny, maar u nie doodgemaak nie. Verstaan nou dat ek nie skuldig is aan onreg nie… Mag die Here tussen my en u oordeel… maar my hand sal u nie aanraak nie.’
Saul het hardop gehuil. ‘Jy is regverdiger as ek. Jy het my goed behandel, maar ek het jou sleg behandel.’

Dawid het elke rede vir wraak gehad. Maar hy het God vertrou om op sy tyd geregtigheid te bring. Paulus het later geskryf: ‘Moenie wraak neem nie, my liewe vriende, maar laat plek vir God se toorn… Moenie deur die kwaad oorwin word nie, maar oorwin die kwaad deur die goeie.’

verse.text: Moenie deur die kwaad oorwin word nie, maar oorwin die kwaad deur die goeie.

lessons: God help my om genade te kies in plaas van wraak.
Ek kan God vertrou om op sy tyd geregtigheid te bring.
Om die kwaad deur die goeie te oorwin, kan harde harte sag maak.
questions: Hoekom het Dawid se manne gedink dit is God se geleentheid vir hom?
Hoekom het Dawid geweier om Saul seer te maak?
Aan wie vind jy dit die moeilikste om genade te bewys?
af.listen: Wees stil en bring vir God iemand wat jou seergemaak het. Vra: ‘Hoe wil U hê moet ek hulle behandel?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U is die regverdige Regter.
Ek gee U my seer oor…, en ek kies om nie wraak te neem nie.
Help my om die kwaad deur die goeie te oorwin.

mission.text: Doen hierdie week iets gaafs vir iemand wat ongaaf met jou was.

af.journal: Skryf oor die verskil tussen geregtigheid en wraak. Hoekom is dit beter om geregtigheid aan God oor te laat?

en.title: Leaving Room for God
story: 1 Samuel 24 is a test of character disguised as an opportunity. David had been anointed king years earlier, yet he was living as a fugitive, hiding in caves while Saul hunted him. Then Saul walks into David’s cave, alone and vulnerable. David’s men interpret it spiritually: ‘This is the day the Lord spoke of.’ They even quote what sounds like a promise from God.

This is worth noticing. Not every ‘open door’ is from God, and not every interpretation that sounds spiritual is true. David’s men used God’s name to justify revenge. David discerned that a shortcut to the throne through violence would be disobedience, however convenient it looked.

Even cutting Saul’s robe troubled David’s conscience. Some suggest that cutting the robe’s hem symbolised taking Saul’s authority. David recognised that he was trying, even in a small way, to seize what God had promised to give in His own time. His sensitivity shows a heart that was soft towards God.

David’s speech outside the cave is remarkable. He calls Saul ‘my father’ and ‘my lord the king’, honouring him despite everything. He states the facts plainly; he doesn’t pretend Saul is innocent. But he places justice in God’s hands: ‘May the Lord judge between you and me. And may the Lord avenge the wrongs you have done to me, but my hand will not touch you.’

This isn’t passivity or pretending wrong is acceptable. It is active trust in God’s justice. Paul teaches the same: ‘Do not repay anyone evil for evil… Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath… “If your enemy is hungry, feed him.”’ Leaving vengeance to God frees us from bitterness and opens the door for God to work, even in our enemies.

Peter points to Jesus as the ultimate example: ‘When they hurled their insults at Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats. Instead, He entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.’
Mercy is not weakness. David had the power to strike and chose not to. That is strength under God’s control.

verse.text: Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath.

lessons: Not every ‘opportunity’ is from God; shortcuts to His promises can be disobedience.
Trusting God’s justice frees us from revenge and bitterness.
Jesus, who entrusted Himself to the just Judge, is our example.
questions: How did David’s men misuse God’s words? How can we avoid doing the same?
What is the difference between leaving justice to God and ignoring wrongdoing?
Is there someone you are holding a grudge against? What would ‘leaving room for God’ look like?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there anyone I want to get even with? How do you want me to respond?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you judge justly, and I trust you.
I place my desire for revenge against… in your hands.
Make me strong enough to show mercy, like David and like Jesus.

mission.text: This week, pray for and bless someone who has wronged you, following Romans 12:20.

en.journal: Write about a time you wanted revenge. What happened? How would leaving room for God have changed the situation?

af.title: Laat Plek vir God
story: 1 Samuel 24 is ’n toets van karakter wat soos ’n geleentheid lyk. Dawid is jare tevore as koning gesalf, tog het hy soos ’n vlugteling gelewe en in grotte weggekruip terwyl Saul hom jag. Dan stap Saul by Dawid se grot in, alleen en kwesbaar. Dawid se manne verklaar dit geestelik: ‘Dit is die dag waarvan die Here gepraat het.’ Hulle haal selfs aan wat soos ’n belofte van God klink.

Dit is die moeite werd om op te let. Nie elke ‘oop deur’ kom van God nie, en nie elke verklaring wat geestelik klink, is waar nie. Dawid se manne het God se Naam gebruik om wraak te regverdig. Dawid het onderskei dat ’n kortpad na die troon deur geweld ongehoorsaamheid sou wees, hoe gerieflik dit ook al gelyk het.

Selfs om Saul se mantel te sny, het Dawid se gewete gepla. Party stel voor dat om die soom van die mantel af te sny, gesimboliseer het dat Saul se gesag geneem word. Dawid het besef dat hy, selfs op ’n klein manier, probeer om te gryp wat God belowe het om op sy eie tyd te gee. Sy sensitiwiteit wys ’n hart wat sag was teenoor God.

Dawid se toespraak buite die grot is merkwaardig. Hy noem Saul ‘my vader’ en ‘my heer die koning’, en eer hom ten spyte van alles. Hy stel die feite duidelik; hy maak nie of Saul onskuldig is nie. Maar hy plaas geregtigheid in God se hande: ‘Mag die Here tussen my en u oordeel. En mag die Here die onreg wreek wat u my aangedoen het, maar my hand sal u nie aanraak nie.’

Dit is nie passiwiteit of om te maak of onreg aanvaarbaar is nie. Dit is aktiewe vertroue in God se geregtigheid. Paulus leer dieselfde: ‘Moenie iemand kwaad met kwaad vergeld nie… Moenie wraak neem nie, my liewe vriende, maar laat plek vir God se toorn… “As jou vyand honger het, gee hom kos.”’ Om wraak aan God oor te laat, maak ons vry van bitterheid en maak die deur oop vir God om te werk, selfs in ons vyande.

Petrus wys na Jesus as die grootste voorbeeld: ‘Toe hulle Hom beledig het, het Hy nie teruggeslaan nie; toe Hy gely het, het Hy nie gedreig nie. In plaas daarvan het Hy Homself toevertrou aan Hom wat regverdig oordeel.’
Genade is nie swakheid nie. Dawid het die mag gehad om toe te slaan en het gekies om dit nie te doen nie. Dit is krag onder God se beheer.

verse.text: Moenie wraak neem nie, my liewe vriende, maar laat plek vir God se toorn.

lessons: Nie elke ‘geleentheid’ kom van God nie; kortpaaie na sy beloftes kan ongehoorsaamheid wees.
Om God se geregtigheid te vertrou, maak ons vry van wraak en bitterheid.
Jesus, wat Homself aan die regverdige Regter toevertrou het, is ons voorbeeld.
questions: Hoe het Dawid se manne God se woorde misbruik? Hoe kan ons vermy om dieselfde te doen?
Wat is die verskil tussen om geregtigheid aan God oor te laat en om onreg te ignoreer?
Is daar iemand teen wie jy ’n wrok hou? Hoe sou dit lyk om ‘plek vir God te laat’?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is daar iemand wat ek wil terugkry? Hoe wil U hê moet ek reageer?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U oordeel regverdig, en ek vertrou U.
Ek plaas my begeerte na wraak teen… in u hande.
Maak my sterk genoeg om genade te bewys, soos Dawid en soos Jesus.

mission.text: Bid hierdie week vir iemand wat jou verontreg het en seën hulle, volgens Romeine 12:20.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy wraak wou neem. Wat het gebeur? Hoe sou dit die situasie verander het as jy plek vir God gelaat het?

en.title: David Chooses Kindness
story: King Saul was chasing David.
Saul went into a dark cave. David was hiding in the very same cave!
David’s friends said, ‘Get him now!’
But David said, ‘No. I won’t hurt him.’
God helps me to be kind, even when someone is unkind to me.

verse.text: Love your enemies.

en.action: Pretend to tiptoe quietly in a dark cave, then fold your arms and say: ‘I choose kindness!’
lessons: God helps me choose kindness, not getting even.
questions: Can you tiptoe very quietly?
prayer: Dear God,
help me to be kind, even when it’s hard. Amen.

af.title: Dawid Kies Goedheid
story: Koning Saul het agter Dawid aan gejaag.
Saul het in ’n donker grot ingegaan. Dawid het in presies dieselfde grot weggekruip!
Dawid se vriende het gesê: ‘Vang hom nou!’
Maar Dawid het gesê: ‘Nee. Ek sal hom nie seermaak nie.’
God help my om gaaf te wees, selfs as iemand ongaaf met my is.

verse.text: Julle moet julle vyande liefhê.

af.action: Maak of jy saggies in ’n donker grot op jou tone loop, vou dan jou arms en sê: ‘Ek kies goedheid!’
lessons: God help my om goedheid te kies, nie terugbetaal nie.
questions: Kan jy baie saggies op jou tone loop?
prayer: Liewe God,
help my om gaaf te wees, selfs as dit moeilik is. Amen.

en.title: In the Dark Cave
story: King Saul was still jealous of David, and he took three thousand soldiers to search for him in the desert. David and his men were hiding deep inside a big, dark cave.
Then guess who came into the very same cave to rest? King Saul! He didn’t know David was hiding in the shadows at the back.
David’s men whispered excitedly, ‘This is your chance! God has given your enemy into your hands. You can get rid of him now!’

David crept forward very quietly in the dark. But instead of hurting Saul, he just cut off a corner of Saul’s robe with his knife. Even that made David feel bad. ‘I must not hurt the king God has chosen,’ he told his men.

When Saul left the cave, David came out behind him and called, ‘My lord the king!’ Saul turned around. David bowed down and held up the piece of robe. ‘Look! I could have hurt you in the cave, but I didn’t. I won’t pay you back for being unkind to me. Let the Lord be the judge.’
Saul started to cry. ‘You are better than I am, David. You have been good to me, and I have been bad to you.’
When people are unkind to us, we might want to get them back. But God helps us choose mercy and kindness instead. God will look after what is fair.

verse.text: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.

lessons: God helps me choose mercy, not revenge.
I can trust God to be the judge.
Kindness can change someone’s heart.
questions: Why didn’t David hurt Saul when he had the chance?
What can you do when someone is unkind to you?
prayer: Dear God,
when people are unkind to me,
help me not to get them back,
but to be kind and trust you. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, if someone is unkind to you, choose to be kind back, and tell God about it.

af.title: In die Donker Grot
story: Koning Saul was steeds jaloers op Dawid, en hy het drieduisend soldate geneem om in die woestyn na hom te soek. Dawid en sy manne het diep binne-in ’n groot, donker grot weggekruip.
Raai wie het toe in presies dieselfde grot ingekom om te rus? Koning Saul! Hy het nie geweet Dawid kruip agter in die skaduwees weg nie.
Dawid se manne het opgewonde gefluister: ‘Dit is jou kans! God het jou vyand in jou hande gegee. Jy kan nou van hom ontslae raak!’

Dawid het baie saggies in die donker vorentoe gekruip. Maar in plaas daarvan om Saul seer te maak, het hy net ’n hoekie van Saul se mantel met sy mes afgesny. Selfs dit het Dawid sleg laat voel. ‘Ek mag nie die koning seermaak wat God gekies het nie,’ het hy vir sy manne gesê.

Toe Saul die grot verlaat, het Dawid agter hom uitgekom en geroep: ‘My heer die koning!’ Saul het omgedraai. Dawid het gebuig en die stukkie mantel opgehou. ‘Kyk! Ek kon jou in die grot seergemaak het, maar ek het nie. Ek sal jou nie terugbetaal omdat jy ongaaf met my was nie. Laat die Here die regter wees.’
Saul het begin huil. ‘Jy is beter as ek, Dawid. Jy was goed vir my, en ek was sleg vir jou.’
As mense ongaaf met ons is, wil ons hulle dalk terugkry. Maar God help ons om eerder genade en goedheid te kies. God sal sorg vir wat regverdig is.

verse.text: Julle moet julle vyande liefhê, doen goed aan die wat julle haat.

lessons: God help my om genade te kies, nie wraak nie.
Ek kan God vertrou om die regter te wees.
Goedheid kan iemand se hart verander.
questions: Hoekom het Dawid nie vir Saul seergemaak toe hy die kans gehad het nie?
Wat kan jy doen as iemand ongaaf met jou is?
prayer: Liewe God,
as mense ongaaf met my is,
help my om hulle nie terug te kry nie,
maar om gaaf te wees en U te vertrou. Amen.

mission.text: As iemand môre ongaaf met jou is, kies om terug gaaf te wees, en vertel God daarvan.

en.journal: Draw a dark cave with David holding up a piece of robe. Write: ‘I choose mercy.’
